package strategy

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	git "github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
)

func TestUpsertSubagentLink_AppendsThenMergesFirstWriteWins(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	var list []checkpoint.SubagentLink
	list = upsertSubagentLink(list, checkpoint.SubagentLink{ToolUseID: "t1", AgentID: "a1", SubagentType: "dev", Description: "build", FileCount: 3})
	list = upsertSubagentLink(list, checkpoint.SubagentLink{ToolUseID: "t2", AgentID: "a2", SubagentType: "reviewer"})
	require.Len(t, list, 2, "distinct keys append as separate entries (it is a list)")

	// Re-fire t1 with a DIFFERENT (higher) FileCount and empty fields. The first
	// record ran with the pre-task baseline and is authoritative: FileCount must
	// NOT change, and non-empty fields are preserved.
	list = upsertSubagentLink(list, checkpoint.SubagentLink{ToolUseID: "t1", FileCount: 99})
	require.Len(t, list, 2, "re-fire merges in place, never appends")
	require.Equal(t, "t1", list[0].ToolUseID, "ordering preserved")
	require.Equal(t, 3, list[0].FileCount, "first FileCount is authoritative — a re-fire cannot overwrite it")
	require.Equal(t, "dev", list[0].SubagentType, "non-empty field preserved")
	require.Equal(t, "build", list[0].Description, "non-empty field preserved")
	require.Equal(t, "a1", list[0].AgentID, "non-empty field preserved")

	// A re-fire fills a field the first record was missing.
	list = upsertSubagentLink(list, checkpoint.SubagentLink{ToolUseID: "t2", Description: "late description"})
	require.Equal(t, "late description", list[1].Description, "a gap in the first record is filled by a re-fire")
}

func TestUpsertSubagentLink_KeysByAgentIDWhenNoToolUseID(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	var list []checkpoint.SubagentLink
	// Two subagents lacking a ToolUseID but with DISTINCT AgentIDs must not
	// collapse onto an empty key.
	list = upsertSubagentLink(list, checkpoint.SubagentLink{AgentID: "a1", SubagentType: "x"})
	list = upsertSubagentLink(list, checkpoint.SubagentLink{AgentID: "a2", SubagentType: "y"})
	require.Len(t, list, 2, "distinct AgentIDs (no ToolUseID) do not collapse")

	// Same AgentID merges in place.
	list = upsertSubagentLink(list, checkpoint.SubagentLink{AgentID: "a1", Description: "fill"})
	require.Len(t, list, 2)
	require.Equal(t, "fill", list[0].Description)
}

func TestCountUniqueFiles_DedupsAcrossLists(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	require.Equal(t, 0, countUniqueFiles(), "no lists -> zero")
	require.Equal(t, 0, countUniqueFiles(nil, nil), "empty lists -> zero")
	require.Equal(t, 2, countUniqueFiles([]string{"a.go", "b.go"}))
	require.Equal(t, 3, countUniqueFiles([]string{"a.go", "b.go"}, []string{"b.go", "c.go"}), "dedup across lists")
	require.Equal(t, 1, countUniqueFiles([]string{"a.go"}, []string{"a.go"}, []string{"a.go"}), "same path across all lists counts once")
}

// TestRecordSubagentLink_AccumulatesAndMergesThroughState drives the real
// RecordSubagentLink -> MutateSessionState -> persisted state path: distinct
// subagents accumulate as a list, a no-file-change subagent is still recorded
// (the full-tree requirement), an ID-less subagent is skipped, and a re-fire
// upserts without overwriting the authoritative first record.
func TestRecordSubagentLink_AccumulatesAndMergesThroughState(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "2026-05-08-record-subagent-link"

	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "test.txt"), []byte("x"), 0o644))
	require.NoError(t, s.SaveStep(context.Background(), StepContext{
		SessionID: sessionID, ModifiedFiles: []string{"test.txt"},
		MetadataDir: metadataDir, MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
		CommitMessage: "c1", AuthorName: "T", AuthorEmail: "t@t.com",
	}))

	ctx := context.Background()
	require.NoError(t, RecordSubagentLink(ctx, sessionID, "t1", "a1", "dev", "build", []string{"x.go", "y.go"}, nil, nil))
	// A subagent that changed nothing must still be recorded (FileCount 0).
	require.NoError(t, RecordSubagentLink(ctx, sessionID, "t2", "a2", "reviewer", "review", nil, nil, nil))

	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, state.Subagents, 2, "two distinct subagents accumulate as a list")
	require.Equal(t, 2, state.Subagents[0].FileCount, "first subagent's file count persisted")
	require.Equal(t, "a2", state.Subagents[1].AgentID)
	require.Equal(t, 0, state.Subagents[1].FileCount, "a no-file-change subagent is still recorded")

	// An ID-less subagent (e.g. copilot) is skipped — no empty-keyed collapse.
	require.NoError(t, RecordSubagentLink(ctx, sessionID, "", "", "", "", nil, nil, nil))
	require.NoError(t, RecordSubagentLink(ctx, sessionID, "", "", "", "", nil, nil, nil))
	state, err = s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, state.Subagents, 2, "ID-less subagents are not recorded")

	// Re-fire t1 baseline-less: upsert (not append) and never overwrite the
	// authoritative first FileCount.
	require.NoError(t, RecordSubagentLink(ctx, sessionID, "t1", "a1", "", "", nil, nil, nil))
	state, err = s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, state.Subagents, 2, "re-fire upserts, does not append")
	require.Equal(t, 2, state.Subagents[0].FileCount, "re-fire does not change the authoritative FileCount")
	require.Equal(t, "dev", state.Subagents[0].SubagentType, "re-fire preserves SubagentType")
}

// TestCondenseSession_RoundTripsSubagents proves the parent->child subagent list
// seeded on session.State flows through condensation into the pushed per-session
// metadata.json — the payload the UI reads. Mirrors the InvestigateRunID
// round-trip test (the precedent this feature follows).
func TestCondenseSession_RoundTripsSubagents(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "2026-05-08-subagents-condensation"

	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))

	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"spawn a worker"}}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":"On it."}}
`

	t.Parallel()
	repo, store, cpID := setupRepoForUpdate(t)

// TestHandleTurnEnd_PublishesTrailingSubagents proves the finalize wiring
// (UpdateOptions.Subagents = state.Subagents in finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints): a
// subagent recorded AFTER the last condensation is published to the turn's
// already-written checkpoint at turn-end. Mirrors TestHandleTurnEnd_PartialFailure.
func TestHandleTurnEnd_PublishesTrailingSubagents(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "test-trailing-subagents"

	setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionID)

	state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	state.Phase = session.PhaseActive
	state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))

	// Commit -> a real v1 checkpoint is condensed while state.Subagents is empty.
	commitWithCheckpointTrailer(t, repo, dir, "a1b2c3d4e5f6")
	require.NoError(t, s.PostCommit(context.Background()))

	state, err = s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Contains(t, state.TurnCheckpointIDs, "a1b2c3d4e5f6", "PostCommit records the turn checkpoint")

	// A subagent completes AFTER the condensation (trailing). Only the turn-end
	// finalize can publish it onto the already-written checkpoint.
	state.Subagents = []checkpoint.SubagentLink{
		{ToolUseID: "trail-1", AgentID: "trail-a", SubagentType: "reader", FileCount: 0},
	}

	fullTranscript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"spawn a reader"}}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":"done"}}
`
	transcriptPath := filepath.Join(dir, ".entire", "metadata", sessionID, "full_transcript.jsonl")
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(transcriptPath), 0o755))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(transcriptPath, []byte(fullTranscript), 0o644))
	state.TranscriptPath = transcriptPath
	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))

	require.NoError(t, s.HandleTurnEnd(context.Background(), state))

	// The trailing subagent must now be present in the checkpoint's v1 metadata.json.
	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("a1b2c3d4e5f6")
	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName), true)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	f, err := tree.File(cpID.Path() + "/0/" + paths.MetadataFileName)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	content, err := f.Contents()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var meta checkpoint.Metadata
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(content), &meta))
	require.Len(t, meta.Subagents, 1, "turn-end finalize must publish the trailing subagent into the checkpoint metadata")
	require.Equal(t, "trail-1", meta.Subagents[0].ToolUseID)
	require.Equal(t, "reader", meta.Subagents[0].SubagentType)
}

  const match = value.trim().match(/^(\d+)\s*([mhdw])$/i)
  if (!match) return null

  const amount = Number(match[1])
  const unit = match[2].toLowerCase()
  const minutes =

        ? amount * 60
        : unit === "d"

          : amount * 60 * 24 * 7

**Entire Dispatch** = an auto-generated markdown "what shipped lately" report across your repos, written by an AI dispatch runner. It's the "Dispatches" item in the app sidebar (backed by `api/src/routes/dispatches.ts` + `lib/dispatch.ts`, gated behind the `dispatch-v2` flag).

How it works:
- You pick a **scope**: which repos, which branches, a **timeframe** (`since`/window like `7d`), and a **voice** (a tone/style preference).
- It pulls your recent Entire activity over that window (commits/checkpoints/sessions — the structured Summary/Investigation/Decision/Highlights data) and an LLM writes a concise digest: title, intro, a `##` section per repo, themed `###` subheadings with bullets, and a sign-off.
- The **voice** restyles tone/phrasing throughout but never the facts (the system prompt hard-forbids inventing work, and treats repo/branch/commit text as untrusted to resist prompt injection).
- It executes as a **runner run** (`runner_id: "dispatch"`), is rate-limited, and you can save a reusable **dispatch setup**.

Plain version: an automated, shareable standup/changelog/weekly-update of agent + human work, in whatever voice you choose.

One naming caveat: the same word is reused for the **marketing blog** — the "Entire Dispatch 0x0001/0x0002…" weekly posts on the website are hand-written company updates, a different thing from the in-app feature.

# Audit loop: fix until genuinely clean

Loop review then fix then re-verify until the code is clean from BOTH a normal reviewer's view and an adversarial bug-hunter's view. Do not stop at the first clean read. Stop only after two consecutive full passes find nothing new and build/lint/tests are green.

## Scope
Default to the current branch's diff vs the base branch (main). If the user names a file, package, or PR, scope to that. State what you are auditing before you start.

## The loop

Run these every iteration:

### Pass A: normal review lens
Read it like a careful reviewer.
- Correctness: does it do what it claims? Off-by-one, inverted conditions, missing cases, wrong defaults.
- Error handling: unchecked errors, swallowed failures, missing early returns, ignored return values.
- Maintainability: dead code, duplication, unclear naming, leftover debug, TODOs left in.
- Consistency: matches the surrounding code's patterns and the repo's conventions.

### Pass B: bugbot / adversarial lens
Now try to break it.
- Edge cases: empty, nil, zero, negative, very large, unicode, whitespace, duplicate, out-of-order.
- Concurrency: races, unsynchronized shared state, goroutine/promise leaks, deadlock.
- Resources: unclosed files/conns/handles, unbounded growth, missing timeouts/contexts.
- Security: injection, path traversal, secrets in code or logs, auth/authz gaps, unsafe deserialization, SSRF.
- Bad assumptions: stale cache, partial failure, reordering, retries that double-apply.
- For each suspected bug, construct the concrete failing input before claiming it.

### Fix
Fix everything found. Keep diffs minimal and targeted. Add or adjust a test for each real bug so it cannot regress.

### Verify the committed state
Run the repo's build + lint + full test suite. Confirm green on the actually-committed/staged tree, not an unsaved buffer. A "reset --soft then commit" or a stash can silently leave the fix out of the commit, so diff `git show HEAD` if in doubt.

### Re-loop
Go back to Pass A on the fixed code. A fix can introduce a new bug. Keep going.

## Stop condition
Exit only when a full Pass A + Pass B finds nothing new TWICE in a row AND build/lint/tests pass. Then report: what was found, what was fixed, and the verified final state.

## Rules
- Never declare clean on a single pass. The subtle bugs surface after the obvious ones are gone.
- Default to skepticism. If you cannot fix something safely because it needs a design decision or a benchmark you cannot run, stop and surface it instead of guessing.
- Report honestly: separate "fixed and verified" from "found but could not verify."
- For a large surface, fan out: review independent areas in parallel, then verify each finding adversarially before trusting it.

## Problem

`entire review` (the command, not agent-session reviews) cancels work on timeouts that are too tight, marking agents **failed**. Reported in entire-cli:

> 2 agent(s) done — 0 succeeded, 2 failed — `review agent claude-code timed out after 10m0s`

A review has **two independent** time bounds, and both are too low for real runs:

1. **Per-reviewer** (`defaultReviewerTimeout`, 10m) — each reviewer subprocess (read diff, run skills, write report).
2. **Judge consolidation** (`defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout`, 2m) — the single text-generation call where the judge reads *every* reviewer report and writes the combined verdict. This is **separate** from `--timeout` and was the easy-to-miss one.

## Change

- `defaultReviewerTimeout` **10m → 20m** (`review/run.go`). One constant drives the per-reviewer bound (single + multi paths) and the `--timeout` flag default; `--timeout DUR` still overrides, `0` still disables.
- `defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout` **2m → 5m** (`review/synthesis_sink.go`) — gives the judge room to consolidate. Added a regression test that an unset `ProviderTimeout` still applies a deadline (the judge must stay bounded, never unbounded).

These are the only two run-bounding timeouts in the review path — verified by sweeping every `time.Minute`/`WithTimeout` in `cmd/entire/cli/review` and confirming the reviewer adapters + `GenerateText` impose no inner cap. (The other timeouts there — a detached 30s finalize/manifest write, timestamp-skew windows, a 2s TUI grace — don't clip a run.)

## Notes

- Values are deliberate, measured bumps. Easy to dial to 15m/30m or 3m/5m if the team prefers.
- `--timeout` still governs only the **reviewers**, not the judge (the judge keeps its own default). Wiring `--timeout` to also bound the judge would change the flag's meaning, so I left it out — happy to add it if desired.

Honest answer to "did you check it all?": **No — and pushing back was right.** I'd missed something real.

## What I'd missed

A review has **two independent** timeouts; I'd only fixed one:

1. **Per-reviewer** — `defaultReviewerTimeout` 10m → 20m (the `claude-code timed out after 10m0s` peyton reported). ✓ already done.
2. **Judge consolidation** — `defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout` = **2m**, a *separate* bound on the single LLM call where the judge reads every reviewer report and writes the verdict. It's **not** governed by `--timeout` and is plausibly the bigger culprit for peyton's "review command **in general** needs help." I'd wrongly claimed "one constant governs the judge too" — the judge is a `SynthesisSink`, not a reviewer. **Now bumped 2m → 5m**, with a regression test that it stays bounded.

## How peyton's message maps out (the part I verified properly this time)

- **"works better in agent sessions vs actual command"** — the failing `N agent(s) done … timed out` output comes from `dump.go`/`tui_sink.go` = the **local command** path (reviewers run as subprocesses under the timeout); agent-session/spawn reviews don't apply that subprocess cap. - **"review command in general"** — that's the judge 2m, now addressed.
- **peyton's PRs** (#1241/#1352/#1370/#1207 + dipree's #1313) — none touches timeouts; no overlap.
- **#1312 (Daniel)** — already in main; my change sits correctly on the multi-agent path it introduced.

After fixing, a second exhaustive pass over **every** `time.Minute`/`WithTimeout` in `cmd/entire/cli/review` (plus the reviewer adapters and `GenerateText`) found no other run-bounding cap — two clean passes. ## Problem

`entire review` (the command, not agent-session reviews) cancels work on timeouts that are too tight, marking agents **failed**. Reported in entire-cli:

> 2 agent(s) done — 0 succeeded, 2 failed — `review agent claude-code timed out after 10m0s`

A review has **two independent** time bounds, both too low for real runs — and the second was **not controllable** at all:

1. **Per-reviewer** (`defaultReviewerTimeout`, 10m) — each reviewer subprocess (read diff, run skills, write report). Governed by `--timeout`.
2. **Judge consolidation** (`defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout`, 2m) — the single text-generation call where the judge reads *every* reviewer report and writes the combined verdict. It runs as a `SynthesisSink`, **separate** from reviewers, and `--timeout` did **not** reach it — so a slow judge was cancelled regardless of the flag.

## Change

- **Reviewers:** `defaultReviewerTimeout` **10m → 20m** (`review/run.go`). One constant drives the per-reviewer bound (single + multi paths) and the `--timeout` flag default.
- **Judge:** `--timeout` now governs the judge too. The resolved timeout is threaded into `SynthesisSink.ProviderTimeout`, and `providerContext` gets the **same three-state convention** as the reviewer timeout — *positive*: use it; *zero (unset)*: default; *negative*: disabled. The unset default is raised **2m → 5m** (library/non-CLI fallback).

Net behavior — one coherent knob for the whole command:

| `--timeout` | reviewers | judge |
|---|---|---|
| *(default)* | 20m | 20m (5m if constructed without the CLI) |
| `30m` | 30m | 30m |
| `0` | disabled | disabled |

These are the only two run-bounding timeouts in the review path — verified by sweeping every `time.Minute`/`WithTimeout` in `cmd/entire/cli/review` and confirming the reviewer adapters + `GenerateText` impose no inner cap. (Other timeouts there — a detached 30s finalize/manifest write, timestamp-skew windows, a 2s TUI grace — don't clip a run.) `SynthesisSink` is constructed only by the review command, so the blast radius is exactly this command.

## Tests

- `synthesis_sink_test.go`: judge call is bounded by default, **honors an explicit timeout**, and is **unbounded when disabled** (negative).
- `cmd_test.go`: `composeMultiAgentSinks` wires `--timeout` into the judge's `ProviderTimeout` in **both** TTY and non-TTY paths.

# Audit loop: fix until genuinely clean

Loop review then fix then re-verify until the code is clean from BOTH a normal reviewer's view and an adversarial bug-hunter's view. Do not stop at the first clean read. Stop only after two consecutive full passes find nothing new and build/lint/tests are green.

## Scope
Default to the current branch's diff vs the base branch (main). If the user names a file, package, or PR, scope to that. State what you are auditing before you start.

## The loop

Run these every iteration:

### Pass A: normal review lens
Read it like a careful reviewer.
- Correctness: does it do what it claims? Off-by-one, inverted conditions, missing cases, wrong defaults.
- Error handling: unchecked errors, swallowed failures, missing early returns, ignored return values.
- Maintainability: dead code, duplication, unclear naming, leftover debug, TODOs left in.
- Consistency: matches the surrounding code's patterns and the repo's conventions.

### Pass B: bugbot / adversarial lens
Now try to break it.
- Edge cases: empty, nil, zero, negative, very large, unicode, whitespace, duplicate, out-of-order.
- Concurrency: races, unsynchronized shared state, goroutine/promise leaks, deadlock.
- Resources: unclosed files/conns/handles, unbounded growth, missing timeouts/contexts.
- Security: injection, path traversal, secrets in code or logs, auth/authz gaps, unsafe deserialization, SSRF.
- Bad assumptions: stale cache, partial failure, reordering, retries that double-apply.
- For each suspected bug, construct the concrete failing input before claiming it.

### Fix
Fix everything found. Keep diffs minimal and targeted. Add or adjust a test for each real bug so it cannot regress.

### Verify the committed state
Run the repo's build + lint + full test suite. Confirm green on the actually-committed/staged tree, not an unsaved buffer. A "reset --soft then commit" or a stash can silently leave the fix out of the commit, so diff `git show HEAD` if in doubt.

### Re-loop
Go back to Pass A on the fixed code. A fix can introduce a new bug. Keep going.

## Stop condition
Exit only when a full Pass A + Pass B finds nothing new TWICE in a row AND build/lint/tests pass. Then report: what was found, what was fixed, and the verified final state.

## Rules
- Never declare clean on a single pass. The subtle bugs surface after the obvious ones are gone.
- Default to skepticism. If you cannot fix something safely because it needs a design decision or a benchmark you cannot run, stop and surface it instead of guessing.
- Report honestly: separate "fixed and verified" from "found but could not verify."
- For a large surface, fan out: review independent areas in parallel, then verify each finding adversarially before trusting it.

The judge exit-code finding (396) wasn't safe to ignore: **my own change amplified it** (routing the judge through `--timeout` makes judge timeouts easy to hit), and exit-0-on-failed-verdict means a CI gate would pass green with no verdict. So I fixed it instead of dismissing.

Implemented via a new `SynthesisSink.OnError` that fires *only* on an attempted-but-failed synthesis — not on a legitimate skip (cancelled run / <2 reviewers) or Ctrl+C. Help text updated to "judge timeout or error fails the review." Tests cover called-on-failure / not-on-success / not-when-skipped.

content.text:
Got the full chain from the code. Short answer: **yes — it's an LLM, but more specifically it's a full coding agent (e.g. Claude Code) running server-side in a sandbox, triggered by your push** — not a single backend prompt.

## How a trail's findings get made

```
git push
  → webhook → api/src/lib/agents/push-router.ts  (launchPushRunners)
      picks runner configs where scope=="trail", triggerTypes∋"push", trailsReviewEnabled
  → trail-runner-launcher.ts (startTrailConfiguredRun)
      • prompt-builder.ts builds the review prompt
      • previous-findings.ts feeds prior findings in (so it dedupes / stays incremental)
      • provisions a SANDBOX run (e2b / Daytona) with the repo + agent credentials
  → a configured agent (Claude Code, etc.) reviews the diff in the sandbox
      LLM calls go through api/src/lib/anthropic-client.ts (Anthropic SDK)
  → review-publication.ts parses its structured output
  → db.codeReview.createReviewCommentsAtomic(...)  → stored as review comments
      = the findings you see via `entire trail finding list` (with file:line + severity)
```

So when findings appeared on #711 without me running anything — that was the **push-triggered server-side runner** reviewing the branch. The earlier findings I resolved were that agent's output.

## The important distinctions

- **Trail findings (server-side)** — a real agent in a cloud sandbox, on push. This is the one that "uses the backend LLM."
- **`entire review` (local CLI)** — the *same idea* run on your machine (reviewer agents + a judge), which can *post* its verdict/findings up to the trail via the API (`maybePostReviewToTrail`). Same finding store, different execution location.
- **PR "checks"** (the green/red ✓ on GitHub: lint, test-core, test-integration…) — those are **GitHub Actions CI**, totally separate from trail findings. "Checks" ≠ "findings" here.
- **Checkpoint analysis** (summaries, attribution) — a lighter pipeline (`analysis-queue.ts`, `checkpoint-analysis-pipeline.ts`) that calls the Anthropic API more directly, not a full agent.

So it's not one backend LLM call — it's an orchestration: push → launch agent in sandbox → agent uses the Anthropic API → its findings are persisted to the trail. There's even rate-limiting infra around it (`anthropic-rate-limiter-do.ts`, a Durable Object) because these are real, repeated model calls.

Want me to go deeper on any piece — e.g. how findings are deduped against previous runs, or the exact runner output format that becomes a finding?

### **"Meaning Tied to Git" Capability: What EXISTS Today**

**Session + Checkpoint Model (CLI):**
- ✅ **Transcripts** pinned to commits: `entire/checkpoints/v1` stores full agent session (prompts, responses, tool calls, token usage) with sharded metadata
- ✅ **Bidirectional links**: User commits carry `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer; checkpoint metadata tree is at `.../ab/c123def456/`
- ✅ **File attribution**: Each checkpoint records `files_touched`, linking code changes to prompts
- ✅ **Rewind/resume**: Agents can resume exactly where they left off by reading transcripts; users can restore code from any checkpoint
- ✅ **Concurrent sessions**: Multiple agent sessions can interleave on same base commit; each tagged with session ID
- ✅ **Compact transcripts**: Best-effort slicing of full transcript to checkpoint-scoped portion for efficient reads
- ⚠️ **Search**: Skills can search by topic/branch/author/time, but this uses API queries on the entire.io control plane, not VCS-native indexing

**Semantic Capture (entire-sem, emerging):**
- ✅ **Entity extraction**: Tree-sitter parses code to extract symbols, functions, types, relations
- ✅ **Multi-language**: Bash, C, C++, C#, CUE, Elixir, Go, Groovy, HCL, Java, JS/TS, Kotlin, Lua, OCaml, PHP, Protobuf, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, SQL, Swift, YAML
- ✅ **Checkpoint pinning**: Can answer "which entities did this checkpoint touch?"
- ⚠️ **Relation graph**: Builds edges/symbols, but integration into checkpoint metadata is **still emerging**—not yet fully codified in the checkpoint schema
- ❌ **Semantic search**: Cannot yet query "show all checkpoints that touched the auth subsystem" or "which prompts led to this entity changing"

**Agent Context Sharing (skills):**
- ✅ **Handoff**: Agents can attach/adopt sessions across repos and worktrees
- ✅ **Search/Explain**: Skills teach agents to query prior work by topic, file, or line number
- ✅ **Intent capture**: Summaries (best-effort) from transcripts record intent, learnings, friction points
- ⚠️ **Cross-agent memory**: Skills work within a single repo/org; cross-team/cross-org agent collaboration requires control-plane API (not pure VCS-native)

---

### **Biggest GAPS Relative to the Vision**

1. **No semantic schema in checkpoint metadata** — Entire-sem parses entities but doesn't embed them into `entire/checkpoints/v1` structure yet. Checkpoints record file paths and commit messages; they don't record "this checkpoint introduced the `auth.UserValidator` type" or "this prompt led to changes in 3 related entities." The semantic layer is a *plugin*, not integrated storage.

2. **No persistent semantic index tied to git history** — You can ask entire-sem "what entities are in this repo?" but not "which checkpoints/sessions touched this entity across time?" Semantic queries are ephemeral (tree-sitter re-parses on demand), not indexed alongside version history.

3. **No shared memory across org/team boundaries** — Checkpoints live on `entire/checkpoints/v1` per repo. Multi-team agents cannot natively query "who on team-B worked on similar code?" without cross-repo control-plane API calls. The VCS-native transport (git branches) stops at repo boundaries.

4. **No collaborative agent-to-agent handoff protocol in VCS** — Skills enable handoff, but it requires control-plane API awareness. A fleet of agents working in parallel can't use git-native primitives to coordinate work or avoid stepping on each other—they need explicit API calls to check session state.

5. **Transparency log not tied to checkpoint lineage** — `tlog-viewer` shows ref changes in real-time (push author, timestamp, change type) but doesn't link them to the semantic intent or session that caused them. You see "refs/entire/checkpoints/v1 moved" but not "this move happened because agent X completed session Y with intent Z."

6. **Async transcript compaction, not semantic compaction** — Checkpoints store raw transcripts + compact (substring slice). There's no semantic summary format like "this session introduced 4 new types, modified 2 functions, deleted 1 permission check, with these dependencies and risks." Summaries are LLM-generated prose, not structured semantic deltas.

7. **No collision/conflict detection at semantic level** — If two agents modify the same semantic entity in parallel, the system warns about concurrent sessions but doesn't understand the semantic overlap. A human has to read both transcripts to understand if they conflict.

---

### **What This Cluster DOES Achieve (The Working Piece)**

The **VCS-Tied Capture Core** is **80% there for agent workflow tracking**:

- ✅ Every agent decision is captured (prompts + responses + files touched + token counts)
- ✅ Linked to commits via git-native metadata (trailers + checkpoint IDs)
- ✅ Stored on a persistent, replicatable branch (`entire/checkpoints/v1`)
- ✅ Searchable and rewindable by session/checkpoint ID
- ✅ Queryable by agents via skills + control-plane API
- ✅ Supports multi-agent workflows (concurrent sessions, handoff, session attach/adopt)

The missing **20% is semantic understanding**:
- Agent work is *recorded* but not *understood* at the code-structure level
- You can replay "what changed" but not "why these entities changed together" or "what depends on this change"
- Concurrent sessions don't automatically detect semantic conflicts
- Cross-repo agent collaboration requires explicit API mediation, not git-native discovery

---

Copyright update to "Entire Inc." suggests this is now core IP, not experimental.

Shows that *agents are being ranked by provenance*, not just "we recorded the session." This is the start of agent-to-agent discovery.

3. **Session adoption (`entire session adopt` 2026+)**: Agents can now *inherit* prior work across repos/worktrees without losing lineage. Moves from "rewind to a checkpoint" to "resume another agent's session as a continuation." Semantic precursor.

4. **transparency-log (`tlog-viewer`, active 2026-05+)**: Real-time visibility into *why* refs moved (push author, event metadata). Not yet linked to checkpoint intent, but the plumbing is ready.

---

### **Concrete Mapping to North-Star Vision**

> *"We will unlock agent-to-agent collaboration with a semantic reasoning layer directly tied to version control history, giving every agent persistent, shared, and pluggable memory."*

**Today:**
- ✅ **Persistent**: Session transcripts are permanently stored on git branches
- ✅ **Shared**: Multiple agents can read the same checkpoint, inherit sessions, share context via skills
- ✅ **Pluggable**: Skills are agent-invokable workflows; entire-sem is a pluggable CLI command
- ❌ **Semantic reasoning layer**: Entire-sem exists but is not yet woven into checkpoint storage or collision detection
- ❌ **Directly tied to VCS**: Semantic queries require control-plane API; git-native discovery stops at repo boundaries

**The roadmap forward** (inferred from commit activity):
1. Embed semantic entities into checkpoint metadata (entire-sem → checkpoint schema)
2. Index semantic deltas on `entire/checkpoints/v1` (who touched which types/functions/classes)
3. Add conflict detection at semantic level (two agents modifying the same entity triggers early warning)
4. Build cross-repo agent discovery on top of semantic index ("team-A's auth work" → find similar sessions in team-B)
5. Extend transparency log to show semantic causality (ref moved because session introduced type X)

---

### **In One Paragraph**

The Entire CLI + EntireDB system has built the **VCS-tied capture and storage foundation** needed for agent collaboration: every session is transcribed, checksummed, sharded, and bidirectionally linked to commits via git-native metadata on a replicated branch. Multiple agents can interleave work, handoff sessions, and query prior intent through skills. **Semantic capture is emerging** (entire-sem 2026-06+) but not yet integrated into checkpoint storage—it's a plugin, not the core. The **biggest gap is collision detection and cross-repo discovery at the semantic level**: two agents can't yet ask "are we touching the same types?" without explicit API calls. The work is git-native up to repo boundaries, then requires control-plane mediation. **The roadmap is clear**: wire entire-sem into checkpoints, build semantic indexing, and enable VCS-native agent-to-agent reasoning across repos.</result>

### WHAT PARALLEL/MULTI-AGENT CAPABILITY EXISTS TODAY

#### 1. **Session Isolation & Worktree Shadowing** (CLI)
- **Mechanism**: Each worktree gets a unique shadow branch `entire/<base-commit[:7]>-<worktree-hash[:6]>`.
- **Isolation guarantee**: Sessions on the same base commit but different worktrees never collide—each worktree's session state is in `.git/entire-sessions/` (shared across worktrees, keyed by worktree ID).
- **Multi-session on same branch**: The CLI supports **multiple concurrent sessions** on the same base commit (different worktrees); `post-rewrite` hook keeps session linkage aligned after rebase.
- **Collision detection**: Fork-PR branch-name collisions are skipped via GitHub (`trail-gh-pr-id-link-on-pr-open.test.ts`).

#### 2. **Trails as Work Unit Containers** (Web)
- **Trail**: A unit of work (usually a PR), with durable code snapshots (`code_version`: immutable base/head SHAs), reviews (one review per actor/run), and a transactional event log.
- **Trail-level events**: SSE stream of review/finding/runner/monitor events, resumable from cursor.
- **Code review append-only**: Comments carry `(location, status, stale)` independently—review state evolves after code changes.
- **Multiple reviews per trail**: Different actors can review the same trail at the same (or different) code versions.
- **No trail grouping**: No concept of a parent/child trail hierarchy or multi-trail workflow ordering.

#### 3. **Dispatches for Multi-Repo Analysis** (Web)
- **Dispatch**: A voice-prompted, multi-repo code analysis that runs voice analysis + dispatch runners in parallel, then persists results.
- **Setup + recent/history**: Setups are reusable configs (repos, time window, branches). Recent dispatches are cached.
- **Per-repo sections**: Generated markdown groups results by repo.
- **Serial runner execution**: Runners are enqueued sequentially (`runDispatchWithRunnerPersistence`), not in parallel.

#### 4. **Agent-Planner for Cross-Directory Coordination** (Standalone)
- **Plans + tasks**: Each plan is a named goal with a task DAG. Tasks can depend on others; the server computes `ready`/`waiting` status per task.
- **Sub-plans**: Tasks can be promoted to sub-plans; parent tracks child status + rollup.
- **Handovers**: A brief from one session for the next; tracked as consumed.
- **Live session presence**: Over SSE, shows which session is currently working on a plan.
- **Directory binding**: Plans bind to directories (longest-prefix match); multiple agents working in that directory see the same plan.
- **MCP surface**: 33 tools expose `get_active_plan_for_cwd`, `add_task`, `update_task`, `set_current_task`, `submit_debrief`, etc.
- **Multi-plan on directory**: If a directory has multiple active plans, a chooser asks which to work on before auto-loading context.

#### 5. **Runners + Sandbox Isolation** (Web + Plugins)
- **Runner concept**: A launcher config (agent, args, scope) that dispatches to a sandbox (E2B, Daytona).
- **Sandbox provider abstraction**: `entire-sandbox` plugin supports Tart, QEMU, Docker, Dev Containers.
- **Per-run prompt execution**: Prompts are serialized per run (`hasActivePrompt` blocks second concurrent prompt).
- **Warm snapshots**: Reusable base snapshots per repo/ref/provider.

#### 6. **Checkpoint Transcript Normalization** (CLI)
- **Subagent tracking**: Parsers identify `subagent`, `dynamic_task`, and `task` events (e.g., Goose parser). Sessions can contain multiple agents' work.
- **Multi-session metadata**: Consolidated on v1 branch per checkpoint; `sessions[]` array with per-session agent, token usage, etc.
- **Transcript path resolution**: Dynamic (repo location + checkpoint ID), not hardcoded, so rewind works after repo moves.

### BIGGEST GAPS: "FLEETS BUILDING IN PARALLEL WITHOUT COLLISION/OVERWRITE/LOSING UNDERSTANDING"

#### 1. **No Agent-to-Agent Message Passing or RPC**
- **Today**: Agents work in isolation; coordination happens via **human-readable context** (handovers, PRs, trails).
- **Missing**: 
  - No inter-sandbox IPC (e.g., agent A finished parsing, publish event for agent B to consume).
  - No structured agent-to-agent request/response (e.g., "agent B, refactor this module while I handle migrations").
  - No discovery protocol (e.g., "which agents are available? what do they specialize in?").

#### 2. **No Explicit Multi-Agent Scheduler**
- **Today**: `agent-planner` computes task readiness (DAG) but doesn't auto-dispatch agents to tasks.
- **Missing**:
  - No scheduler that says "Task A is ready → dispatch Agent-1 with context + handover."
  - No load balancing across parallel agent instances.
  - No preemption/handoff when an agent gets stuck.

#### 3. **No Transactional Multi-Trail Workflows**
- **Today**: Trails are isolated work units; dispatches span repos but run serially.
- **Missing**:
  - No concept of a "multi-trail epic" or "campaign" that ensures all trails stay in sync.
  - No atomic multi-trail commit (e.g., "merge all three trails together" fails transactionally if one PR has conflicts).
  - No trail grouping/ordering constraints.

#### 4. **Collision Avoidance Incomplete for Multi-Agent Scenarios**
- **Today**: 
  - CLI shadow branches are worktree-specific (good for local parallel sessions).
  - Dispatches have repo + branch scoping (good for preventing accidental repo overwrites).
- **Missing**:
  - No global lock/lease system for preventing two agents from writing the same file.
  - No merge-conflict early detection (e.g., agent A and agent B both modify `src/auth.ts`; surface conflict before commit).
  - No "file ownership" metadata (e.g., "agent planner owns migrations; don't let other agents touch migrations/").

#### 5. **Handovers Are Append-Only Human-Readable Text, Not Structured Data**
- **Today**: `agent-planner` has `create_handover` (text), `submit_debrief` (artifact/gate), but both are narrative.
- **Missing**:
  - No structured handover format (e.g., "context=ContextDelta{modified_files: […], tokens_used: …}, task_state=TaskState{…}").
  - No schema validation or evolution (e.g., "v1 handover format → v2 format migration").
  - No automatic context hydration from handover (agent must manually parse and re-import).

#### 6. **No Central Agent Registry or Capability Discovery**
- **Today**: 
  - `external-agents` repo shows 3 implementations (kiro, amp, qwen).
  - `entire agent list` shows enabled agents per repo.
- **Missing**:
  - No global registry of agent capabilities (e.g., "kiro specializes in dependency upgrades").
  - No automatic capability matching (e.g., "I need a refactoring agent; call agent B").
  - No capability version negotiation (e.g., "agent A speaks protocol v2; agent B speaks v1; fallback to common subset").

#### 7. **Runners Don't Share State or Communicate During Execution**
- **Today**: Runners are isolated sandbox VMs/containers; each gets its own prompt.
- **Missing**:
  - No inter-runner file sync (e.g., "agent A built a lib in `/tmp/lib`; agent B needs to import it").
  - No progress polling (human must check trails/events manually).
  - No runner-to-runner triggering (e.g., "when agent A finishes, automatically start agent B").

#### 8. **"Understanding" (Provenance) Not Captured Across Multi-Agent Workflows**
- **Today**: 
  - Each checkpoint links to a session (agent, prompts, tool calls).
  - Trails capture code versions + reviews.
  - No cross-agent dependency tracking.
- **Missing**:
  - No "provenance graph" showing how agent A's output fed into agent B's input.
  - No "decision cascade" (e.g., "decision D1 → agent A's task T1 → PR P1 → review R1 → decision D2 → agent B starts").
  - No blame/audit trail for "agent B did X because agent A recommended Y" (structured, not in transcript).

# Roadmap: The Semantic Reasoning Layer — from capture to shared agent memory

## Context

**North-star:** *"Version control preserves change, not meaning. Without shared context, agents can't collaborate. We will unlock agent-to-agent collaboration with a semantic reasoning layer directly tied to version-control history, giving every agent persistent, shared, and pluggable memory — so groups of humans and fleets of agents can reason, coordinate, and build in parallel without overwriting, colliding, or losing understanding."*

This roadmap comes from analyzing **all active repos across `entireio` + `entirehq`** (three parallel Explore passes: the VCS-tied storage core, the semantic-reasoning/memory layer, and the agent-to-agent execution/collaboration layer). It answers: *how close are we, are we drifting, and what's the path.*

**Honest verdict up front:** The direction is **right, not different** — but current effort is going into **substrate + breadth** (more capture, more execution surfaces, several parallel search/knowledge experiments), while the **actual differentiator in the vision — the semantic reasoning layer and unified shared memory — is the least converged part.** The crown jewel (`entire-sem`, a benchmarked semantic extractor) is proven but **not yet wired into the memory/collaboration loop.** The near-term win is **convergence and closing the loop**, not building more substrate.

### How close are we (scorecard)

| Vision sub-claim | Maturity | Reality |
|---|---|---|
| Capture tied to VCS history | **~80%** | `cli` checkpoints/trails/shadow branches + `entiredb` storage are production. But capture records *files + transcripts*, not *meaning*. |
| Semantic reasoning layer | **~40%** | `entire-sem` extraction is converged & benchmarked (`brain-bench` F1 1.0 symbols / 0.949 call-graph) — but it's a **plugin**, not woven into the store or the memory API. |
| Persistent, shared, pluggable memory | **~40%** | Pieces exist (`mcp`, `librarian`, `entire-search`, `skills`) but memory is **fragmented** (2 knowledge systems, 3 search engines) and reasoning is **ephemeral** (no persistent reasoning record). |
| Fleets coordinating without collision | **~10%** | Strong isolation primitives (worktree shadow branches, sandboxes) + `agent-planner` task DAG, but **no scheduler, no agent-to-agent messaging, no semantic collision detection, no structured handover, no provenance graph.** |

**Net: humans+agents building together ≈ 80–90% there; fleets of agents reasoning over shared semantic memory ≈ 20–30% there.**

---

## Where we are today (the map)

**Substrate — largely built (reuse, don't rebuild):**
- Capture: `entireio/cli` (checkpoints on `entire/checkpoints/v1`, shadow branches, trails, subagent tracking, review/judge). Production.
- Storage/federation: `entirehq/entiredb` (content-addressed, transparency log), `mirror-pipeline`, `git-sync`, `go-git-api`, `go-gitea`. Active.
- Semantic extraction: `entireio/entire-sem` (tree-sitter entities + call graph, 15–20 langs) validated by `entirehq/brain-bench`. **Converged, now core IP.**
- Retrieval: `entirehq/peregrine` (fast Rust engine), `entireio/pgr` (agent-ranked), `entireio/symbolic-search-poc`/`symq` (SCIP two-tier, POC). **Fragmented — 3 paths, no winner.**
- Knowledge/memory: `entirehq/librarian` (Slack/Linear/GitHub → pgvector/Cohere), `entirehq/entire-search` + `entirehq/search` (checkpoints/commits → Turbopuffer/LanceDB, multi-region). **Two parallel systems.**
- Pluggable surface: `entirehq/mcp` (control-plane + product tools over MCP), `entireio/skills`, `entireio/external-agents` (Claude/Codex/Droid/Gemini/Cursor/Copilot/kiro/amp/qwen).
- Execution: `entirehq/ferrata` + `entireio/entire-sandbox` + `entirehq/runner-proxy` (sandboxed agents), `entirehq/anodyne` + `entireio/entire-worktree` (parallel worktree isolation).
- Coordination seed: `entirehq/agent-planner` (task DAG, readiness, handovers, live session presence — the closest thing to multi-agent coordination).
- Reasoning apps: `entirehq/dispatch-live` (scheduled momentum synthesis via Librarian), `entirehq/marvin` (Slack), `entireio/entire-judge` (reads brains + sem snapshots).

**The missing middle & top:**
1. **Meaning isn't in the store.** `entire-sem` output is not embedded in checkpoints/`entiredb`; no persistent entity→checkpoint index across time; no semantic causality on the transparency log.
2. **Memory is fragmented.** `librarian` (human) vs `entire-search` (code) don't share a schema or query surface; 3 code-search engines; no single "pluggable shared memory" API.
3. **Reasoning is ephemeral.** `dispatch-live`/`marvin`/reviews produce prose that's overwritten; agents *consume* memory but don't *write back* reasoned semantic facts, so understanding doesn't compound.
4. **No fleet coordination.** No scheduler, no agent-to-agent RPC/events, no structured handover, no entity-level leases/ownership, no pre-merge semantic conflict detection, no cross-agent provenance graph. Git-native discovery stops at the repo boundary.

---

## The core architectural bet

**One unifying object: a Semantic Memory Graph tied to VCS history.** Entity-level meaning (`entire-sem`) + intent/reasoning (checkpoints, trails, reviews, agent runs) persisted onto version-control history (`entiredb`), unified across today's fragmented search/knowledge systems, exposed through **one** pluggable memory API (`mcp`), that agents both **read and write**, with coordination primitives (entity leases, structured handovers, provenance) on top. Every phase either *ties meaning to VCS*, *converges fragmented memory*, or *lets agents write reasoning back and coordinate over it*.

---

## Roadmap (phased; each names leverage + a convergence decision)

### Phase 0 — Wire meaning INTO the VCS store *(the literal "semantic layer tied to version control")*
- Embed `entire-sem` entity deltas into checkpoint metadata: each checkpoint records *which entities changed* (`auth.UserValidator` + callers), not just files. Reuse `entire-sem` snapshot export (already consumed by `entire-judge`) + the checkpoint metadata pipeline in `cli` (`api/checkpoint/metadata.go`, `strategy` condensation).
- Persist a **semantic index** (entity → checkpoints/sessions/authors over time) on the pushed `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch (or in `entiredb`), so "which sessions touched this subsystem?" is answerable git-natively.
- Extend the transparency log (`tlog-viewer`) to carry **semantic causality** (ref moved *because* session X changed entity Y).
- **Outcome:** meaning is stored *with* history, not re-parsed on demand. This is the keystone; everything above depends on it.

### Phase 1 — Converge the fragmented memory & retrieval *(one shared, pluggable memory)*
- **Decision A (code search):** pick one path — `peregrine` (perf/coverage) as the engine + a SCIP/`symq` precision tier + `pgr`'s agent-ranking output shaping. Kill or fold the others.
- **Decision B (knowledge):** unify `librarian` (human context) + `entire-search`/`search` (code artifacts) behind **one memory API + one embedding backbone** (the in-flight LanceDB / Qwen3-vLLM consolidation is the moment to do this).
- Expose the unified memory (semantic index + retrieval + knowledge) through **`mcp` as the single "pluggable shared memory" surface** every agent queries — same tools for Claude/Codex/Droid/etc.
- **Outcome:** "persistent, shared, pluggable memory" becomes one queryable thing instead of 5.

### Phase 2 — Capture reasoning, not just transcripts *(preserve meaning, compound it)*
- Add a **structured reasoning record** per checkpoint/trail: entities changed, decisions, constraints, risks, blast radius (from `entire-sem`) — machine-readable, not LLM prose.
- Make reasoning apps **write back**: `dispatch-live`, `marvin`, and review findings emit durable semantic facts into the memory graph (close the loop `entire-judge` hints at), so the next agent inherits prior reasoning instead of restarting.
- **Outcome:** understanding accumulates across runs; "why did we build this / what constrained it" is queryable.

### Phase 3 — Agent-to-agent coordination *(fleets in parallel, no collisions)*
- Elevate `agent-planner`'s task DAG into a **scheduler** that auto-dispatches ready tasks to sandboxes (`ferrata`/`entire-sandbox`/runners) — not just tracks readiness.
- **Structured handover format** (ContextDelta + TaskState) with auto-hydration via `mcp` (replace prose handovers).
- **Semantic collision avoidance:** entity-level leases/ownership + **pre-merge semantic conflict detection** ("agent A and B both touch `auth.Validator`") using the Phase-0 index. Extend the existing lease pattern (`repo-sync-service`) + worktree shadow branches (tag by agent id).
- **Cross-agent provenance graph:** decision → task → PR → review → decision, queryable (built on `entiredb` + the reasoning records).
- **Outcome:** fleets coordinate over shared memory without overwriting or losing understanding.

### Phase 4 — Cross-repo / cross-org shared reasoning *(break the repo boundary)*
- Git-native discovery across repos via `mirror-pipeline`/`entiredb` federation: "who reasoned about similar code elsewhere?"
- Agent **capability registry + discovery** (extend `external-agents`) so tasks route to the right agent.
- **Outcome:** the memory is shared across teams and fleets, not just within a repo.

---

## Sequencing recommendation (the one bet)

**Do Phase 0 first and treat it as the company's convergence forcing-function.** It is the literal thesis ("semantic layer tied to VCS"), it's unblocked (`entire-sem` is proven, checkpoints are production), and it turns the scattered experiments into *consumers of one index* — which naturally drives the Phase-1 convergence decisions. Resist adding more capture/execution surfaces until meaning is in the store and memory is unified; that breadth is where drift is happening now.

## Risks / decisions the team must make
- **Convergence courage:** Phases 1 requires *killing* duplicate search/knowledge efforts. Politically hard, technically essential.
- **Where the semantic index lives:** on `entire/checkpoints/v1` (git-native, portable) vs in `entiredb`/control-plane (queryable at scale). Likely both, but the source of truth must be decided.
- **Write-back trust:** agents writing reasoned facts into shared memory needs provenance + authz (`mcp`/SpiceDB already gate this) so a bad agent can't poison shared understanding.
- **Scope of "reasoning record":** structured schema vs freeform — must be structured enough to query, loose enough to not straitjacket agents.

## How we'd know each phase landed (verification)
- **P0:** `entire`/`mcp` can answer "which checkpoints changed entity X" from the git-native index; a checkpoint's metadata shows entity deltas.
- **P1:** one `mcp` tool returns unified results across code + human knowledge; only one search engine and one embedding backbone remain in prod.
- **P2:** a second agent run demonstrably reuses the prior run's structured reasoning (not re-derived); reasoning survives across sessions.
- **P3:** two agents editing the same entity in parallel get a pre-merge conflict warning; a scheduler auto-dispatches a ready task; provenance query returns the decision cascade.
- **P4:** an agent in repo A surfaces relevant reasoning from repo B.

---

*Note: this plan file is a strategy roadmap, not a code-change plan. "Approving" it means the direction/sequencing is agreed; concrete implementation plans (e.g. Phase 0 checkpoint↔entire-sem wiring) would each get their own focused plan.*

########### entirehq/peregrine ###########
=== README ===
# peregrine

A fast code search engine with trigram indexing, cross-file navigation, and a web UI. Single binary, single `.pg` index format.

## Features

- **Trigram-based search** — content and path search with regex support. Extracts literal fragments from regex patterns to prune via trigram index before running the regex engine.
- **Cross-file go-to-definition** — click any reference and navigate to its definition within the same repo. 15 languages supported via tree-sitter.
- **Incremental indexing** — file-level granularity using git diff-tree. Only changed files are re-indexed; unchanged files are carried forward as compressed blobs.
- **Compact indexes** — zstd-compressed file content. 4-5x smaller than Zoekt on the same corpus.
- **Multi-repo search** — parallel fan-out across repos with configurable concurrency.
- **Web UI** — Next.js frontend with search, file viewer, clickable code references, and collapsible symbol sidebar.

## Performance

Benchmarked on Apple M4 Pro against Zoekt across 10 Go repos (72K files):

| Metric | peregrine | Zoekt | Ratio |
|--------|-----------|-------|-------|
| Index size (kubernetes, 29K files) | 125 MB | 612 MB | **4.9x smaller** |
| Full build (kubernetes) | 2.5s | 4.5s | **1.8x faster** |
| Incremental rebuild, no changes (kubernetes) | 2.6ms | 33.6ms | **13x faster** |
| Incremental rebuild, small change (kubernetes) | 457ms | 8.6s | **19x faster** |
| Exact search `HandleFunc` | 10.7ms | 42.3ms | **4.0x faster** |
| Regex `if\s+err\s*!=\s*nil` | 106ms | 499ms | **4.7x faster** |

## Supported Languages

**Tier 1** — full symbol extraction + cross-file resolution:

Go, Rust, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C, C++, C#, Ruby, Kotlin, Scala, Swift, PHP, Elixir

**Tier 2** — indexed and searchable, no symbol extraction:

HTML, CSS, SQL, YAML, TOML, JSON, Markdown, Protobuf, Dockerfile, HCL, Bash, Lua

## Quick Start

### Build

```bash
cargo build --release
```

### Index a repo

```bash
peregrine index \
  --source /path/to/repo \
  --output ./data/myrepo.pg \
  --repo-name myrepo \
  --org-id myorg
```

### Search from CLI

```bash
# Text search
peregrine search --index ./data/myrepo.pg "HandleFunc"

# Regex search
peregrine search --index ./data/myrepo.pg "func\s+\w+\(" --json

# Search across all indexes in a directory
peregrine search --index-dir ./data "TODO"

# Symbol search
peregrine search --index ./data/myrepo.pg "Config" --kind struct --defs
```

### Start the server

```bash
peregrine serve --index-dir ./data --http-port 8080
```

This starts both the gRPC server (port 50051) and the HTTP/JSON API (port 8080).

content.text:
This is the most on-thesis thing I've seen all session. Here's what I got out of it.

## What `regente` is

**"A local coordination backplane for already-running coding agents."** It doesn't spawn agents — it coordinates ones already running (claude-code/cursor/codex/gemini) via **MCP + hooks + CLI**, storing everything in a per-project `.regente/` dir (I see it embedded in `entire-judge`, `comm`, `Ultron`, `entire-brain`). Zero-dependency Node, ~20 test suites (fencing, signing, symbol-claims, enforcement, concurrency, roles, lanes…) — a real, tested prototype, not a toy.

## Why it matters: it fills the *exact* gap the ecosystem is missing

Agent 3's finding was blunt: Entire is "~90% humans+agents together, ~0–10% fleets coordinating without collision" — no agent↔agent messaging, no scheduler, no structured handovers, no **semantic collision detection**, no registry. `regente` implements essentially all of it, and its `.regente/` files map 1:1 onto those gaps:

| Roadmap gap (Phase 3) | `regente` primitive |
|---|---|
| Agent↔agent messaging | `messages.jsonl`, `post_message`/`inbox`/`ack_message` with **read receipts** |
| Agent registry / discovery | `roles.json`, `team.json`, `list_agents`, presence via MCP heartbeat |
| Structured handovers | `handoffs.jsonl`, `check_handoffs`, auto-handoff on expiry |
| Leases / fencing | claim expiry + sweep, `fencing_test`, `enforcement` |
| Delegation / scheduler seed | `regente call <agent>` → creates a task, assigns, messages, writes handoff |
| **Semantic collision avoidance** | **`claim_path` with a `symbol` arg — claim a single function, not the whole file**; edit-guard auto-claims + warns on recent same-file edits |
| Provenance | commit signing / `verify_commit` |

The standout is **symbol-level claims** — the single hardest gap in my roadmap (entity-level ownership so two agents can work the same file without colliding). `regente` already does it.

## The killer synergy (this is the "help")

`regente`'s symbol parser is honestly a **zero-dependency heuristic** — JS/TS/Py only, and its own header admits the limits (multi-line sigs, TS generics, JSX, nested funcs). **That's precisely what `entire-sem` is: an AST-accurate, benchmarked (F1 1.0 symbols), 15+-language entity+call-graph extractor.**

> **`regente` (coordination) ⊗ `entire-sem` (semantic truth) = the full "semantic collision avoidance / entity-level leases" capability** my roadmap's Phase 0+3 needs — and it's the piece nobody in the ecosystem has built. `regente` proves the coordination UX works; `entire-sem` upgrades its claim substrate from heuristic to compiler-grade. And if claims/handoffs get persisted onto VCS history (`entiredb`) instead of a local `.regente/` dir, you've got the *shared* (not just local) coordination the vision demands.

## Honest caveats
- It's your **personal repo** (`suhaanthayyil/regente-core`, 3 commits, ~3 weeks old), **local-first** (`.regente/` is per-machine, not shared across a fleet on different machines yet), and the symbol parser is heuristic. So it's a **strong proof-of-concept + design source**, not production.
- It overlaps with `agent-planner` (task DAG/handovers/presence) — so the question isn't "regente vs agent-planner," it's "regente's *symbol-claim + fencing + read-receipt* model is the missing coordination substrate `agent-planner` doesn't have."

## What I'd do with it
1. **Use it as the reference design for Phase 3** of the roadmap — it de-risks the hardest layer (proven UX for claims/handoffs/messaging/fencing).
2. **Prototype the `regente` ⊗ `entire-sem` swap**: replace the heuristic symbol parser with `entire-sem` snapshots → real semantic claims. Small, high-signal spike.
3. **Sketch making claims *shared*** (persist to a branch/`entiredb`) so coordination survives across machines — that turns it from "local backplane" into the vision's "shared memory for fleets."

Want me to (a) write up a focused spike plan for `regente` ⊗ `entire-sem`, or (b) do a deeper read of `regente-core` (the fencing/enforcement + MCP tool surface) and produce a proper design doc comparing it to `agent-planner` so you can decide what to upstream into Entire?

input.name: Semantic Index Tied to VCS History
input.summary: Keystone: persist entity-level meaning (from the semantic extractor) onto checkpoints + a git-native index, so meaning is stored with version-control history, not re-parsed on demand.
input.description:
**The keystone of the initiative.** "Version control preserves change, not meaning." We have an accurate semantic extractor (entity + call-graph, compiler-benchmarked in `brain-bench`), but its output is not persisted with checkpoints — so meaning is re-parsed on demand and can't be queried over history.

## Outcome
Every checkpoint records *which semantic entities changed* (e.g. `auth.UserValidator` + its callers), and a git-native index answers *"which sessions/authors touched entity X over time."* This is the literal "semantic layer directly tied to version-control history" — and everything else in the initiative depends on it.

## Key work
- Wire semantic entity deltas into checkpoint metadata (CLI checkpoint metadata + condensation path).
- Persist an entity → checkpoint/session index on the pushed `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch (and/or entiredb).
- Add semantic causality to the transparency log (a ref moved *because* session X changed entity Y).

## Dependencies
Semantic extractor (`entire-sem`), CLI checkpoints, `entiredb`.

## Definition of done
`entire` / MCP can answer "which checkpoints changed entity X" from the index; a checkpoint's metadata shows its entity deltas.

input.name: Unified, Pluggable Agent Memory
input.summary: Converge the fragmented retrieval + knowledge systems into one shared memory on one backbone, exposed through MCP so every agent queries the same thing.
input.description:
**Make memory "shared and pluggable."** Today memory + retrieval are fragmented: several parallel code-search efforts and two parallel knowledge systems. No single shared, pluggable memory surface exists — which the vision explicitly requires.

## Outcome
One shared memory (semantic index + code retrieval + knowledge) on **one** embedding backbone, exposed through **MCP** so every agent (Claude Code / Codex / Droid / Cursor / Gemini / …) queries the same memory with the same tools.

## Key work
- Converge code search on one engine (fast trigram engine + compiler-precise symbol tier + agent-aware ranking); retire duplicates.
- Unify the human-knowledge and code-artifact indexes on one embedding / vector backbone (the in-flight consolidation is the moment to do it).
- Expose the unified memory (semantic index + retrieval + knowledge) as a single MCP shared-memory surface.

## Dependencies
Semantic index (P0), the code-search + knowledge/search services, MCP.

## Definition of done
One MCP tool returns unified results across code + knowledge; only one search engine and one embedding backbone remain in production.

content.text: Two projects created. Now the remaining three:

input.name: Reasoning Capture & Compounding Memory
input.summary: Capture agent reasoning (not just transcripts) as structured, queryable facts that compound across runs — so understanding is preserved, not restarted.
input.description:
**Preserve meaning, and make it compound.** Agents capture transcripts, not reasoning. Reasoning surfaces (review, scheduled synthesis, chat assistants) emit prose that gets overwritten; agents *consume* memory but don't *write reasoned facts back* — so understanding restarts every run.

## Outcome
A structured reasoning record per checkpoint/trail (entities changed, decisions, constraints, risks, blast radius — machine-readable, not LLM prose), reasoning apps that write durable semantic facts back, and a provenance graph. Understanding accumulates; *"why did we build this / what constrained it"* becomes queryable.

## Key work
- Define a structured reasoning-record schema (built on the P0 entity deltas).
- Make reasoning producers (review findings, scheduled synthesis, assistants) write durable semantic facts into shared memory.
- Build a provenance graph: decision → task → PR → review → decision.

## Dependencies
Semantic index (P0), unified memory (P1), CLI, existing reasoning/synthesis surfaces.

## Definition of done
A second agent run demonstrably reuses the prior run's structured reasoning (not re-derived); a provenance query returns the decision cascade.

input.name: Semantic Collision-Free Parallel Agents
input.summary: Let fleets of agents build in parallel without colliding: entity-level claims, pre-merge semantic conflict detection, structured handovers, and a scheduler over ready tasks.
input.description:
**Fleets that build in parallel "without overwriting, colliding, or losing understanding."** Today agents can't coordinate: no entity-level ownership, no pre-merge semantic conflict detection, no structured handovers, no scheduler. Two agents editing the same function silently collide.

## Outcome
Agents claim work at the **entity level** (a function/type, not the whole file) using the P0 semantic index; overlapping edits are detected **before merge**; handovers are **structured and auto-hydrated** (not prose); ready tasks **auto-dispatch** to sandboxes. Isolation primitives already exist (worktree shadow branches, sandboxes, a task DAG) — this composes them into real coordination.

## Key work
- Entity-level claim/lease primitive with expiry/sweep (built on the P0 entity model).
- Pre-merge semantic conflict detection over concurrent claims.
- Structured handover format + auto-hydration via MCP.
- Scheduler that dispatches ready tasks to sandboxes; agent presence + read-receipt messaging.

## Dependencies
Semantic index (P0), the task-DAG/handover substrate (`agent-planner`), CLI worktree shadow branches, the sandbox execution stack.

## Definition of done
Two agents editing the same entity get a pre-merge conflict warning; a ready task auto-dispatches; a handover auto-hydrates into the next agent's context.

input.name: Cross-Repo Shared Reasoning
input.summary: Break the repo boundary: shared semantic reasoning across repos/orgs, plus a capability registry so tasks route to the right agent.
input.description:
**Make the memory shared across teams and fleets, not just within a repo.** Git-native discovery stops at the repo boundary — an agent can't find who reasoned about similar code elsewhere, and there's no registry to route a task to the right agent.

## Outcome
Shared reasoning across repos/orgs: an agent in one repo surfaces relevant prior reasoning from another; tasks route to the right agent by capability.

## Key work
- Cross-repo semantic discovery over the federated index (git mirroring / `entiredb` federation on top of the P0 index).
- Agent capability registry + discovery (extend the external-agents plugin model).

## Dependencies
Semantic index (P0), unified memory (P1), git mirror pipeline, `entiredb`, external-agents.

## Definition of done
An agent working in repo A surfaces relevant reasoning from repo B; tasks route to an agent by declared capability.

--- README ---
# Entire Brain

Entire Brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI. It builds a
local, inspectable "brain" for a repository from Entire session history, seeded
repository context, a local history index, an index of the brain's own docs (seed
summaries and copied repo markdown), optional semantic records from `entire-sem`,
and a curated layer of durable facts distilled from past sessions.

The plugin binary is named `entire-brain` and is invoked through Entire as:

```sh
entire brain
```

Generated brain artifacts are local and inspectable by default: deterministic
refresh/index/retrieval reads local repositories and writes local plugin data,
and the MCP adapter is stdio-only. Optional agent-gated steps can send selected
context to the configured agent (`refresh --agent auto`, `distill --agent
codex|claude-code`, `recall --expand`, and judged evals). Use `--agent none`,
`--dry-run`, `--agent command` with a local command, or loopback-only Ollama to
avoid hosted model egress. Strict no-egress mode (`ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS=1` or
`ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY=1`) can only enforce no-agent, dry-run, and Ollama
paths whose URLs, redirects, and resolved dial targets stay loopback-only;
arbitrary `--agent command` runners are trusted local commands but not
enforceably loopback-only. Separately, repos that configure a
`checkpoint_remote` allow `refresh` (and its `sessions` export stage) to `git fetch` checkpoint history
from that remote into a throwaway temp repo unless no-egress mode is set.

## Install

```sh
mise install
mise run check
mise run build
entire plugin install ./entire-brain
entire brain
```

For a one-command local source install of this plugin, run:

```sh
scripts/install-local.sh
```

For an end-to-end local install that builds the sibling `entire-sem` checkout
first and then installs `entire-brain`, run:

```sh
scripts/install.sh
```

For local release archives with `SHA256SUMS`, run:

```sh
scripts/release.sh
```

See [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md) for target, cgo, and shared
baseline details.

# Entire Sem

`entire-sem` is an Entire CLI plugin for entity-level checkpoint context.

Entire already knows a checkpoint touched `auth.py` or `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
This plugin answers the next question: which semantic entities changed inside that file?

This plugin builds a binary named `entire-sem`, which is invoked through Entire as:

```sh
entire sem commit HEAD
entire sem checkpoint abc123def456
entire sem diff --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD
entire sem analyze --json
entire sem capabilities --json
entire sem snapshot --repo . --format ndjson
entire sem symbols --repo . --format ndjson
entire sem edges --repo . --format ndjson
entire sem snapshot --repo . --format ndjson --worktree --ignore-file .brainignore
entire sem snapshot --repo . --format ndjson --worktree --include-file .seminclude
```

## Status

This plugin implements the semantic checkpoint context proposed in
[entireio/cli#589](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/589). It intentionally
does not vendor or copy Ataraxy Labs' `inspect` / `sem` projects.

The plugin uses a tree-sitter-backed parser for:

- Bash
- C / C++
- C#
- CUE
- Elixir
- Go
- Groovy
- HCL / Terraform
- Java
- JavaScript / TypeScript
- Kotlin
- Lua
- OCaml
- PHP
- Protocol Buffers

43	// crossJurisRoundTripper handles two recoverable failure modes uniformly,
44	// for every control-plane HTTP call that wraps its transport:
45	//
46	//   - 421 Misdirected Request: a control-plane core responded that the
47	//     target resource lives in another jurisdiction and returned the
48	//     home core's base URL. The transport rewrites the request URL and
49	//     retries once.
50	//   - 401 needing a cross-juris token exchange. Two shapes:
51	//     (a) the structured hint `{"error":"cross_juris_token_required",
52	//     "token_exchange_url":"...","audience":"..."}` — emitted by a core
53	//     that can verify the JWT's signature but sees a sibling audience; and
54	//     (b) a BARE 401 received right after following a 421 — the home core
55	//     can't verify a foreign-region login JWT's signature (its API
56	//     verifier trusts only local JWKS), so it never reaches the audience
57	//     check and emits no hint. In both cases the transport POSTs an RFC
58	//     8693 exchange at the home core's /oauth/token (subject_token = the
59	//     original Authorization Bearer), caches the resulting access token
60	//     keyed by origin, swaps the Authorization header, and retries once.
61	//
62	// Each original request gets at most one redirect and one exchange per
63	// origin — a 421 followed by an exchange-retry is allowed; further
64	// recursion is a server bug we want to surface, not paper over.
65	//
66	// Per-origin token cache lives on the transport instance, scoped to one
67	// CLI invocation. A cached token's TTL honors the exchange response's
68	// expires_in (minus a safety buffer), capped at cachedTokenTTL so we

102	// expiry — the server would 401, we'd re-exchange, and the user would

163	// RoundTrip implements http.RoundTripper. On the first attempt it swaps
164	// the Authorization header to a cached exchanged token when one exists
165	// for the request origin; otherwise the caller-supplied header is used.
166	//
167	// The original caller-supplied bearer is snapshotted at entry and used
168	// as the subject_token on every exchange — re-using a previously-
169	// exchanged token would already carry foreign_iss and the validator
170	// rejects chained cross-juris exchanges.
171	func (t *crossJurisRoundTripper) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
172		body, err := bufferBody(req)
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cross-juris transport: buffer body: %w", err)
175		}
176		originalAuth := req.Header.Get("Authorization")
177		return t.send(req, body, originalAuth, retryBudget{redirects: 1, triedExchange: map[string]bool{}})
178	}

180	// retryBudget caps the recursion. Redirects share one budget across the
181	// whole call; exchanges are bounded per-origin via triedExchange so a
182	// 421-then-401 chain doesn't starve the home core of its first attempt.
183	//
184	// afterRedirect records that the current hop was reached by following a
185	// 421. It flips on the bare-401 recovery: a home core reached via 421
186	// can't verify a foreign-region login JWT's signature (its API verifier
187	// trusts only local JWKS), so it returns a bare 401 rather than the
188	// cross_juris_token_required hint. On a redirected hop we treat that
189	// bare 401 as an exchange trigger; on a non-redirected hop a bare 401 is
190	// a genuine auth failure and passes through.
191	type retryBudget struct {
192		redirects     int
193		triedExchange map[string]bool
194		afterRedirect bool
195	}
