197	func (t *crossJurisRoundTripper) send(req *http.Request, body []byte, originalAuth string, budget retryBudget) (*http.Response, error) {
198		// Pick the Authorization for this hop: cached exchanged token for
199		// this origin if present (cache hit), otherwise the original caller-
200		// supplied bearer. Crucially we DON'T inherit whatever Authorization
201		// happens to be on req.Header — a previous hop may have stamped an
202		// exchanged token scoped to a different origin, and presenting that
203		// here would be wrong on its face AND would corrupt subject_token
204		// for any exchange this hop ends up doing.
205		origin := requestOrigin(req)
206		switch cached, ok := t.lookupToken(origin); {
207		case ok:
208			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+cached)
209		case originalAuth != "":
210			req.Header.Set("Authorization", originalAuth)
211		}
212		resetBody(req, body)
213	
214		resp, err := t.base.RoundTrip(req)
215		if err != nil {
216			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cross-juris transport: base round trip: %w", err)
217		}
218	
219		switch resp.StatusCode {
220		case http.StatusMisdirectedRequest:
221			if budget.redirects <= 0 {
222				return resp, nil
223			}
224			newReq, err := t.followMisdirected(req, resp, origin)
225			if err != nil {
226				// Couldn't follow — surface the original response so the
227				// caller sees the server's body.
228				debugf("421 follow failed: %v", err)
229				return resp, nil
230			}
231			_ = resp.Body.Close()
232			budget.redirects--
233			budget.afterRedirect = true
234			return t.send(newReq, body, originalAuth, budget)
235		case http.StatusUnauthorized:
236			if budget.triedExchange[origin] {
237				return resp, nil
238			}
239			hint, ok, err := readCrossJurisHint(resp)
240			if err != nil {
241				debugf("read 401 body failed: %v", err)
242				return resp, nil
243			}
244			if !ok {
245				// No structured hint. On a non-redirected hop this is an
246				// ordinary auth failure — pass it through. But a home core
247				// reached by following a 421 returns a bare 401 for a
248				// foreign-region login JWT (its API verifier trusts only
249				// local JWKS, so the signature check fails before audience and
250				// no cross_juris_token_required hint is emitted). We already
251				// vetted this origin against the responding core's federation
252				// manifest when we followed the 421, so synthesize the hint
253				// from it: the core's /oauth/token is same-origin and its
254				// audience is its own base URL.
255				if !budget.afterRedirect {
256					return resp, nil
257				}
258				hint = crossJurisErrorBody{
259					Error:            "cross_juris_token_required",
260					TokenExchangeURL: origin + oauthTokenPath,
261					Audience:         origin,
262				}
263			}
264			// Same-origin + safe-scheme check before re-targeting the user's
265			// login JWT: a 401 emitted by a core has no legitimate reason to
266			// point token_exchange_url at any other host. Off-origin or
267			// http:// (non-loopback) hints get the original 401 passed
268			// through unchanged so the caller sees the server's bytes and
269			// the JWT never leaves the trusted origin.
270			if err := validateExchangeURL(hint.TokenExchangeURL, req.URL); err != nil {
271				debugf("rejecting token_exchange_url: %v", err)
272				return resp, nil
273			}
274			// Exchange the ORIGINAL login JWT (not whatever exchanged token
275			// a prior hop stashed on req). An exchanged token already
276			// carries foreign_iss; the server rejects chained cross-juris hops.
277			subjectToken, found := strings.CutPrefix(originalAuth, "Bearer ")
278			if !found || subjectToken == "" {
279				return resp, nil
280			}
281			exchanged, expiresIn, err := t.exchangeSubjectToken(req.Context(), hint, subjectToken)
282			if err != nil {
283				debugf("exchange failed: %v", err)
284				return resp, nil
285			}
286			t.storeToken(origin, exchanged, effectiveTokenTTL(expiresIn))
287			budget.triedExchange[origin] = true
288			_ = resp.Body.Close()
289			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+exchanged)
290			return t.send(req, body, originalAuth, budget)
291		}
292		return resp, nil
293	}
294	
295	// followMisdirected reads the 421 envelope and constructs a fresh
296	// request aimed at the home core. Method, headers, and (buffered) body
297	// are preserved on the new request. On parse failure the original
298	// response body is restored (the caller is about to return resp
299	// unchanged) so downstream consumers still see the server's bytes.
300	//
301	// Trust gate: home_core_url must be HTTPS (loopback http allowed for
302	// tests), and its host must appear in the federation manifest fetched
303	// lazily from responseOrigin (the host that emitted the 421 — already
304	// a trusted origin for the CLI). Off-federation or off-scheme targets
305	// surface the original 421 unchanged.
306	func (t *crossJurisRoundTripper) followMisdirected(orig *http.Request, resp *http.Response, responseOrigin string) (*http.Request, error) {
307		body, err := drainAndRestoreBody(resp, 64*1024)
308		if err != nil {
309			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read 421 body: %w", err)
310		}
311		var env mirror421Body
312		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &env); err != nil {
313			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse 421 body: %w", err)
314		}
315		if env.HomeCoreURL == "" {
316			return nil, errors.New("421 body missing home_core_url")
317		}
318		homeCore, err := url.Parse(strings.TrimRight(env.HomeCoreURL, "/"))
319		if err != nil {
320			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse home_core_url: %w", err)
321		}
322		if !isSafeOrigin(homeCore) {
323			return nil, fmt.Errorf("home_core_url %q is not https (or http loopback)", env.HomeCoreURL)
324		}
325		peers := t.federationHostsFor(orig.Context(), responseOrigin)
326		if _, ok := peers[homeCore.Host]; !ok {
327			return nil, fmt.Errorf("home_core_url host %q is not in the responding core's federation manifest", homeCore.Host)
328		}
329		target := *homeCore
330		target.Path = orig.URL.Path
331		target.RawQuery = orig.URL.RawQuery
332		newReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(orig.Context(), orig.Method, target.String(), nil)
333		if err != nil {
334			return nil, fmt.Errorf("build redirected request: %w", err)
335		}
336		newReq.Header = orig.Header.Clone()
337		return newReq, nil
338	}

340	// validateExchangeURL gates the URL the transport will POST the user's
341	// login JWT to for an RFC 8693 exchange. Two checks:
342	//
343	//   - Scheme must be https, except http://localhost for tests.
344	//   - Host must equal the request URL host that emitted the 401. A
345	//     core's /oauth/token always lives on the same origin as its
346	//     middleware; off-origin hints have no legitimate use and would
347	//     let a misconfigured / hostile core exfiltrate the user's JWT.
348	//   - Path must be exactly oauthTokenPath. exchangeSubjectToken strips

353		if raw == "" {
354			return errors.New("token_exchange_url missing")
355		}
356		exchange, err := url.Parse(raw)
357		if err != nil {
358			return fmt.Errorf("parse token_exchange_url: %w", err)
359		}
360		if !isSafeOrigin(exchange) {
361			return fmt.Errorf("token_exchange_url %q is not https (or http loopback)", raw)
362		}
363		if requestURL == nil || requestURL.Host == "" {
364			return errors.New("cannot determine response origin for same-origin check")
365		}
366		if exchange.Host != requestURL.Host {
367			return fmt.Errorf("token_exchange_url host %q must match response host %q", exchange.Host, requestURL.Host)
368		}
369		if exchange.Path != oauthTokenPath {
370			return fmt.Errorf("token_exchange_url path %q must be %q", exchange.Path, oauthTokenPath)
371		}
372		return nil
373	}

375	// isSafeOrigin reports whether u is acceptable as a destination for the
376	// user's login JWT. https is always allowed; http is allowed only for
377	// loopback so httptest fixtures keep working.
378	func isSafeOrigin(u *url.URL) bool {
379		switch u.Scheme {
380		case "https":
381			return u.Host != ""
382		case "http":
383			return isLoopbackHost(u.Hostname())
384		default:
385			return false
386		}
387	}

389	// isLoopbackHost reports whether host is a loopback name or IP. Used
390	// only to widen isSafeOrigin for local/test fixtures — production
391	// federation traffic is always https.
392	func isLoopbackHost(host string) bool {
393		switch host {
394		case "localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1":
395			return true
396		}
397		return false
398	}

400	// federationHostsFor returns the set of hosts the core at origin
401	// publishes as its federation peers (via GET /.well-known/entire-
402	// federation). Cached for the life of the transport. nil result means
403	// the origin advertises no peers OR the fetch failed; either way, no
404	// 421 redirect from this origin will be followed.
405	func (t *crossJurisRoundTripper) federationHostsFor(ctx context.Context, origin string) map[string]struct{} {
406		if origin == "" {
407			return nil
408		}
409		if v, ok := t.federation.Load(origin); ok {
410			cached, _ := v.(cachedFederation) //nolint:errcheck // type assertion, not error
411			return cached.hosts
412		}
413		hosts := t.fetchFederationHosts(ctx, origin)
414		t.federation.Store(origin, cachedFederation{hosts: hosts})
415		return hosts
416	}
417	
418	// fetchFederationHosts performs the one-shot GET against origin's
419	// well-known endpoint. Returns nil on any failure (transport error,
420	// non-200, parse error, empty list) — federationHostsFor caches the
421	// nil so we don't pound the endpoint per 421.
422	func (t *crossJurisRoundTripper) fetchFederationHosts(ctx context.Context, origin string) map[string]struct{} {
423		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, federationLookupTimeout)
424		defer cancel()
425		// origin is the scheme://host of a core the CLI is already configured to
426		// talk to (or one it just received a response from), and the path is a
427		// fixed public well-known endpoint — not attacker-controlled SSRF.
428		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, origin+federationWellKnownPath, nil) //nolint:gosec // G704: origin is a core the CLI already dials; fixed well-known path
429		if err != nil {
430			debugf("build federation request: %v", err)
431			return nil
432		}
433		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
434		resp, err := t.base.RoundTrip(req)
435		if err != nil {
436			debugf("federation fetch: %v", err)
437			return nil
438		}
439		defer resp.Body.Close()
440		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
441			debugf("federation fetch returned HTTP %d", resp.StatusCode)
442			return nil
443		}
444		body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 16*1024))
445		if err != nil {
446			debugf("read federation body: %v", err)
447			return nil
448		}
449		var env federationBody
450		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &env); err != nil {
451			debugf("parse federation body: %v", err)
452			return nil
453		}
454		if len(env.PeerAuthHosts) == 0 {
455			return nil
456		}
457		out := make(map[string]struct{}, len(env.PeerAuthHosts))
458		for _, raw := range env.PeerAuthHosts {
459			u, err := url.Parse(raw)
460			if err != nil || u.Host == "" {
461				continue
462			}
463			out[u.Host] = struct{}{}
464		}
465		return out
466	}
467	
468	// readCrossJurisHint reads the structured 401 envelope. Returns ok=false
469	// when the body isn't the expected shape (a plain 401 from somewhere
470	// else, an HTML proxy error, etc.) so the caller passes the response
471	// through unchanged. The body is restored regardless so downstream
472	// consumers can re-read.
473	func readCrossJurisHint(resp *http.Response) (crossJurisErrorBody, bool, error) {
474		body, err := drainAndRestoreBody(resp, 8*1024)
475		if err != nil {
476			return crossJurisErrorBody{}, false, fmt.Errorf("read 401 body: %w", err)
477		}
478		var env crossJurisErrorBody
479		// Unmarshal failure means the body isn't our envelope shape (HTML
480		// proxy error, a different JSON shape, garbage). That's the
481		// not-a-hint case, not an error condition — the caller passes the
482		// response through unchanged.
483		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &env); err != nil {
484			return crossJurisErrorBody{}, false, nil //nolint:nilerr // unmarshal-fail = "not our envelope shape"
485		}
486		if env.Error != "cross_juris_token_required" || env.TokenExchangeURL == "" {
487			return crossJurisErrorBody{}, false, nil
488		}
489		return env, true, nil
490	}
491	
492	// drainAndRestoreBody reads up to maxBytes from resp.Body and replaces
493	// resp.Body with a fresh in-memory reader over those bytes, so the
494	// caller can hand resp back to its own caller with the body still
495	// readable. Cap is conservative — control-plane error envelopes are
496	// always small.
497	func drainAndRestoreBody(resp *http.Response, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, error) {
498		body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxBytes))
499		_ = resp.Body.Close()
500		resp.Body = io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(body)) // restore even on error
501		if err != nil {
502			return nil, fmt.Errorf("drain response body: %w", err)
503		}
504		return body, nil
505	}
506	
507	// exchangeSubjectToken performs the RFC 8693 cross-juris session
508	// exchange and returns the issued access_token. Delegates the wire-
509	// level details (form encode, lifting client_id into Basic auth,
510	// response decode) to httputil.PostOAuthToken.
511	func (t *crossJurisRoundTripper) exchangeSubjectToken(ctx context.Context, hint crossJurisErrorBody, subjectToken string) (string, int, error) {
512		form := url.Values{}
513		form.Set("grant_type", httputil.GrantTypeTokenExchange)
514		form.Set("subject_token", subjectToken)
515		form.Set("subject_token_type", "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt")
516		form.Set("requested_token_type", httputil.TokenTypeAccessToken)
517		if hint.Audience != "" {
518			form.Set("audience", hint.Audience)
519		}
520		// "entire-cli" is the public client every CLI binary identifies as on
521		// /oauth/token; PostOAuthToken lifts it into Basic auth because
522		// pkg/op's token-exchange handler reads client credentials only from
523		// the Authorization header. The subject_token is the real authorizer.
524		form.Set("client_id", "entire-cli")
525		// PostOAuthToken expects a base core URL and appends /oauth/token
526		// itself; hint.TokenExchangeURL is already the full path (and
527		// validateExchangeURL has gated both origin and path == oauthTokenPath),
528		// so stripping the suffix yields exactly the origin.
529		coreURL := strings.TrimSuffix(hint.TokenExchangeURL, oauthTokenPath)
530		// Exchange goes through the base transport so we don't re-enter our
531		// own retry logic — a non-200 here is terminal.
532		client := &http.Client{Transport: t.base}
533		token, expiresIn, err := httputil.PostOAuthToken(ctx, client, coreURL, form)
534		if err != nil {
535			return "", 0, fmt.Errorf("exchange: %w", err)
536		}
537		return token, expiresIn, nil
538	}
539	
540	func (t *crossJurisRoundTripper) lookupToken(origin string) (string, bool) {
541		v, ok := t.tokens.Load(origin)
542		if !ok {
543			return "", false
544		}
545		cached, _ := v.(cachedExchangedToken) //nolint:errcheck // type assertion, not error
546		if time.Now().After(cached.exp) {
547			t.tokens.Delete(origin)
548			return "", false
549		}
550		return cached.token, true
551	}
552	
553	func (t *crossJurisRoundTripper) storeToken(origin, token string, ttl time.Duration) {
554		if origin == "" || token == "" || ttl <= 0 {
555			return
556		}
557		t.tokens.Store(origin, cachedExchangedToken{
558			token: token,
559			exp:   time.Now().Add(ttl),
560		})
561	}
562	
563	// effectiveTokenTTL picks how long an exchanged token may live in the
564	// per-origin cache. It honors the exchange response's expires_in (less a
565	// safety buffer so we never serve a token within seconds of expiry),
566	// capped at cachedTokenTTL. A non-positive expires_in means the server
567	// advertised no lifetime, so we fall back to the conservative cap; a
568	// lifetime shorter than the buffer yields <=0, which storeToken declines
569	// to cache (the triggering request still succeeds via the live retry).
570	func effectiveTokenTTL(expiresIn int) time.Duration {
571		if expiresIn <= 0 {
572			return cachedTokenTTL
573		}
574		ttl := time.Duration(expiresIn)*time.Second - tokenExpiryBuffer
575		if ttl > cachedTokenTTL {
576			return cachedTokenTTL
577		}
578		return ttl
579	}
580	
581	// bufferBody reads req.Body once into memory and sets GetBody so each
582	// retry produces a fresh reader. Returns nil when there's no body.
583	func bufferBody(req *http.Request) ([]byte, error) {
584		if req.Body == nil || req.Body == http.NoBody {
585			return nil, nil
586		}
587		buf, err := io.ReadAll(req.Body)
588		if err != nil {
589			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read request body: %w", err)
590		}
591		_ = req.Body.Close()
592		return buf, nil
593	}
594	
595	// resetBody attaches a fresh body reader (and ContentLength) to req,
596	// using the buffer captured by bufferBody. Safe to call when buf is nil.
597	func resetBody(req *http.Request, buf []byte) {
598		if buf == nil {
599			req.Body = http.NoBody
600			req.ContentLength = 0
601			req.GetBody = func() (io.ReadCloser, error) { return http.NoBody, nil }
602			return
603		}
604		req.Body = io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(buf))
605		req.ContentLength = int64(len(buf))
606		req.GetBody = func() (io.ReadCloser, error) {
607			return io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(buf)), nil
608		}
609	}
610	
611	// requestOrigin returns scheme://host of req, the cache key for
612	// exchanged tokens. Empty when req.URL is malformed.
613	func requestOrigin(req *http.Request) string {
614		if req.URL == nil || req.URL.Scheme == "" || req.URL.Host == "" {
615			return ""
616		}
617		return req.URL.Scheme + "://" + req.URL.Host
618	}

1	package discovery
2	
3	import (
4		"path/filepath"
5		"time"
6	)
7	
8	const (
9		clusterCoresFileName = "cluster_cores.json"
10	
11		// apiDiscoveryFileName caches a data-API host's trusted issuer URLs, the
12		// same shape a git cluster's cores take. Kept in a separate file from
13		// cluster_cores.json so a cluster host and an API host that happen to share
14		// a name can't collide on one cache key.
15		apiDiscoveryFileName = "api_discovery.json"
16	
17		// ClusterCoresTTL bounds how long a cached host→trusted-issuer-URLs mapping
18		// is treated as fresh, for both clusters and data APIs. Which login
19		// server(s) front a resource is near-static infra — once homed it stays —
20		// so a long TTL is fine. On expiry we re-fetch /.well-known and only fall
21		// back to the stale entry if that fetch fails.
22		ClusterCoresTTL = 24 * time.Hour
23	)
24	
25	// ClusterCoresCache maps a cluster host to the control-plane core URLs that
26	// front it, memoizing /.well-known/entire-cluster.json so routine git ops
27	// don't re-fetch it every time. It stores only the objective cluster→core
28	// fact — never which local account to authenticate as. The account is chosen
29	// fresh on every operation from the user's contexts, so a multi-account user
30	// is never silently pinned to one identity.
31	//
32	// Cache file: cluster_cores.json in the cache dir (alongside nodes.json).
33	// Safe to delete by hand to force re-discovery.
34	type ClusterCoresCache map[string]*CoresEntry
35	
36	// CoresEntry is one cluster's cached core URLs plus when they were fetched.
37	// Freshness is fetched_at + ClusterCoresTTL, computed at read time so a TTL
38	// change re-interprets existing entries without a migration.
39	type CoresEntry struct {
40		CoreURLs  []string  `json:"core_urls"`
41		FetchedAt time.Time `json:"fetched_at"`
42	}
43	
44	// LoadClusterCores reads the cluster→cores cache. A missing or corrupt file
45	// yields an empty cache. Unlocked read; use ModifyClusterCores for a
46	// read-modify-write sequence.
47	func LoadClusterCores(cacheDir string) (ClusterCoresCache, error) {
48		return readClusterCoresNoLock(filepath.Join(cacheDir, clusterCoresFileName))
49	}
50	
51	// ModifyClusterCores atomically applies fn to the cluster→cores cache under a
52	// single exclusive flock.
53	func ModifyClusterCores(cacheDir string, fn func(ClusterCoresCache) error) error {
54		return modifyCacheFile(cacheDir, clusterCoresFileName, readClusterCoresNoLock, writeClusterCoresNoLock, fn)
55	}
56	
57	func readClusterCoresNoLock(path string) (ClusterCoresCache, error) {
58		cache := make(ClusterCoresCache)
59		err := loadCacheFile(path, &cache, func() ClusterCoresCache { return make(ClusterCoresCache) })
60		return cache, err
61	}
62	
63	func writeClusterCoresNoLock(path string, cache ClusterCoresCache) error {
64		return writeCacheFile(path, cache)
65	}
66	
67	// LoadAPICores / ModifyAPICores are the data-API siblings of
68	// LoadClusterCores / ModifyClusterCores: same ClusterCoresCache type and TTL,
69	// different cache file (api_discovery.json). A data API's advertised
70	// trusted_issuers ARE core URLs (the login servers whose JWTs it accepts), so
71	// the cluster cores cache fits verbatim — the audience the CLI exchanges for is
72	// the data host origin itself, derived at call time, never cached.
73	
74	// LoadAPICores reads the api-host→trusted-issuer-URLs cache. Unlocked read; use
75	// ModifyAPICores for a read-modify-write sequence.
76	func LoadAPICores(cacheDir string) (ClusterCoresCache, error) {
77		return readClusterCoresNoLock(filepath.Join(cacheDir, apiDiscoveryFileName))
78	}
79	
80	// ModifyAPICores atomically applies fn to the api-host→trusted-issuer-URLs
81	// cache under a single exclusive flock.
82	func ModifyAPICores(cacheDir string, fn func(ClusterCoresCache) error) error {
83		return modifyCacheFile(cacheDir, apiDiscoveryFileName, readClusterCoresNoLock, writeClusterCoresNoLock, fn)
84	}
85	
86	// Get returns a cluster's cached core URLs, whether the entry is still fresh,
87	// and whether it exists at all. A present-but-stale entry returns
88	// (urls, false, true) so callers can attempt a re-fetch yet fall back to the
89	// stale URLs if that fetch fails.
90	func (c ClusterCoresCache) Get(cluster string) (urls []string, fresh, ok bool) {
91		entry := c[cluster]
92		if entry == nil || len(entry.CoreURLs) == 0 {
93			return nil, false, false
94		}
95		return entry.CoreURLs, time.Now().Before(entry.FetchedAt.Add(ClusterCoresTTL)), true
96	}
97	
98	// Set records a cluster's core URLs, stamping the fetch time to now. The
99	// slice is copied so later mutation by the caller can't corrupt the cache.
100	func (c ClusterCoresCache) Set(cluster string, urls []string) {
101		c[cluster] = &CoresEntry{
102			CoreURLs:  append([]string(nil), urls...),
103			FetchedAt: time.Now(),
104		}
105	}

content.text:
This is a major finding. The codebase **already has a proven, server-driven cross-jurisdiction mechanism** (`crossJurisRoundTripper`) that the control-plane client uses: it reacts to a `421` redirect or a `401 {"error":"cross_juris_token_required","token_exchange_url":...,"audience":...}` hint and does the RFC 8693 exchange with the **server-supplied** audience — rather than hard-coding `https://{jurisdiction}.entire.io` and a `/api/v1/clusters` endpoint like the new fix does.

The new fix may be reinventing this with guessed endpoints/audiences that might not exist in prod. Let me verify the risky assumptions: does `/api/v1/clusters` (returning `apiUrl`) actually exist, and what token does the cell actually accept? Let me check the generated coreapi client and the OAS spec.

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/cli
echo "=== '/api/v1/clusters' or clusters-with-apiUrl anywhere in CLI? ==="
grep -rn "api/v1/clusters\|/clusters\b\|apiUrl\|ApiURL\|APIURL\|api_url" --include="*.go" internal cmd 2>/dev/null | grep -vi "_test.go" | grep -vi "cell_data_api" | head -30
echo
echo "=== coreapi generated: any 'cluster' operations / apiUrl fields? ==="
grep -rni "cluster" internal/coreapi/oas_client_gen.go 2>/dev/null | head -20
echo
echo "=== does coreapi list repos with jurisdiction? repo.go usage ==="
grep -n "func \|coreapi\.\|Cluster\|Jurisdiction\|apiUrl" cmd/entire/cli/repo.go 2>/dev/null | head -30
input.description: Search for /api/v1/clusters and apiUrl in CLI

content.text: `GET /clusters` (i.e. `/api/v1/clusters`) **does** exist as a generated `coreapi.ListClusters()` returning `apiUrl`, and `coreapi.Repo` already carries `ID` (ULID) + `ClusterHost`. So the new fix's hand-rolled `resolveCellAPIBaseURL` is **duplicating** proven generated client code — and, more importantly, it routes to the *user's* home jurisdiction rather than the *repo's* cluster, which would break for cross-jurisdiction repos. Let me confirm what bearer the control-plane client uses and read the ListClusters output shape.

34	// token for one that core accepts (see newCrossJurisHTTPClient).

125	}
126	
127	// CoreOrigin reports the control-plane core origin this client dials —
128	// scheme://host, the apiBasePath stripped. It is the single source of truth
129	// for "which core am I talking to": whether the client came from New (active
130	// context), NewForCluster (the cluster's core), or the ENTIRE_TOKEN bypass
131	// (the token's aud), the origin is whatever was actually wired in. Use it for
132	// user-facing "talking to <core>" output so the named core can never diverge
133	// from where requests go — re-deriving it from ResolveControlPlaneTarget would
134	// silently miss the ENTIRE_TOKEN and cluster cases.
135	func (c *Client) CoreOrigin() string {
136		return c.serverURL.Scheme + "://" + c.serverURL.Host
137	}
138	
139	// NewWithBearer returns a *Client targeting an explicit core origin with a
140	// fixed bearer token: the token is sent verbatim, not re-resolved or
141	// re-minted per request. Used when a command must hit a specific login
142	// server with a token already in hand: e.g. `entire auth status` querying
143	// /me on the active context's core with that context's session token. A
144	// cross-jurisdiction call still follows the home core's 421 and exchanges
145	// this token for that core's audience (see newCrossJurisHTTPClient).
146	func NewWithBearer(coreBaseURL, token string) (*Client, error) {
147		base := strings.TrimRight(coreBaseURL, "/")
148		client, err := NewClient(base+apiBasePath, staticBearer{token: token}, WithClient(newCrossJurisHTTPClient()))
149		if err != nil {
150			return nil, fmt.Errorf("build Entire API client: %w", err)
151		}
152		return client, nil
153	}
154	
155	// staticBearer is a SecuritySource that returns a fixed bearer token. Same
156	// sessionAuth-skipping rationale as providerSource.
157	type staticBearer struct{ token string }
158	
159	func (s staticBearer) BearerAuth(context.Context, OperationName) (BearerAuth, error) {
160		return BearerAuth{Token: s.token}, nil
161	}
162	
163	func (s staticBearer) SessionAuth(context.Context, OperationName) (SessionAuth, error) {
164		return SessionAuth{}, ogenerrors.ErrSkipClientSecurity
165	}
166	
167	// providerSource implements the generated SecuritySource, supplying the
168	// logged-in user's bearer token for every request from a token-provider
169	// func (auth.ControlPlaneTarget.TokenSource). The control plane only uses
170	// bearerAuth from the CLI; the sessionAuth (browser cookie) scheme is
171	// reported as ErrSkipClientSecurity so ogen's middleware satisfies the
172	// "bearerAuth OR sessionAuth" requirement via the bearer alone — without
173	// adding a stray `Cookie: entire_session=` header. (Returning an empty
174	// SessionAuth would not skip the cookie: the generated securitySessionAuth
175	// unconditionally calls req.AddCookie.)
176	type providerSource struct {
177		provide func(context.Context) (string, error)
178	}
179	
180	func (p *providerSource) BearerAuth(ctx context.Context, _ OperationName) (BearerAuth, error) {
181		token, err := p.provide(ctx)
182		if err != nil {
183			// The per-context provider returns a tailored message that already
184			// names the context, its login server, and the exact re-login command
185			// — surface it verbatim rather than burying it under a generic prefix;
186			// other failures (STS rejection, network) are likewise
187			// self-descriptive. A bare ErrNotLoggedIn (no tailored text) gets the
188			// standard login hint as a backstop.
189			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
190				return BearerAuth{}, fmt.Errorf("not logged in — run 'entire login': %w", err)
191			}
192			return BearerAuth{}, err
193		}
194		return BearerAuth{Token: token}, nil
195	}
196	
197	func (p *providerSource) SessionAuth(context.Context, OperationName) (SessionAuth, error) {
198		// The CLI authenticates with a bearer token, never the browser
199		// session cookie. ErrSkipClientSecurity tells ogen to drop this
200		// scheme entirely for the request (no Cookie header added); the
201		// bearerAuth path alone satisfies the OR-requirement.
202		return SessionAuth{}, ogenerrors.ErrSkipClientSecurity
203	}
204	
205	// APIError reports the title/detail/status of a control-plane RFC 7807
206	// problem response, or "" if err isn't a control-plane API error. Use it
207	// to render a clean message instead of ogen's wrapped decode string:
208	//
209	//	if _, err := client.CreateOrg(ctx, body); err != nil {
210	//	    if msg := coreapi.APIError(err); msg != "" {
211	//	        return cli.NewSilentError(errors.New(msg))
212	//	    }
213	//	    return err
214	//	}
215	func APIError(err error) string {
216		var statusErr *ErrorModelStatusCode
217		if !errors.As(err, &statusErr) {
218			return ""
219		}
220		m := statusErr.Response
221		switch {
222		case m.Detail.Set && m.Detail.Value != "":
223			return m.Detail.Value
224		case m.Title.Set && m.Title.Value != "":
225			return m.Title.Value
226		default:
227			return fmt.Sprintf("control-plane request failed with status %d", statusErr.StatusCode)
228		}
229	}
230

  name: 'audit-experts-cell-routing',
  description: 'Adversarial audit of the experts cell-routing 401 fix, seeded with cell/BFF ground truth',
  phases: [

    { title: 'Verify' },

}

const GROUND_TRUTH = `
FIX UNDER AUDIT (repo /Users/suhaan/devenv/cli, branch codex/experts-cell-routing, base main a3b80f273, commit 3047e8594):
- cmd/entire/cli/auth/cell_data_api.go  (NEW ~245 lines, the core of the fix)
- cmd/entire/cli/auth/cell_data_api_test.go (NEW tests)
- cmd/entire/cli/api_client.go  (adds NewAuthenticatedEntireAPICellClient)
- cmd/entire/cli/experts_cmd.go (newExpertsAPIClient now uses the cell client; note repo-ULID resolution via GET /api/v1/repos on the cell, then POST /api/v1/repos/{ulid}/experts)

GOAL: 'entire experts --repo owner/repo' must reach entire-api cell route POST /api/v1/repos/{ulid}/experts and succeed for a logged-in user.

GROUND TRUTH — the entire-api CELL (verified in /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-api/internal/auth/auth.go) requires an IDENTITY token that satisfies ALL of:
  - scope=openid
  - aud EXACTLY equal to the cell's ENTIRE_JURISDICTION_AUDIENCE = that cell's jurisdiction host (prod https://us.entire.io ; staging https://us.partial.to)
  - signature valid against Core JWKS; sub (account id) present; carries home_jurisdiction/handle/provider claims
  Then a SpiceDB repo.pull gate; if the repo is NOT homed in that cell -> HTTP 404 "repo not in this region (locate it via /me's jurisdiction)".

GROUND TRUTH — the BFF reference (verified in /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire.io, mintJurisdictionToken + repos-stream.ts):
  - Mints via RFC 8693 token-exchange: subject_token=loginJWT, subject_token_type=access_token, audience=<jurisdiction host built from ENTIRE_CORE/audience templates per jurisdiction>, scope=openid. (IDENTICAL shape to the CLI fix's exchangeJurisdictionToken — so the token MECHANISM is correct.)
  - The BFF mints ONE token PER TARGET jurisdiction and fans out to the cell that HOSTS THE REPO (per-jurisdiction), NOT just the caller's home jurisdiction.
  - The BFF does NOT proxy /api/v1/repos or /api/v1/repos/{id}/experts for bearer callers (a session-only requireAuth catches them -> 401). So the CLI dialing the cell DIRECTLY is the only viable path (the fix does this).

GROUND TRUTH — coreapi (control plane, /Users/suhaan/devenv/cli/internal/coreapi):
  - Has generated ListClusters() -> Cluster{ApiUrl, IsDefault, Jurisdiction, PublicUrl, Slug}; GetRepo(id)->Repo{ID, ClusterHost}. NO owner/repo->ULID resolver exists.

  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: {
      type: 'array',

        type: 'object',

          category: { type: 'string' },
          explanation: { type: 'string' },
          concrete_failing_input: { type: 'string' },
          suggested_fix: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['title', 'file', 'severity', 'category', 'explanation'],
        additionalProperties: false,
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['findings'],
  additionalProperties: false,
}

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    is_real: { type: 'boolean' },
    confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
    reasoning: { type: 'string' },
    corrected_severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'nit'] },
    recommended_action: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['is_real', 'confidence', 'reasoning', 'recommended_action'],
  additionalProperties: false,
}

const DIMENSIONS = [
  {
    key: 'correctness-routing',
    prompt: `Audit dimension: CORRECTNESS & CELL ROUTING.
Read the four fix files in full. Trace the exact end-to-end flow of 'entire experts --repo owner/repo' and 'entire experts --repo <ULID>' from experts_cmd.go through api_client.go into auth/cell_data_api.go.
Focus on: is the jurisdiction/cell resolution correct? Does the audience actually match what the cell validates? Does the code correctly handle: (a) data host = entire.io BFF, (b) data host already a direct cell URL, (c) local dev (ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1). Is resolveCellAPIBaseURL's cluster matching (jurisdiction + isDefault) right? Does the login JWT actually carry home_jurisdiction in production? Are the audience/core templates correct for prod AND staging (partial.to)?
Construct concrete failing inputs. Report only real defects.
${GROUND_TRUTH}`,
  },
  {
    key: 'security-token-handling',
    prompt: `Audit dimension: SECURITY of credential/token handling.
Read auth/cell_data_api.go and the exchange helpers it calls. Focus on: is the login JWT ever sent to an attacker-influenceable host? Are the core URL / audience derived from trusted inputs (signed-JWT claim + constant/env templates) vs untrusted server responses? Is resolveCellAPIBaseURL's use of the /api/v1/clusters apiUrl a value that the login JWT is then re-targeted at (SSRF/JWT-exfil risk)? Is HTTPS enforced except for loopback? Does insecureHTTP widen anything dangerously? Compare against the strict same-origin/federation gates the existing cross_juris_transport.go uses.
Construct concrete exploit scenarios. Report only real risks.
${GROUND_TRUTH}`,
  },
  {
    key: 'edge-errors',
    prompt: `Audit dimension: EDGE CASES, ERROR HANDLING, RESOURCE SAFETY.
Read auth/cell_data_api.go + experts_cmd.go. Focus on: empty/missing home_jurisdiction; malformed login JWT; /api/v1/clusters returns empty or no match; token exchange returns empty token; response bodies not closed; context/timeout propagation (note dctx uses dataAPIDiscoveryTimeout=8s while httpClient uses cellDataAPITimeout=30s — is the exchange/clusters call bounded correctly, and is the parent ctx honored?); nil map/slice; user-facing error clarity when the repo isn't in the reached cell (404). 
Construct concrete failing inputs. Report only real defects.
${GROUND_TRUTH}`,
  },
  {
    key: 'duplication-consistency',
    prompt: `Audit dimension: DUPLICATION & CONSISTENCY with existing proven machinery.
The repo has a dupl linter (threshold 75) and strong conventions. Focus on: resolveCellAPIBaseURL hand-rolls GET /api/v1/clusters + manual JSON parsing that DUPLICATES the generated coreapi.ListClusters() (Cluster{ApiUrl,IsDefault,Jurisdiction,PublicUrl,Slug}). Note the import cycle (auth cannot import coreapi). Assess: is the hand-rolled clusterListingRow parsing at risk of drifting from the OAS schema? Would the fix be more robust reusing coreapi from the cli package (api_client.go) instead of hand-rolling in auth? Also check: does it bypass the cross-juris transport that coreapi uses? Are naming/patterns consistent with data_api.go / refresh.go? 
Report concrete maintainability/correctness risks from the duplication.
${GROUND_TRUTH}`,
  },
]

phase('Find')
const results = await pipeline(
  DIMENSIONS,
  (d) => agent(d.prompt, { label: `find:${d.key}`, phase: 'Find', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA }),
  (review, d) => {
    const findings = (review && review.findings) || []
    if (findings.length === 0) return []
    return parallel(findings.map((f) => () =>
      agent(
        `Adversarially VERIFY this audit finding against the actual code. Read the cited file(s) yourself. Try hard to REFUTE it — is it actually a real defect that would occur in production, or a false positive / already-handled / out-of-scope? Judge severity honestly given that this is a hidden/labs command and that the token mechanism is already verified-correct.

FINDING (from dimension ${d.key}):
${JSON.stringify(f, null, 2)}

${GROUND_TRUTH}`,
        { label: `verify:${d.key}:${(f.file || '').split('/').pop()}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA },
      ).then((v) => ({ finding: f, verdict: v, dimension: d.key })),
    ))
  },
)

const all = results.flat().filter(Boolean)
const confirmed = all.filter((r) => r.verdict && r.verdict.is_real)
const rejected = all.filter((r) => r.verdict && !r.verdict.is_real)

log(`Confirmed ${confirmed.length} real findings; rejected ${rejected.length} false positives.`)

return {
  confirmed_count: confirmed.length,
  rejected_count: rejected.length,
  confirmed: confirmed.map((r) => ({
    dimension: r.dimension,
    severity: r.verdict.corrected_severity || r.finding.severity,
    title: r.finding.title,
    file: r.finding.file,
    lines: r.finding.lines,
    explanation: r.finding.explanation,
    concrete_failing_input: r.finding.concrete_failing_input,
    suggested_fix: r.finding.suggested_fix,
    verify_reasoning: r.verdict.reasoning,
    recommended_action: r.verdict.recommended_action,
  })),
  rejected: rejected.map((r) => ({ title: r.finding.title, why_rejected: r.verdict.reasoning })),
}

- ✅ **Dialing the cell directly is the only viable path** — I confirmed the entire.io BFF does *not* proxy `/api/v1/repos/*` for bearer callers (a session-only `requireAuth` catches it → the 401 you saw). So the fix's approach is architecturally right.
- ✅ Baseline **builds and its tests pass**.

**Two issues I've already flagged** (audit is verifying + hunting for more):
1. It routes to the **user's** home jurisdiction, not the **repo's** cluster — a repo homed in another region would 404. (Real, but hard to fix cleanly CLI-side since `coreapi` has no owner/repo→ULID resolver and can't be imported by `auth`; likely a clear-error + doc rather than a rearchitect.)
2. `resolveCellAPIBaseURL` **hand-rolls** `GET /api/v1/clusters` that already exists as the generated `coreapi.ListClusters()`.

Comprehensive audit: **15 confirmed, 5 false positives** (good — the workflow correctly rejected things like the "no timeout on refresh leg" and the self-flagged import-cycle non-issue). Deduping the confirmed findings into distinct root causes:

- **A. Cross-jurisdiction routing** (findings 1,5,7,8) — routes to the *user's* home cell, not the *repo's* cell. The audit notes the BFF resolves the repo's cell via **mirrors** (`resolve-cluster-host.ts` → `GET /api/v1/mirrors`), and the CLI already has `listMirrorsForRepo`.
- **B. Staging (partial.to) unsupported** (finding 2) — `isEntireIOBFF` + hard-coded `*.entire.io` templates.
- **C. Local dev broken** (finding 3) — token exchange always hits **prod** core, ignoring the discovered local core. This breaks the documented `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1` workflow.
- **D. Security hardening** (9,10,11) — no HTTPS guard before POSTing the login JWT; cell `apiUrl` trusted verbatim; unvalidated `home_jurisdiction` label into URL templates.
- **E. Misleading errors** (6,12) — cross-region shows "not onboarded/no access"; raw 404 "locate via /me".
- **F. Test gaps + nits** (4,13,14,15).

Before deciding whether to do the full per-repo routing rewrite (A) or a robust stopgap, let me check if the mirrors→cluster path is clean enough to route correctly.

The experts cell client had several defects surfaced by an adversarial audit
against the entire-api cell + entire.io BFF ground truth:

- Cross-jurisdiction routing: it dialed the CALLER's home cell (login JWT
  home_jurisdiction), so a repo homed in another region always failed with a
  misleading "not onboarded/no access" error. Now the cli layer resolves the
  repo's OWN cell + jurisdiction from the control plane (coreapi mirrors for
  owner/repo, GetRepo for a ULID; mapped to a cell apiUrl via ListClusters) and
  passes it as an explicit CellTarget — mirroring how the BFF mints one token
  per target jurisdiction and fans out to the repo's cell. Resolution is
  best-effort: any failure falls back to home-jurisdiction routing, so the
  common same-region path can never regress.

- Staging (partial.to) was unsupported: isEntireIOBFF only matched *.entire.io
  and the audience/core templates were hardcoded to prod. Cell-vs-BFF detection
  is now environment-agnostic (a direct cell is any host with ".api."), and the
  audience/core follow the environment family (entire.io vs partial.to) derived
  from the configured data host, with the discovered core as fallback.

- Local dev sent the exchange to PRODUCTION core (the prod template ignored the
  discovered local core). A loopback discovered core is now honored verbatim so
  the local login JWT is exchanged at the local core.

- Security: the login JWT / identity token targets (core + cell apiUrl) are now
  gated to https (loopback/--insecure-http-auth excepted), and home_jurisdiction
  is validated as a DNS label before templating into URLs.

- Clearer errors: a cross-region 404 ("repo not in this region") and the
  repo-not-found path now tell the user the repo may be homed in another region
  instead of implying it isn't onboarded / accessible.

Adds unit tests for per-repo cell resolution, cross-jurisdiction routing,
environment-family templates, loopback core, and jurisdiction-label validation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
Confirmed precisely. Here's the exact picture:

- `api.BaseURL()` defaults to **`https://entire.io`** (the BFF), and `NewEntireAPICellClient` runs **discovery against it** — `entire.io/.well-known/entire-api.json` (cached 24h) — *before* the target branch. So yes, **my fix still makes one BFF call: the discovery bootstrap.**
- **But the actual experts *data* path is already off the BFF** — it dials the cell (`*.api.entire.io`) directly; the token exchange goes to entire-**core** (`*.auth.entire.io`). The 401 happened precisely *because* the BFF was in the data path before; my fix removed it there.
- **`coreapi.New()` proves the BFF-free pattern exists**: it resolves everything from the **active context** (`ResolveControlPlaneTarget → activeContext`), never touching the BFF. My per-repo resolution already uses that (`coreapi` → mirrors/GetRepo/ListClusters, all entire-core).

So the leftover BFF touch is the *shared discovery bootstrap* that anchors `api.BaseURL()=entire.io` — inherited by all data-API commands (`activity`, `search` too), not experts-specific. Let me pull ENT-976 to align my recommendation with the tracked direction.

ENT-976 (Evis, Urgent, in progress) directly validates the approach and clarifies the boundary:

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

This is a technical PR walkthrough for two senior engineers making an architecture call — so: a polished, utilitarian **engineering memo** treatment, with the routing table and request-flow as the visual centerpieces, not a flashy hero.

**Design plan:**
- **Color** — cool slate, not the AI-cream cliché. Ground `#F3F5F7` (cool off-white), ink `#16212B` (slate-black), muted `#5A6B78`, accent deep petrol-teal `#0E6E73` (infra/routing), semantic `#2E7D57` good / `#B0463B` bad / `#B07A1E` warn. Neutrals biased cool toward the teal.
- **Type** — restrained serif headings (`Georgia` stack) over a system-sans body, with **monospace carrying the technical tokens** (hosts, paths, CLI, JSON) — grounded in a CLI/infra subject. System stacks (CSP blocks font CDNs; no silent fallback risk).
- **Layout** — single reading column (~models a memo), with a vertical **request-flow** diagram and two data tables (routing tiers, live verification) as the anchors; the open architecture decision as a highlighted callout.

Every data command dials https://entire.io with the same bearer. Mint the identity token, dial the cell that hosts the repo

The experts data path no longer touches the BFF

Resolution and token exchange go to entire-core; the data calls go straight to the entire-api cell. The BFF is out of the data path — that's what removed the 401.

5 parallel readers mapped each phase against the ACTUAL repos (entire-sem, entire-brain, brain-bench, entiredb, cli incl. checkpoint/remote + strategy + mcp, entire-api, external-agents, and the private regente-core), then a synthesis + completeness pass. `entire-brain` is a **local, no-egress** Go plugin invoked as `entire brain`. - **New Go file:** `internal/cli/viz.go` — `newVizCommand`, `runViz`, the `http.ServeMux`, and JSON handlers. Mirrors dash.go being the single "touches the brain on disk" file (`assembleBrainSnapshot`, `dash.go:136`).

1. Resolve target exactly like dash: `repoDir, brainDir, branch, err := resolveFactsTarget(ctx, opts, target, flags.branch)` (`facts.go`, called at `dash.go:76`), then `status, err := buildBrainStatusReport(ctx, opts, target)` to obtain `status.Manifest` (`*exportManifest` with `.Sources.Semantic/.History/.Sessions`), same as `assembleBrainSnapshot` (`dash.go:139`).
2. Bind loopback only: `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:"+port)` — never `0.0.0.0`. Repo precedent for hard-coded loopback: `distill_cmd.go:1862` (`http://127.0.0.1:11434/...`).
3. `srv := &http.Server{Handler: vizMux(brainDir, repoDir, branch, status.Manifest, opts)}`; print `http://127.0.0.1:<actual-port>` to `cmd.OutOrStdout()`; optionally `open`/`xdg-open` unless `--no-open`; serve with `srv.Serve(ln)`; `srv.Shutdown` on `ctx.Done()`.

### No-egress compliance
- A loopback server with embedded assets and disk-only reads has no outbound sockets and never calls a model — inherently compliant. Do **not** gate it behind `brainNoEgressMode()` (`agent_policy.go:14`); that toggle blocks *outbound agent* egress (`agent_policy.go:52-59`), which viz doesn't have. # Plan: `entire brain viz` — a local, Apple/Obsidian-style visual interface for the brain

> Note: this plan file previously held the "Semantic Reasoning Layer roadmap." That content is a different task and is safely recoverable (workflow output `w4e29z5sf` + `scratchpad/roadmap_full.md` + our chat); I'll restore it to a separate doc after we exit plan mode.

## Context
`entire-brain` builds a rich per-repo "brain" (semantic code graph, durable facts, history, docs, patterns) but it's only explorable via the CLI and a terminal TUI (`entire brain dash`). There is **no visual way to navigate the brain**. This adds a state-of-the-art, **local, no-egress** web interface — `entire brain viz` — that renders the brain as an explorable force-directed graph with search, a node inspector, and a ⌘K palette, styled exactly to the Entire dark theme. Outcome: any dev runs `entire brain viz` and visually navigates their repo's brain in the browser, fully offline, in one static Go binary.

## Locked decisions
- **Integrated, real, phased** — a real `entire brain viz` command over LIVE brain data (not a throwaway prototype). Phase 1 is a real, demoable slice.
- **Graph hero = the code graph** (entities + `CALLS`/`IMPORTS`), grounded in `semantic.sqlite` (the strongest, real-edge data). Facts/history/sessions appear *on* a node in the inspector. The **mixed "memory web"** (facts/sessions/docs as first-class nodes) is a **Phase 2 toggle**, because fact↔symbol links are name/locus-approximate.
- **Self-contained, no JS toolchain** — hand-authored vendored SPA embedded via `go:embed`; the repo's pure-Go build is preserved.

## Architecture
- **Command:** `entire brain viz [path]` in the **`explore`** group. Register in `internal/cli/root.go` right after the dashboard (`addGrouped("explore", newDashCommand(opts))`, ~root.go:112) with `addGrouped("explore", newVizCommand(opts))`. Groups + `addGrouped` verified at root.go:67-73.
- **New file `internal/cli/viz.go`:** `newVizCommand` (copy the shape of `newDashCommand`, dash.go:37; `Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)`), `runViz`, an `http.ServeMux`, and the JSON handlers. Flags: `--port` (default `0` = auto free port), `--branch`, `--no-open`, `--limit` (default ~4000). This is the single "touches the brain on disk" file, like dash.go.
- **`runViz` startup:** resolve target exactly like dash — `resolveFactsTarget(ctx, opts, target, flags.branch)` then `buildBrainStatusReport` for `status.Manifest` (`assembleBrainSnapshot`, dash.go:136/139). Bind **loopback only**: `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:"+port)` (never `0.0.0.0`; hard-loopback precedent at distill_cmd.go:1862). Print `http://127.0.0.1:<actual-port>` to `cmd.OutOrStdout()`; `open`/`xdg-open` unless `--no-open` (never fail the command on open error); `srv.Serve(ln)`; `srv.Shutdown` on `ctx.Done()`.
- **Embed (module-root `webui.go`, package `entirebrain`):** `//go:embed webui/dist` → `var WebUI embed.FS`, mirroring `templates.go` + `embedmodel.go` (go:embed cannot reference parent dirs — verified note in both). Serve via `http.FileServer(http.FS(fs.Sub(entirebrain.WebUI, "webui/dist")))`, with `/api/*` routed to JSON handlers first.
- **No-egress compliance:** loopback + embedded assets + disk-only reads = inherently compliant. Do **not** gate behind `brainNoEgressMode()` (agent_policy.go:14 — that toggle is for *outbound agent* egress, which viz has none). Emit a CSP header on the HTML as machine-checkable proof: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'`.

## Data / endpoints (all GET, read-only; each wraps a verified existing func)
| Endpoint | Returns | Wraps |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/summary` | repo, branch, freshness, counts, warnings | `buildBrainStatusReport` + `dashHomeView` (dash.go:139/188) |
| `/api/graph?limit=N` | `{nodes,edges}` base graph | nodes `loadSemanticSymbols` (dash.go:415, `RecordType=="symbol"`); edges `findSemanticRelationsByTypesSQLite` (semantic.go:3743) or `findSemanticRelationsForSymbolsInSQLite` (3706); snapshot fallback 4225/4269 when `StorePath==""` |
| `/api/node?id&limit` | `{symbol,neighbors,relations,snippet,facts,history}` | `semanticContextFacts` (semantic.go:2986); snippet `semanticRecord.Blob`/`loadSemanticSymbolsByIDsSQLite` (3851); facts `loadFacts` (facts.go:208) filtered by Locus/name; history `loadBrainHistoryIndex` (history.go:1579) filtered |
| `/api/impact?id&depth&limit` | transitive subgraph | `semanticImpactFacts` (semantic.go:3152) |
| `/api/search?q&limit` | unified hits (facts+history+docs+symbols) for search / ⌘K | `retrieveUnified` (dash.go:100 `brainSearchFunc`) + `searchResultFromUnified` (dash.go:117) |
| `/api/facts`, `/api/history`, `/api/patterns` | lists (Phase 2/4) | `loadFacts`, `loadBrainHistoryIndex`, `loadCorpusPatternViews`/`runPatternsList` |

- **Node JSON** (`semanticRecord`, semantic.go:219): `{id, kind, name, qualified_name, file_path, start_line, end_line, signature, language, container_id}`.
- **Edge JSON:** `{from_id, to_id, type, confidence, resolution, relation_scope, target_kind}`.
- **Unbuilt brain:** loaders return `(nil,nil)`; handlers emit `{nodes:[],edges:[]}` + `warnings`, never 500.

## Frontend (vendored, hand-authored, zero build)
```
webui/dist/  index.html · app.js (router+fetch+wiring) · graph.js (Canvas2D force sim) · style.css (tokens+layout) · fonts/
```

- **Interactions:** wheel/pinch zoom + drag pan w/ inertia, `0`=fit; click→focus+inspector; dbl-click/Expand→merge `/api/node` neighbors into the sim; Impact→`/api/impact` overlay; hover→highlight incident edges, dim rest; drag→pin (ring); keys `/` `⌘K` `Esc` `Tab`/arrows `f` (open file, best-effort). Empty/loading/unbuilt("run `entire brain refresh`")/truncated states.

## Visual design (exact tokens — from `entire.io/frontend/src/index.css` `.dark`)
- Surfaces `--surface-sunken:#111 / base:#161616 / raised:#1c1c1c / floating:#222`; hover/active/selected = white overlays. Text `#f3f3f3 / #b9b9b9 / #707070`. Border `rgb(250 250 250/.10)` & `/.08`. **Accent `#f25333`** (Entire orange) = focus. Fonts `Entire Headline NEW` + `Entire Mono` (system-ui/mono fallback if not vendorable). Hand-write the four `webui/dist/` files (no npm/bundler/transpile); `go build` embeds them via `webui.go`; the mise flow stays pure-Go (preserves the single-static-binary property `embedmodel.go` prizes). **Gotcha:** `//go:embed webui/dist` fails on an empty dir — commit the Phase-1 files (or a placeholder) so it compiles. Fonts: vendor Entire woff2 under `webui/dist/fonts/` if licensing allows (same-origin); else the token block already falls back to system fonts. No CDN (CSP + no-egress forbid it).

## Phasing
- **P1 (real minimal slice):** `newVizCommand` + `runViz` + loopback server + embed; `/api/summary`, `/api/graph`, `/api/node`, `/api/search`; canvas graph + left rail (search+legend) + inspector (symbol/neighbors/snippet) + zoom/pan/hover/click + empty/loading + full dark theme.
- **P2 (mixed memory web):** fact/session/doc nodes as a toggle; facts+history in `/api/node`; inspector tabs (`loadFacts`, `loadBrainHistoryIndex`).
- **P3:** `/api/impact` "Show impact" overlay + camera framing + breadcrumbs.
- **P4:** `/api/patterns` pattern nodes + panel.
- **P5:** full ⌘K palette (search + actions) + edge-type/confidence/language filters + view state in URL hash.

## Verification
- **Build & run:** `go build ./...` (confirms embed compiles) → `entire brain refresh` (built brain) → `entire brain viz .` prints the URL → exercise graph render, hover highlight, click→inspector (neighbors+snippet), search filter, zoom/pan, empty state on an unbuilt repo.
- **No-egress proof:** `lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -p <pid>` shows `127.0.0.1` only; `curl -sv /` shows the CSP header; DevTools Network shows only same-origin (`/api/*` + assets); run under `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS=1` — identical behavior.
- **Regression:** `go test ./internal/cli/...` with `httptest` handler tests (repo already uses `httptest.NewServer`) asserting JSON shapes and that a missing brain yields `{nodes:[],edges:[]}` + warnings, not 500.

## Critical files
- `internal/cli/root.go` — register `newVizCommand` in `explore` (~line 112).
- `internal/cli/dash.go` — copy the factory + reuse loaders (`newDashCommand`:37, `assembleBrainSnapshot`:136, `loadSemanticSymbols`:415, `brainSearchFunc`:100).
- `internal/cli/semantic.go` — edge/neighbor/impact readers (`semanticContextFacts`:2986, `semanticImpactFacts`:3152, `findSemanticRelationsForSymbolsInSQLite`:3706, snapshot fallbacks 4225/4269).
- `templates.go` + `embedmodel.go` — the module-root `//go:embed` pattern to replicate in new `webui.go`.
- **NEW:** `internal/cli/viz.go`, `webui.go`, `webui/dist/{index.html,app.js,graph.js,style.css}`.

## Risks / open items
- **Edge source of truth:** prefer SQLite `relations` (semantic.go:3706) when `StorePath!=""`, snapshot fallback (4225) — mirror `semanticContextFacts`.
- **Scale:** large repos exceed a few thousand symbols → `--limit` + degree-based pruning (drop leaf externals first); pick a sane default.
- **Opaque compound IDs** (`{repo}:{lang}:{path}:{kind}:{name}`) — internal keys only; always display `qualified_name`.
- **Fuzzy fact↔symbol linking** (name/`Locus`) — start exact-name, refine later.
- **Font licensing** — vendor Entire woff2 or ship system fallback (decide before P1 polish).
- **Concurrent `refresh` mid-serve** — loaders tolerate missing files; v1 uses a manual "refresh" re-fetch button, not a file watcher.
- **Single-brain-per-server** (captures one brainDir at start, like dash); multi-repo switching is out of scope for v1.

## What it is
`entire brain viz` starts a **local, no-egress web interface** that renders the brain's semantic graph as an explorable, Apple/Obsidian-style force graph — dark theme matched exactly to `entire.io` (`.dark` tokens: `#161616` surfaces, `#f25333` accent, kind-colored nodes: cyan functions, indigo types, amber values).

Every brain feature now drills from the radial hub into a **force-directed graph** (no more lists), and every node carries a **real Entire link**:

Fixed. The "empty" was a real bug I'd introduced, plus a layout issue — both resolved now.

## What was actually wrong

1. **Blank for 3-4 seconds on load** — `boot()` waited for `/api/summary` before drawing anything, and that endpoint rebuilt the *entire* status report (~3-4s on the cli brain) on every call. → Now served straight from the in-memory manifest (**0.01s**), and the hub paints immediately regardless.

2. **The counts/search silently broke** — my first "fix" made `boot()` a synchronous IIFE at the top of the file. It called `showHub()` → `clearSearch()`, which touched a `const` declared later (temporal dead zone), threw, and **halted the whole module** — so `renderSummary` and every event listener never ran. → `boot()` now runs at the *end* of the module, after everything is initialized.

3. **"Too much blank"** — your window is narrow, and the fixed 280px rail crammed the hub into ~160px. → Responsive layout: the rail trims on medium screens and **stacks into a top bar on narrow/portrait** so the hub uses full width, with the inspector sliding in as an overlay.

## Verified (headless Chrome, at 440px and 1280px)
- Hub paints instantly; `cli · main` + all counts populate (rail + per-feature + core)
- Search works (50 hits for "session"); listeners attach
- Narrow: full-width constellation, inspector slides in as an overlay showing real session detail + "Open in Entire ↗"
- gofmt clean · vet clean · viz tests pass · no NUL bytes

func (s *vizServer) sourceLink(file string, line int) string {
	file = strings.TrimSpace(file)
	if file == "" || s.provider != "gh" {
		return ""
	}
	branch := s.branch
	if branch == "" {
		branch = "HEAD"
	}
	u := fmt.Sprintf("https://github.com/%s/%s/blob/%s/%s", s.owner, s.repo, branch, file)
	if line > 0 {

	}
	return u

# Make a clean PR

The commit history and PR should read like a careful engineer wrote them for the permanent record. Nothing personal, conversational, or AI-meta belongs in them.

## Never include
- **No Claude / AI session links or footers.** No `Claude-Session:` line, no `https://claude.ai/code/...`, no "Generated with Claude Code", no robot emoji footer, no "Co-Authored-By: Claude".
- **No references to people or conversations.** Never write "Thomas said this", "as X asked", "reply to him", "addressing Y's comment", "per Slack/Discord", "as discussed". The change is justified by what it does, not who mentioned it.
- **No weird meta.** No "I", "let me", "as an AI", no apologies, no narrating the process, no hedging.

## Commits
- Conventional and scoped: `type(scope): imperative summary` (e.g. `fix(auth): reject expired tokens`).
- One logical change per commit. Keep the diff tight, no unrelated formatting churn.
- Body only when it adds value: explain WHAT changed and WHY in plain technical terms.
- **The only way a person's name appears** is a real `Co-authored-by: Name <email>` trailer, used when you actually incorporated their code. That is factual attribution, never "X said in chat". Get a valid email (e.g. GitHub `id+login@users.noreply.github.com`) or skip the trailer.

## Before pushing
- Branch off the latest base. Never commit straight to a protected main.
- Run the repo's format + lint + tests. Confirm green on the committed tree before pushing.

## PR description: use this structure

Title is conventional style, same as the commit (`type(scope): summary`). For the body, fill the sections that apply and drop the ones that don't. Bullets over paragraphs throughout. A small change gets a few bullets, not a wall.

- **What** — one or two lines on what changed. Plain and concrete.
- **Why / how it helps** — the problem it solves and the impact (fixes a bug, unblocks X, cuts Y). The reviewer should get the motivation without asking. Tie it to the outcome, never to who requested it.
- **How** (non-trivial changes) — the approach plus any key decision or tradeoff, and what a reviewer should look at closely.
- **Testing / verification** — exactly what you ran and the result. Be specific:
  - the commands (build, lint, the test suite) and that they passed
  - which cases you covered, including edge cases and the bug's repro
  - any manual checks (what you ran/clicked and what you saw)
  - confirm green on the COMMITTED tree, not an unsaved buffer (`git show HEAD` if unsure)
- **Risk / rollback** (risky changes only) — blast radius and how to revert.
- **Anything else that helps the reviewer:**
  - related issues/PRs, linked by number
  - breaking changes or migration steps, called out clearly
  - screenshots or before/after for UI changes
  - follow-ups intentionally left out of scope

input.content:
**What**
- Adds `entire brain viz [path]` (in the `explore` group): a local, loopback-only, no-egress web interface that renders the brain as an explorable, force-directed graph. The semantic code graph, facts, sessions, history, and docs each render as their own graph, with search, a ⌘K palette, a node inspector, a node-count slider, and session replay.
- Self-contained: a hand-authored, zero-build SPA embedded via `go:embed` — no CDN, no JS toolchain — so the pure-Go single-binary build is preserved.

**Why / how it helps**
- The brain was only explorable via the CLI and the terminal dashboard. This adds a visual way to navigate a repo's brain in the browser, fully offline.

**How**
- New `internal/cli/viz.go`: a cobra command + `http.ServeMux` + read-only JSON handlers, each wrapping an existing brain loader. Binds `127.0.0.1` only; a CSP header (`default-src 'self'` …) makes the no-egress guarantee machine-checkable.
- New module-root `webui.go` embeds `webui/dist` (mirrors `templates.go`/`embedmodel.go`). Frontend: `graph.js` (Canvas2D Barnes-Hut force sim + renderer), `app.js` (router/fetch/wiring), `index.html`, `style.css`.
- One-line command registration in `root.go`.
- Scale: the node-count slider reaches each feature's true total, bounded by a 300k safety ceiling; the semantic edge budget scales with node count (~4/node, capped at 90k). The relations query is chunked so a large graph can't exceed SQLite's bound-variable limit.

**Testing / verification**
- `go build ./...`, `gofmt -l`, and `go vet ./internal/cli/` clean.
- `go test ./internal/cli/` — full package green, including the new tests. Confirmed on the committed tree (`git show HEAD`).
- New tests: chunked relations query at 20k symbols (the old single query bound 40001 params and errored with "too many SQL variables"); all six feature endpoints degrade to 200 + valid JSON on an unbuilt brain; loopback-only bind asserts `127.0.0.1`; CSP/nosniff applied through the real mux; a huge `?limit` clamps without panic; node/edge JSON field mappings.
- Manual: rendered the semantic graph at full scale (11,211 nodes / 44,844 edges) and full history (172,432 nodes) with no collapse or tab crash; exercised session replay, search, and the empty/unbuilt-brain states.
- An adversarial audit (7 dimensions, each finding independently verified) surfaced 8 issues; all are fixed in this branch: SQLite IN-clause variable-limit → chunked; `?limit=0` history ceiling bypass → clamped; search/palette stale-response race → sequence guard; plus the test-coverage gaps above.

**No-egress**
- Loopback bind, embedded assets, disk-only reads, and a CSP enforced on every response. No outbound network of any kind.

**Risk / rollback**
- Additive: a new command (~2.6k lines) and a one-line `root.go` change. The single shared change is chunking `findSemanticRelationsForSymbolsInSQLite` — behavior is identical for small symbol sets (one batch) and correct for large sets where it previously errored; the full package suite is green. Rollback: drop the branch.

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'reasoning-layer-plan-buildout',
  description: 'Build the Semantic Reasoning Layer roadmap into a fully executable plan, one project per agent',
  phases: [
    { title: 'BuildOut', detail: 'P0–P4 each expanded into a full plan section with DoD, effort, deps, critical path' },
  ],
}

const ROADMAP = args.roadmap
const REPOS = args.repos // map name -> path
const repoList = Object.entries(REPOS).map(([k, v]) => `  - ${k}: ${v}`).join('\n')

const CTX = `You are building out ONE project of the "Semantic Reasoning Layer" initiative into a fully executable plan section.
The evidence-grounded roadmap skeleton is at ${ROADMAP} — READ IT FIRST and locate your assigned project (P0/P1/P2/P3/P4).
The initiative's spine: GA the local brain -> make it SHARED/hosted -> unify memory -> coordinate parallel agents -> federate cross-repo/org.
Status legend already used: [exists] verified/shipped · [partial] design/half exists · [todo] to build.

Local repos you may read to sharpen/verify evidence, effort, and dependencies (do NOT clone anything new; if a repo is "referenced-not-verified" keep it flagged as such):
${repoList}

YOUR JOB: turn your project's milestones + issues into a fully built-out, executable plan section. For your project produce clean markdown with:
- A tightened "What exists vs to-build" paragraph (keep it honest and evidence-anchored).
- For EACH milestone: a **Definition of Done** (2–4 concrete, checkable acceptance criteria), then its issues as a table/list where each issue has: status tag [exists|partial|todo], a one-line evidence-or-scope note (keep the leverage repo/file pointer), an effort size (S ≤2d / M ~1wk / L multi-wk), and explicit dependencies (intra-project "after M1.2" and cross-project "needs P1.M1"). Preserve every issue already in the roadmap; you may split or sharpen but do not drop scope or invent new scope beyond what the evidence supports.
- The project's **critical path** (the ordered chain of must-finish-first issues).
- **Open decisions / ADRs** this project forces (name the decision, the options, and who/what it blocks).
- Keep honest posture: things that are "referenced-not-verified" or "no_release_claim" stay explicitly caveated, never asserted as done.

Ground every claim in the roadmap text or a repo you actually read. Be concrete and executable — a competent engineer should be able to pick up any milestone and know what "done" means and what it depends on.`

// P3 carries a hard confidentiality constraint that must survive the build-out.
const P3_GUARD = `\n\nHARD CONSTRAINT FOR P3: a PRIVATE Node reference prototype informs this project's design. Its details are DESIGN SOURCE ONLY. Never surface it as an issue title, never phrase an issue as "port the private prototype", and keep any reference to it OFF anything that would become a company-visible issue title. In the plan, describe the capabilities to build in their own terms (entity claims/leases, semantic conflict detection, signed handovers, presence/messaging) and, if you must note provenance, do it once in a clearly-marked private aside — exactly as the roadmap does.`

const SECTION_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['project', 'section_markdown', 'milestone_count', 'issue_count', 'cross_project_deps', 'critical_path', 'open_decisions'],
  properties: {
    project: { type: 'string' },
    section_markdown: { type: 'string', description: 'the fully built-out plan section for this project, in markdown' },
    milestone_count: { type: 'integer' },
    issue_count: { type: 'integer' },
    cross_project_deps: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'e.g. "P1.M1 (hosted store) blocks P3.M1 (durable leases)"' },
    critical_path: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    open_decisions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const PROJECTS = [
  { key: 'P0', focus: 'GA entire-sem + entire-brain (the local brain): release hygiene, version stamping, schema freeze, brain-bench-as-CI-gate, honest claims, tagged main, distribution. Repos: entire-sem, entire-brain, brain-bench.' },
  { key: 'P1', focus: 'Shared/hosted brain: server-side brain store, sync protocol over checkpoint_remote+entiredb, multi-machine shared query, auth/tenancy. Repos: entire-brain, entiredb, entire-api, cli.' },
  { key: 'P2', focus: 'Unified pluggable memory (one MCP surface): converge code-search to one engine, converge knowledge backbone, one MCP aggregator, write/remember + resources, retire duplicates. Repos: cli, entire-brain, entire-sem (+ peregrine/pgr/symq/librarian/entire-search referenced-not-verified).' },
  { key: 'P3', focus: 'Semantic collision-free parallel agents: entity claims/leases, pre-merge semantic conflict detection, signed handovers + MCP auto-hydration, scheduler->sandboxes, presence + read-receipts. Repos: entire-brain, cli, entire-api, entiredb (+ ferrata/entire-sandbox, agent-planner referenced-not-verified). Depends on P1 + P2.' },
  { key: 'P4', focus: 'Cross-repo/cross-org federated reasoning: federated semantic index + query, agent capability registry, cross-org SpiceDB authz. Repos: entiredb, entire-api, entire-sem, external-agents, cli. Depends on P1 + P2.' },
]

phase('BuildOut')
const sections = await parallel(PROJECTS.map((p) => () =>
  agent(`${CTX}${p.key === 'P3' ? P3_GUARD : ''}\n\nBUILD OUT PROJECT ${p.key}: ${p.focus}`,
    { label: `buildout:${p.key}`, phase: 'BuildOut', effort: 'high', schema: SECTION_SCHEMA })
))

const ok = sections.filter(Boolean)
ok.sort((a, b) => a.project.localeCompare(b.project))
log(`Built out ${ok.length}/5 projects; ${ok.reduce((n, s) => n + (s.issue_count || 0), 0)} issues detailed.`)
return {
  sections: ok,
  totals: {
    projects: ok.length,
    milestones: ok.reduce((n, s) => n + (s.milestone_count || 0), 0),
    issues: ok.reduce((n, s) => n + (s.issue_count || 0), 0),
  },
  cross_project_deps: ok.flatMap((s) => (s.cross_project_deps || []).map((d) => `${s.project}: ${d}`)),
  critical_paths: Object.fromEntries(ok.map((s) => [s.project, s.critical_path || []])),
  open_decisions: Object.fromEntries(ok.map((s) => [s.project, s.open_decisions || []])),
}

            elif c=='"': instr=False
            continue
        if c=='"': instr=True
        elif c=='{': depth+=1
        elif c=='}':
            depth-=1
            if depth==0: return json.loads(s[st:k+1])
    return None

### Milestone M2 — Prompt-quality classifier (the direct customer ask)

**Definition of Done**
1. A `brain prompts score`-style verb classifies each user prompt into a quality signal (good/mixed/poor) with a **reason** (e.g. "under-specified, no acceptance criteria", "led to a revert", "one-shot success"), computed from the M1 outcome record + prompt features — not just the raw reinforcement label.

### Milestone M3 — Agent-task-fit & person-task-fit model

**Definition of Done**

2. Fit is scored **per task signature** (`intentSignature`) so it is task-relative, not a global "best coworker" ranking, and every fit score carries a support count + confidence (thin data → low confidence, never a spurious ranking).
