79	`entire-sem` and `entire-brain` were cloned side by side with the names shown
80	above. See [Operations](operations.md) for `entire-brain` build details and
81	`../entire-sem/docs/operations.md` for `entire-sem` release/cgo details.
82	
83	### 3. Build The Deterministic Brain
84	
85	Run the first refresh in the Entire-enabled repository you want agents to work
86	in:
87	
88	```sh
89	cd /path/to/your/repo
90	
91	entire brain refresh --agent none
92	entire brain status
93	```
94	
95	The semantic refresh refuses a dirty worktree by default. Run it on a clean
96	checkout, or use the advanced `entire brain refresh index --worktree` path only
97	when you intentionally want the current uncommitted state indexed. Worktree-
98	backed semantic indexes are rejected by bundle export.
99	
100	`--agent none` keeps the first build deterministic and token-free, with no
101	hosted-model calls. Refresh exports captured sessions, builds the local
102	history/doc indexes, asks `entire-sem` for a semantic snapshot, and stores the
103	derived brain under Entire's local plugin data directory.
104	
105	At this point the brain can answer from captured history, docs, semantic code
106	structure, runtime traces, patterns, and any existing durable facts. It has not
107	yet extracted new durable facts from retained sessions.
108	
109	### 4. Distill Durable Facts
110	
111	Distillation is the egress-gated agent step that turns captured sessions into
112	durable project knowledge: decisions, constraints, preferences, gotchas,
113	conventions, and invariants. If your goal is a full brain with newly extracted
114	durable facts, this is the next step after deterministic refresh:
115	
116	```sh
117	entire brain distill --agent codex --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low
118	```
119	
120	To estimate cost before spending agent calls, run a dry run first:
121	
122	```sh
123	entire brain distill --dry-run --json
124	```
125	
126	To inspect the resulting facts:
127	
128	```sh
129	entire brain facts status --json
130	entire brain facts tree --depth 1
131	```
132	
133	Distillation sends redacted transcript chunks to the selected agent unless you
134	use a local loopback agent such as Ollama. It is incremental and cached:
135	unchanged sessions are skipped, near-duplicate facts are reconciled against the
136	branch's existing facts, and low-confidence merge/supersede decisions are
137	queued for `entire brain facts review`.
138	
139	For active repos, keep the brain current with the watcher:
140	
141	```sh
142	entire brain watch
143	```
144	
145	The default watcher performs deterministic refreshes only. Token-spending work,
146	such as fact distillation or seed synthesis, is opt-in and separately gated.
147	
148	To keep the durable-facts layer fresh as new sessions land, enable distillation
149	explicitly:
150	
151	```sh
152	entire brain watch --distill --distill-every 24h --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low --budget 1
153	```
154	
155	If you also want generated seed summaries, run refresh with an agent instead of
156	the deterministic seed path:
157	
158	```sh
159	entire brain refresh --agent auto --seed-model gpt-5.4-mini --seed-effort low
160	```
161	
162	Seed synthesis is separate from fact distillation: seed files orient an agent on
163	the repository, while durable facts are branch-scoped retained knowledge.
164	
165	## How Agents Use The Brain
166	
167	Agents rely on a capture layer plus four consumption surfaces. The capture
168	layer produces the raw material; the consumption surfaces are how an agent
169	actually queries or receives brain context. Which surface matters depends on the
170	agent client and how the repository is configured.
171	
172	### Capture Layer: Entire Hooks Produce The Raw Material
173	
174	`entire-cli` installs lifecycle hooks for agents such as Claude Code, Codex,
175	Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, and Pi. Those
176	hooks start and stop sessions, capture prompts and transcripts, track changed
177	files, record subagent work where the agent exposes it, and attach checkpoint
178	metadata to commits.
179	
180	This capture path is background infrastructure. The coding agent does not need
181	to remember to save a transcript, and the human does not need to paste context
182	into the brain. `entire-brain refresh` later ingests the retained sessions and
183	checkpoint history that the hooks produced.
184	
185	If an agent is not seeing Entire context at all, first check the base Entire
186	integration, not the brain:
187	
188	```sh
189	entire status
190	entire agent
191	```
192	
193	### 1. MCP Is The Preferred Agent Tool Surface
194	
195	For agents that support MCP, register `entire brain mcp` as a local stdio MCP
196	server. The server opens no network listener and wraps the local brain's JSON
197	contracts as tools.
198	
199	Once MCP is available, an agent should call MCP tools instead of shelling out to
200	the `entire brain` CLI. The normal first call is `brain_brief` for the task.
201	Then the agent should make only targeted follow-up calls:
202	
203	- `brain_brief` for task-shaped context, history hits, likely files, and tests
204	- `brain_status` to check freshness, coverage, and blind spots
205	- retrieval tools such as `brain_query` and `brain_get` for facts, docs, and
206	  history
207	- semantic tools such as `brain_code`, `brain_context`, `brain_impact`, and
208	  `brain_tests` for code navigation and validation planning
209	- review, workspace, and pattern tools such as `brain_regressions`,
210	  `brain_workspace_graph`, `brain_workspace_review`, and `brain_patterns` when
211	  the task calls for them
212	
213	Some MCP tools write local state. For example, `brain_ingest_traces` persists
214	runtime edges as `RUNTIME_TRACE` facts. Pattern MCP tools are read-only; skill
215	formation remains a CLI-only write path.
216	
217	The benchmark harness treats this as the cleanest agent contract: MCP-backed
218	agents call named `brain_*` tools, and in MCP conditions they are explicitly
219	kept away from direct `entire brain` shell commands or prewritten history
220	excerpt files. See [Semantic MCP Guide](semantic_mcp_guide.md) for the full tool
221	surface.
222	
223	The MCP and CLI surfaces are intentionally close, but they are not perfect
224	mirrors. Some CLI-only flows, such as `recall --expand`, have no dedicated MCP
225	tool. Some MCP tools, such as `brain_review`, wrap machine contracts that are
226	hidden or discouraged as direct human CLI verbs. Prefer the native surface your
227	agent client has, then translate only when needed.
228	
229	### 2. Intake Instructions Are The File-Based Fallback
230	
231	When MCP is not available, an agent can still use the brain through the intake
232	instructions in `templates/`. The Codex and Claude templates tell the agent to
233	locate the brain with:
234	
235	```sh
236	entire brain path "$PWD"
237	```
238	
239	Then the agent reads staged context instead of blindly opening everything:
240	
241	- `README.md` and `manifest.json` in the brain directory
242	- seed files such as `seed/agent/quick-overview.md`,
243	  `seed/agent/overview.md`, `seed/agent/architecture.md`,
244	  `seed/agent/risks.md`, `seed/agent/maintenance-guide.md`, and
245	  `seed/agent/open-questions.md`
246	- `seed/history-gaps.md`, when present
247	- only task-relevant transcripts or records selected from the manifest
248	
249	This is how an agent like Codex can use `entire-brain` without a dedicated MCP
250	connection: resolve the local brain, read the manifest and seed context, inspect
251	only the relevant retained history, and treat gaps as uncertainty rather than
252	inventing rationale.
253	
254	### 3. Direct CLI Is A Compatibility Surface
255	
256	For agent clients without MCP, direct `entire brain ... --json` calls are the
257	compatibility surface. Humans and scripts can use the same commands. Agents
258	using this surface should treat it like a tool API, not as an invitation to run
259	a long command tour.
260	
261	A disciplined direct-CLI intake is:
262	
263	```sh
264	entire brain status --json
265	entire brain brief "<task>" --json
266	```
267	
268	Then ask the smallest next question. Examples:
269	
270	```sh
271	entire brain query "<decision or prior-work question>" --json
272	entire brain inspect code "<symbol or concept>" --json
273	entire brain inspect context "<symbol-or-id>" --json
274	entire brain inspect tests "<symbol-or-id>" --json
275	entire brain inspect regressions "<task or invariant>" --location-only --json
276	```
277	
278	Agents should prefer `query` for broad facts/history/docs, `search` for exact
279	terms, semantic `inspect` subcommands for code graph questions, and `get` or
280	`multi-get` when a prior result returned an id. They should not broaden into
281	repo-wide text search until the brain's targeted context has been used.
282	
283	### 4. Hidden Hooks Deliver Context At The Moment Of Relevance
284	
285	`entire-brain` also has a hidden hook surface for harness integrations. These
286	hooks are not installed by the base Entire repository enablement flow; a harness
287	must be configured to invoke them, for example from Claude Code
288	`PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` hooks or Entire CLI lifecycle hooks. Until then they
289	have no effect. They are not intended as human-facing commands, although they
290	can be hand-tested when
291	debugging harness wiring. They are designed to surface a small, high-confidence
292	fact exactly when it matters:
293	
294	- before editing a file, facts anchored to that file
295	- after a failed command, gotchas and known dead ends that match the failure
296	- after a session ends, optional one-session refresh and distillation
297	
298	The contract is intentionally quiet: if there is no relevant fact, no local
299	brain, or an environment problem, the hook exits successfully with no output on
300	stdout. Diagnostic one-liners may still go to stderr. That keeps hooks from
301	breaking the agent workflow or flooding the transcript. Session-end distillation
302	is still an explicit token-spending path: it skips when no agent is available
303	and must respect no-egress/local-only policy.
304	
305	## Usage Scenarios
306	
307	The examples below name the preferred MCP tool when there is one. Agent clients
308	without MCP should use the equivalent `entire brain ... --json` command from
309	the direct-CLI surface above.
310	
311	### Orient An Agent On A New Task
312	
313	The agent should start by asking for task-shaped context, not a generic project
314	summary. The normal tool is `brain_brief`. The useful output is the freshness
315	state, likely files and symbols, relevant history records, durable facts, likely
316	tests, and any blind spots.
317	
318	The agent should use the brief before broad shell search or file reads. If the
319	brief points to likely files, inspect those first. If freshness is degraded, the
320	agent should say so and either refresh the brain or lower confidence in semantic
321	answers.
322	
323	For repo-level orientation rather than task-specific orientation, use
324	`overview`. It returns a compact project map: stack signals, entrypoints,
325	commands, key documents, and recent decisions.
326	
327	```sh
328	entire brain overview --json
329	```
330	
331	### Keep The Brain Fresh
332	
333	Freshness is part of every answer. A stale semantic index, missing provider,
334	dirty-worktree mismatch, or parser blind spot changes how much an agent should
335	trust the brain.
336	
337	Agents should check freshness through `brain_status` or `status --json` before
338	relying on semantic answers. If freshness is unsafe, an agent with write
339	permission can request a refresh; otherwise it should report the limitation and
340	fall back to direct repository inspection.
341	
342	Humans or automation should keep the brain fresh:
343	
344	```sh
345	entire brain status
346	entire brain refresh --agent none
347	entire brain watch
348	```
349	
350	When semantic artifacts are out of sync or damaged, use the semantic
351	maintenance paths instead of deleting the whole brain:
352	
353	```sh
354	entire brain refresh index
355	entire brain repair
356	entire brain reset --semantic-only --force
357	```
358	
359	Use `refresh index --worktree` only when you intentionally want uncommitted
360	state in the semantic index. Exported bundles reject worktree-backed semantic
361	indexes.
362	
363	### Continue Or Explain Prior Work
364	
365	When the question is "why is this like this?", "what did the previous agent
366	try?", or "where did this session leave off?", the agent should search the
367	history and facts layers. The normal tools are `brain_query` or `brain_search`,
368	followed by `brain_get` for specific ids.
369	
370	This is the main reason Entire capture matters: the original prompt, attempts,
371	validation, correction, and rationale can survive the code diff and become
372	available to the next agent.
373	
374	### Ask Across Facts, History, And Docs
375	
376	When the question is not tied to one symbol, use the unified retrieval layer.
377	`query` is the normal hybrid path over durable facts, indexed history, and docs.
378	Use `search` for exact keywords, `vsearch` for semantic matches, and
379	`get`/`multi-get` when a result returns an id worth reading in full.
380	
381	```sh
382	entire brain query "how does checkpointing work" --json
383	entire brain search "checkpoint" --json
384	entire brain vsearch "preventing data races" --json
385	entire brain get fact:<id> --json
386	```
387	
388	For durable facts specifically, use `recall`. `recall --expand` is an
389	agent-assisted query expansion path, so it belongs behind the same egress
390	judgment as other agent calls.
391	
392	```sh
393	entire brain recall "account deletion" --k 5
394	entire brain recall "MirrorCommittedMetadataRef" --expand
395	```
396	
397	### Navigate Code By Meaning
398	
399	When a task depends on structure rather than text, the agent should use semantic
400	tools. The normal path is: find candidate symbols, inspect relation-aware
401	context, inspect likely impact, then ask for tests. The normal tools are
402	`brain_code` or `brain_search_code`, followed by `brain_context`,
403	`brain_impact`, and `brain_tests`.
404	
405	This is where `entire-sem` matters. It is not an agent memory layer; it is the
406	local parser/provider that gives `entire-brain` the graph the agent queries.
407	Semantic depth is language-dependent: parser-backed extraction covers the
408	semantic language set, while many recognized filetypes are inventory-only. For
409	inventory-only files, prefer text retrieval and lower confidence in
410	impact/context answers.
411	
412	For deeper graph work, use the graph specialists: schema inventory, local graph
413	UI, source snippets, directed trace paths, dead-code candidates, boundary
414	enumeration, and working-tree change mapping.
415	
416	```sh
417	entire brain inspect graph-schema --json
418	entire brain inspect graph-ui semantic-graph.html
419	entire brain inspect snippet "<symbol-or-id>" --json
420	entire brain inspect trace-path "<caller>" "<callee>" --json
421	entire brain inspect dead-code --json
422	entire brain inspect boundaries --kind tool --json
423	entire brain inspect changes --json
424	```
425	
426	### Review Risk Without A Clean Diff
427	
428	For long-running sessions, manual edits, or suspected regressions from memory,
429	the agent should use diff-less regression review. The normal tools are
430	`brain_regressions` or `brain_review`.
431	
432	When the goal is a fair investigation, prefer location-only output first. It
433	points the agent to suspected files and lines without handing it the expected
434	answer text.
435	
436	### Connect Runtime Evidence To Source
437	
438	When static structure is not enough, import runtime trace edges with
439	`brain_ingest_traces` or `inspect ingest-traces`. The brain compares the runtime
440	edges with known static relations, persists them as `RUNTIME_TRACE` graph facts,
441	and makes them available to graph schema, trace-path, and brief/context flows.
442	
443	This is useful for incidents and performance/debugging tasks where "what
444	actually happened?" matters more than "what could call this?"
445	
446	### Work Across Multiple Repositories
447	
448	Use workspaces when the behavior crosses repository boundaries: a frontend calls
449	an API, a service emits an event another service consumes, one repo imports a
450	package from another, or deployment/config resources connect separate projects.
451	
452	Humans create and refresh the workspace. Agents consume workspace context
453	through MCP workspace tools where available, or through direct workspace CLI
454	commands when MCP does not expose the required traversal. The workspace brain
455	keeps member repos local and builds cross-repo contracts and graph edges from
456	their existing local brains.
457	
458	```sh
459	entire brain workspace create platform
460	entire brain workspace add platform ../api --name api
461	entire brain workspace add platform ../web --name web
462	entire brain workspace refresh platform --full
463	```
464	
465	After the workspace exists, use workspace context, graph, impact, retrieval,
466	and review flows when the question crosses repos:
467	
468	```sh
469	entire brain workspace inspect context platform "checkout" --json
470	entire brain workspace inspect impact platform "checkout" --json
471	entire brain workspace inspect graph platform --json
472	entire brain workspace query platform "checkout" --json
473	entire brain workspace review platform "checkout regression" --json
474	entire brain workspace watch platform --once
475	```
476	
477	### Preserve Durable Project Knowledge
478	
479	Durable facts are short, provenance-anchored statements about decisions,
480	constraints, preferences, pitfalls, and standing rules. Humans can write them
481	directly when they know the rule. Agents can distill candidate facts from
482	captured sessions when explicitly asked or when a session-end integration is
483	configured to do so.
484	
485	```sh
486	entire brain remember "Prefer table-driven tests for parser edge cases" --path preferences.tests
487	entire brain distill --dry-run --json
488	entire brain distill --agent codex --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low
489	entire brain facts tree --depth 1
490	```
491	
492	Distillation is the token-spending path. It is incremental and cached, but it
493	still sends redacted transcript chunks to the selected agent unless you choose a
494	local loopback agent such as Ollama or use dry-run/no-egress mode.
495	
496	Durable facts also have a lifecycle. Review queued merge/supersede proposals,
497	promote branch facts when they should carry forward, retract facts that are no
498	longer true, and garbage-collect stale retractions.
499	
500	```sh
501	entire brain facts review
502	entire brain facts promote --from <branch> --strategy keep-both
503	entire brain facts retract <fact-id>
504	entire brain facts gc --force
505	entire brain inspect blame <fact-id> --json
506	```
507	
508	### Extract Reusable Agent Skills
509	
510	Skill extraction is not "turn repeated commands into a checklist." The current
511	pipeline forms skills only from accepted deep dossiers: verified evidence that a
512	pattern is non-obvious and useful to future agents.
513	
514	There are several evidence paths:
515	
516	- recurring task patterns that pass deep verification
517	- verified themes that capture latent practices by meaning
518	- corrected or failed episodes grouped into lessons
519	- durable gotchas, conventions, and invariants grouped into capabilities
520	- workspace families where equivalent procedures differ across repos
521	
522	A human or explicitly authorized automation runs the egress-gated verification
523	and formation commands. The agent performs the verification and `SKILL.md`
524	synthesis under that explicit request. The verifier is cached. Refresh, watch,
525	brief, query, MCP reads, and workspace reads do not silently call it.
526	
527	```sh
528	entire brain patterns
529	entire brain patterns verify --deep
530	entire brain patterns verify --themes
531	entire brain patterns verify --lessons
532	entire brain patterns verify --conventions
533	entire brain patterns skills
534	entire brain patterns skills form <id>
535	entire brain patterns skills form <id> --yes
536	```
537	
538	`patterns skills` lists formable proposals, not raw pattern rows. `form <id>`
539	previews the evidence, generated `SKILL.md`, and destination paths without
540	writing. If no accepted deep dossier exists yet, `form` refuses and tells you to
541	run verification first; it never falls back to shallow evidence. `--yes` writes
542	the skill; existing files require `--force`.
543	
544	By default, generated skills target the cross-agent `standard` destination
545	(`.agents/skills/`). Use `--target claude-code|codex|factoryai-droid|all` only
546	when an agent-specific destination is needed.
547	
548	Workspaces mirror the same flow for cross-repo families:
549	
550	```sh
551	entire brain workspace patterns verify <workspace>
552	entire brain workspace patterns skills <workspace>
553	entire brain workspace patterns skills form <workspace> <id>
554	```
555	
556	Pattern inspection is useful even when you are not forming skills. Use it to see
557	recurring tasks, practices, risks, themes, verifier state, and whether accepted
558	skills are stale.
559	
560	```sh
561	entire brain patterns
562	entire brain patterns status
563	entire brain workspace patterns <workspace>
564	entire brain workspace patterns status <workspace>
565	```
566	
567	### Measure Brain Quality
568	
569	The brain includes evaluation harnesses for maintainers who need evidence that a
570	retriever or fact layer is actually helping. These are not required for everyday
571	use, but they are the right surface before claiming quality improvements.
572	
573	```sh
574	entire brain facts eval-gen > facts-tasks.json
575	entire brain facts eval --tasks facts-tasks.json --retriever facts --json > facts-eval.json
576	entire brain facts eval-compare --a <before.json> --b <after.json>
577	entire brain history-eval-gen > history-tasks.json
578	entire brain history-eval --tasks history-tasks.json --json
579	```
580	
581	For semantic performance and provider output, use the semantic benchmark and
582	status audit instead of relying on anecdotes:
583	
584	```sh
585	entire brain bench semantic .
586	entire brain status --json
587	```
588	
589	### Tune Retrieval
590	
591	The default vector arm uses the bundled local Model2Vec embedder. For higher
592	semantic recall, opt into a local transformer embedder served by Ollama or a
593	compatible loopback endpoint:
594	
595	```sh
596	ollama pull embeddinggemma
597	ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBEDDER=ollama entire brain query "preventing data races" --json
598	```
599	
600	Keep this distinction clear: changing the embedder changes retrieval behavior,
601	not the underlying source of truth. Facts, history, docs, and semantic records
602	still come from the local brain.
603	
604	## Privacy And Egress
605	
606	The default brain artifacts are local and inspectable. Deterministic refresh,
607	semantic indexing, local history indexing, and MCP tool calls do not require a
608	hosted model. The MCP adapter is stdio-only.
609	
610	Some operations perform network egress, either by sending selected context to a
611	model or by fetching over the network:
612	
613	- a configured `checkpoint_remote` lets `refresh` and its `sessions` export
614	  stage fetch checkpoint history from that remote into a throwaway temp repo;
615	  this is network egress, not a hosted-model call, and is skipped under
616	  no-egress mode
617	- seed synthesis during `refresh --agent auto`
618	- fact distillation with `distill --agent ...`
619	- query expansion with `recall --expand`
620	- pattern verification and skill synthesis
621	- judged evaluation commands
622	
623	Use `--agent none`, `--dry-run`, local loopback Ollama, or
624	`ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS=1` / `ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY=1` when the repo must stay
625	strictly local. No-egress mode enforces locality for no-agent, dry-run, and
626	loopback-Ollama paths by validating URLs, redirects, and resolved dial targets.
627	A custom `--agent command` runner is treated as a trusted local command and is
628	not enforceably loopback-only; no-egress mode cannot stop that runner from
629	making its own network calls.
630	
631	Remember that base Entire session capture stores transcripts and metadata on
632	the repository's `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. Anyone with access to that
633	branch can read captured prompts, tool activity, and retained transcript data.
634	Entire redacts detected secrets before writing checkpoint metadata, but
635	redaction is best-effort. Redaction covers transcript and checkpoint metadata,
636	not every local working artifact. Entire also writes temporary shadow branches
637	such as `entire/<short-hash>` whose code-file snapshots are raw, unredacted
638	blobs of the working tree. Gitignored files are filtered out only as a partial
639	defense. Entire does not push shadow branches; do not push them manually, or
640	unredacted source could reach the remote. Review the Entire CLI security and
641	privacy guide before enabling Entire on sensitive or public repositories.
642	
643	## Storage And Configuration
644	
645	Entire CLI supplies the plugin directories that make the brain durable:
646	
647	- `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR` for `brain.json`
648	- `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` for generated repo brains and workspaces
649	- `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` for regenerable cursors such as watcher state
650	- `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` for caches
651	- `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT` for the current checkout when invoked inside a repo
652	
653	Repo keys are derived from the repository origin. For example,
654	`github.com/entireio/cli` becomes `gh/entireio/cli`.
655

4	local, inspectable "brain" for a repository from Entire session history, seeded
5	repository context, a local history index, an index of the brain's own docs (seed
6	summaries and copied repo markdown), optional semantic records from `entire-sem`,
7	and a curated layer of durable facts distilled from past sessions.
8	
9	The plugin binary is named `entire-brain` and is invoked through Entire as:
10	
11	```sh
12	entire brain
13	```
14

16	refresh/index/retrieval reads local repositories and writes local plugin data,
17	and the MCP adapter is stdio-only. Optional agent-gated steps can send selected
18	context to the configured agent (`refresh --agent auto`, `distill --agent
19	codex|claude-code`, `recall --expand`, and judged evals). Use `--agent none`,
20	`--dry-run`, `--agent command` with a local command, or loopback-only Ollama to
21	avoid hosted model egress. Strict no-egress mode (`ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS=1` or
22	`ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY=1`) can only enforce no-agent, dry-run, and Ollama
23	paths whose URLs, redirects, and resolved dial targets stay loopback-only;
24	arbitrary `--agent command` runners are trusted local commands but not
25	enforceably loopback-only. Separately, repos that configure a
26	`checkpoint_remote` allow `refresh` (and its `sessions` export stage) to `git fetch` checkpoint history
27	from that remote into a throwaway temp repo unless no-egress mode is set.
28	
29	## Install
30	
31	```sh
32	mise install
33	mise run check
34	mise run build
35	entire plugin install ./entire-brain
36	entire brain
37	```
38	
39	For a one-command local source install of this plugin, run:
40	
41	```sh
42	scripts/install-local.sh
43	```
44	
45	For an end-to-end local install that builds the sibling `entire-sem` checkout
46	first and then installs `entire-brain`, run:
47	
48	```sh
49	scripts/install.sh
50	```
51	
52	For local release archives with `SHA256SUMS`, run:
53	
54	```sh
55	scripts/release.sh
56	```
57	
58	See [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md) for target, cgo, and shared
59	baseline details.
60	
61	## Common Workflows
62	
63	### Create Or Refresh A Brain
64	
65	```sh
66	entire brain refresh
67	entire brain refresh --agent none
68	entire brain refresh --output /tmp/repo-brain
69	entire brain refresh --force
70	```
71	
72	`refresh` is the normal entry point. It writes the newest known checkpoint
73	version of every discoverable Entire session into the persistent brain
74	directory, builds deterministic repository seed context, runs `entire sem`, and
75	builds the local semantic context graph used by the `inspect`
76	`code`/`context`/`impact`/`changes`/`tests` commands and `brief`. It also derives
77	the local decision/rationale history index from the exported sessions and a doc
78	index over the brain's seed markdown. `--agent` controls optional seed synthesis:
79	the default is `auto`, which uses Codex when available, then Claude Code when
80	available, otherwise deterministic seed-only mode. `--output` writes a complete
81	brain to an explicit directory. `--force` rebuilds generated sources and
82	overwrites an explicit output directory when one is provided.
83	
84	The semantic refresh stores semantic snapshots, a SQLite query store, metrics,
85	parse cache, and branch overlays in the local brain directory. It refuses dirty
86	worktrees unless semantic worktree indexing is explicitly enabled through the
87	advanced `refresh index --worktree` maintenance path.
88	
89	Use `--worktree` on `refresh index` only when you intentionally want the current
90	dirty worktree represented. Bundle export rejects worktree-backed semantic indexes.
91	`repair` rebuilds derived semantic stores from the active local snapshot.
92	`reset --semantic-only --force` removes semantic artifacts and manifest metadata
93	without touching seed or session sources. `reset --force` removes the generated
94	brain directory for the repo.
95	
96	`bench semantic <repo> --profile syntax-only --sem-binary <entire>` measures the
97	end-to-end semantic Brain path in an isolated temporary plugin store. It reports
98	wall time, peak RSS, provider/schema metadata, and file/symbol/relation counts
99	without overwriting the normal local brain for that repository. Add `--json` for
100	machine-readable output and `--progress` for phase updates.
101	
102	### Keep The Brain Fresh Automatically
103	
104	```sh
105	entire brain watch                       # poll every 5m; deterministic refresh only (NO tokens)
106	entire brain watch --once                # single pass (handy for a cron/CI hook)
107	entire brain watch --distill --distill-every 24h --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low --budget 1
108	```
109	
110	`watch` keeps the brain current without manual refreshes, and its token-frugality is **structural,
111	not a quota**:
112	
113	- It detects new work cheaply (local + origin checkpoint refs + worktree HEAD), and on a change runs a
114	  **deterministic refresh** — sessions, semantic index, and history index, with the seed agent **always**
115	  `none` — which spends **zero agent tokens**.
116	- The token-spending work — `--distill` and/or agent seed synthesis (`--seed-agent codex|claude-code`) —
117	  is **off by default** and only ever runs on a brain that was actually refreshed this tick (a failed
118	  refresh skips it). When enabled, **both steps share one gate**: they run at most once per
119	  `--distill-every`, on the cheap `--model`/`--effort`, and `--budget N` caps the *number of gated agent
120	  runs* per process. So `--seed-agent` is bounded exactly like `--distill` — it is **not** per-change
121	  spend. A persisted cursor (`<state>/repos/<repo-key>/watch.json`) means a restart never re-refreshes
122	  unchanged state or re-runs the agent work within the interval. (Budget counts reset on restart; the
123	  durable guard is `--distill-every` + the cursor. A transient failure of one gated step is best-effort —
124	  it retries on the next interval, not every tick.)
125	
126	So the default daemon is free; you opt into token spend explicitly and bound it. Run **one watcher per
127	repo** — the cursor write is atomic, so concurrent watchers won't corrupt it, but they may do redundant
128	refreshes. On a very active repo with a short `--interval`, note that the free refresh re-indexes on
129	every commit, so the semantic reindex can be CPU/IO-heavy; widen `--interval` if that matters.
130	
131	### Work Across Multiple Repos
132	
133	```sh
134	entire brain workspace create platform
135	entire brain workspace add platform ../api --name api
136	entire brain workspace add platform ../web --name web
137	entire brain workspace refresh platform          # membership freshness; --full also refreshes each member brain
138	entire brain workspace inspect context platform "checkout" --json   # symbols (multi-repo `context`)
139	entire brain workspace search platform "checkout" --json    # facts/history/docs (also: vsearch, query)
140	entire brain workspace inspect impact platform "checkout" --json
141	entire brain workspace watch platform --once          # fan the token-frugal daemon over every member
142	```
143	
144	Workspaces coordinate already-local repo brains by repo key and local path hint.
145	They do not sync or publish generated brain data. `workspace watch` runs the same
146	deterministic-refresh-is-free / agent-steps-are-gated loop as `watch` across every member repo, with a
147	single `--budget` shared across all members so a workspace tick can't multiply token spend by repo count.
148	
149	### Use MCP Locally
150	
151	```sh
152	entire brain mcp
153	```
154	
155	The MCP adapter is stdio-only and exposes local tools `brain_status`
156	(`brain_index_status` alias), `brain_brief`, the unified retrieval verbs
157	`brain_query` (hybrid lexical+vector over facts/history/docs), `brain_search`,
158	`brain_vsearch`, `brain_get`, and `brain_multi_get`, the code and graph tools
159	`brain_index_repository`, `brain_list_projects`, `brain_delete_project`,
160	`brain_code`/`brain_search_code`, `brain_context`, `brain_impact`,
161	`brain_changes`/`brain_detect_changes`, `brain_tests`, `brain_boundaries`,
162	`brain_search_graph`, `brain_query_graph`, `brain_get_graph_schema`,
163	`brain_get_architecture`, `brain_get_code_snippet`, `brain_trace_path`,
164	`brain_dead_code`, and `brain_ingest_traces`, the diff-less reviewer
165	`brain_regressions`/`brain_review`, and the cross-repo
166	`brain_workspace_graph`/`brain_workspace_regressions`/`brain_workspace_review`,
167	plus read-only pattern inspection via `brain_patterns`/`brain_patterns_status`.
168	See `docs/semantic_mcp_guide.md`.
169	
170	### Diff-less review (suspected regressions: current tree vs session memory)
171	
172	The brain can act as a reviewer without a diff: it compares the current working tree against what
173	session history asserts the code used to be, and flags suspected regressions (`file:line`, expected
174	vs current, confidence, provenance). Surfaces:
175	
176	```sh
177	entire brain inspect regressions "<task + failing symbols>"   # raw anomalies
178	entire brain review "<task + failing symbols>" --json         # review-shaped findings (hidden; the machine contract)
179	entire brain workspace inspect regressions <ws> "<query>"             # fan out across a multi-repo workspace
180	entire brain workspace review <ws> "<query>"                  # same, review-shaped, per repo
181	```
182	
183	- `--location-only` (all of the above; `location_only` for the MCP tools) returns only the suspected
184	  `file:line`, never the expected/current values — so a fair A/B can't paste the answer.
185	- `--include-deletions` adds the noisier deleted-assignment signal (opt-in).
186	- `entire brain review --json` emits a **versioned `reviewReport` contract** (`schema_version`); see
187	  `docs/diffless_review_seam.md`.
188	
189	`entire brain review` is hidden because it is the **machine contract**, not a human verb. The intended
190	human surfaces are the cli's `entire review` (a diff-less mode that *would* turn on when the brain is installed)
191	and `entire labs investigate`. Those consumers live in the `entireio/cli` repo and are **not yet wired**
192	(review has a CLI prototype; investigate is designed only) — see `docs/diffless_review_seam.md`.
193	
194	### Ask The Brain
195	
196	The qmd-inspired retrieval verbs rank across the brain's text layers — durable
197	facts, indexed history, and docs — and return ids you can fetch in full:
198	
199	```sh
200	entire brain query "how does checkpointing work" --json   # hybrid (lexical + vector, RRF) — the default
201	entire brain search "checkpoint" --json                   # lexical keyword (facts + BM25 history/docs)
202	entire brain vsearch "preventing data races" --json       # vector / semantic (facts + docs; + history with a Gemma-class embedder)
203	entire brain get fact:<id> --json                         # fetch one item by id (fact:… | history:… | doc:…)
204	entire brain multi-get fact:<id> doc:<id> --json          # fetch several by id
205	```
206	
207	All five accept `--json`, `--format json|cli`, and `--branch`; `search`,
208	`vsearch`, and `query` also take `--limit`/`-n`. Every result carries an `id`
209	you can pass to `get`/`multi-get`. `--branch` selects the durable-facts branch;
210	history and docs come from the local indexed brain sources.
211	
212	#### Semantic embedder (vector arm)
213	
214	The vector arm behind `vsearch`/`query` embeds with a **bundled, pure-Go
215	Model2Vec** static model by default — zero config, no daemon, fully offline. For
216	higher recall you can opt into a **transformer embedder (EmbeddingGemma-300M)**
217	served over a local HTTP endpoint (Ollama, or qmd's node-llama-cpp server):
218	
219	```sh
220	ollama pull embeddinggemma                       # one-time
221	ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBEDDER=ollama entire brain query "preventing data races" --json
222	```
223	
224	- `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBEDDER=ollama` selects the transformer arm. It measured **+14%
225	  useful-facts-per-1k-tokens** over Model2Vec on the facts eval (pooled across
226	  repos), driven mostly by *reachability* — it surfaces conceptually-related
227	  facts that share no query term.
228	- `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL` (default `embeddinggemma`) and
229	  `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBED_URL` (default `http://localhost:11434/api/embed`) override
230	  the model and endpoint. The endpoint just needs to accept `{"model","input"}`
231	  and return `{"embeddings":[[…]]}`.
232	- **Graceful fallback (one-time startup probe):** the embedder is chosen once, on
233	  first use. If the opt-in is set but the embed server does not return an
234	  embedding then (unreachable, wrong model, or an error response), the brain
235	  selects the bundled Model2Vec model (one consistent vector space) and prints a
236	  one-line notice on stderr rather than selecting an embedder that fails every
237	  call. The probe is not repeated per embed: if a server that was healthy at
238	  startup later fails mid-run, those individual embeds degrade to lexical for
239	  that run. Switching embedders re-namespaces the vector cache, so the two never
240	  mix.
241	
242	This is the Stage 1b transformer embedder available **without cgo** today; the
243	in-process single-binary form is deferred (tracked in the alignment plan outside this repository).
244	
245	`overview` is the fastest way to orient on an unfamiliar repo: it returns a
246	single project map — stack stats, route/tool/workflow counts, build/test
247	commands, entrypoints, key documents, and recent decisions newest-first.
248	
249	```sh
250	entire brain overview --json
251	```
252	
253	`brief` is the per-task entry point: it combines brain availability, freshness,
254	live git state, semantic context and test suggestions, matching history records,
255	and the top matching durable facts for the task (sized to the requested
256	`--limit`). `status`, `show`, and the retrieval verbs above provide smaller
257	top-level queries for agents and scripts.
258	
259	For symbol-graph navigation and regression analysis — what the retrieval verbs
260	don't cover — use the `inspect` specialists:
261	
262	```sh
263	entire brain guide
264	entire brain inspect code "ValidateToken" --json         # find a symbol in the graph
265	entire brain inspect search-graph "ValidateToken" --json # search symbols and relations
266	entire brain inspect query-graph 'MATCH (a)-[r:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.name CONTAINS "Validate" RETURN a,r,b LIMIT 10' --json
267	entire brain inspect graph-schema --json                 # relation/schema inventory
268	entire brain inspect graph-ui semantic-graph.html        # local static graph explorer
269	entire brain inspect snippet "ValidateToken" --json      # source for one symbol
270	entire brain inspect trace-path "caller" "callee" --json # directed relation path
271	entire brain inspect dead-code --json                    # heuristic unused callable candidates
272	entire brain inspect ingest-traces traces.ndjson --json  # compare and persist queryable runtime traces
273	entire brain inspect context "main" --json               # relation-aware context for a symbol
274	entire brain inspect impact "main" --json                # impact set via typed relations
275	entire brain inspect changes --json                      # map the working-tree diff to symbols
276	entire brain inspect tests "main" --json                 # test suggestions for a symbol
277	entire brain inspect boundaries --kind tool --json       # route / tool / workflow boundaries
278	entire brain workspace inspect graph platform --json     # per-repo graph + shared contracts; writes workspaces/platform/graph.json
279	entire brain inspect regressions "<task>" --json         # suspected regressions vs session memory
280	entire brain inspect blame <fact-id> --json              # the source anchors a fact was derived from
281	```
282	
283	History content (decisions, validations, tool paths, architecture notes) is no
284	longer a set of per-kind commands — it is indexed into the history layer and
285	surfaced through the unified `search`/`query` verbs above. Symbol lookup that used
286	to be the top-level `search` now lives at `inspect code`; `inspect context`/`impact`
287	accept a symbol name or a record id.
288	
289	The `status` Semantic section lists the files the semantic provider could not
290	fully index (blind spots), so an agent knows where its semantic answers are
291	untrustworthy:
292	
293	```sh
294	entire brain status
295	```
296	
297	### Durable Facts
298	
299	The brain also keeps a curated **durable-facts** layer: short, self-contained,
300	provenance-anchored statements about how work on the repo should be done —
301	resolved decisions and their *why*, standing rules, stated preferences, and
302	non-obvious constraints. Unlike the history index (read-only excerpts), facts
303	are distilled, deduplicated, branch-scoped, and agent-writable. Facts carry
304	retained session/checkpoint anchors; `verify` reports whether those anchors are
305	verified, stale, orphaned, or unverifiable-here. Full turn-level cryptographic
306	verification depends on CLI-side turn signing.
307	
308	```sh
309	entire brain distill --agent codex                         # extract facts from captured sessions
310	entire brain distill --dry-run --json                      # estimate sessions/chunks/calls without agent work
311	entire brain distill --agent codex --jobs 4                # parallelize extraction, reconcile deterministically
312	entire brain distill --agent ollama --model llama3.2       # local loopback Ollama
313	entire brain distill --agent codex --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low   # run it on a fast/cheap model
314	entire brain remember "Prefer table-driven tests" --path preferences.coding.style
315	entire brain recall "account deletion" --k 5
316	entire brain recall "MirrorCommittedMetadataRef" --expand   # agent expands the query first
317	entire brain facts status --json           # read-only fact/eval readiness summary
318	entire brain facts tree --depth 1           # navigable map of what the brain knows
319	entire brain facts tree --path constraints  # drill into a category
320	```
321	
322	`distill` runs one extraction call per uncached transcript chunk, plus up to one
323	reconcile call for chunks that produce candidates, so it is worth running on a
324	**fast/cheap model**: `--model`/`--effort` pin the model + reasoning effort for
325	both the distill and reconcile agent calls (codex: `--model <m> --config
326	model_reasoning_effort=<e>`; claude-code: `--model <m> --effort <e>`).
327	The same `--model`/`--effort` flags exist on `seed`, and `refresh` forwards them as `--seed-model`/
328	`--seed-effort`, so a full `entire brain refresh` can synthesize its seed cheaply too.
329	
330	`distill` is agent-required: it sends line-numbered transcript chunks to the
331	selected agent under a strict quality gate (`--agent auto` chooses Codex, then
332	Claude Code; `ollama` and `command` are explicit), then reconciles each candidate
333	against the branch's existing facts so near-duplicates merge and contradictions
334	supersede (low-confidence calls are queued for review). It is incremental by
335	default; `--force` rebuilds. `remember` authors a fact directly (the agent
336	classifies it when `--path` is omitted). `recall` retrieves by keyword + taxonomy
337	+ code-locus match, scoped to the current branch; `--scope local|cross-cutting`
338	separates code facts from how-we-work facts, and `--expand` has the agent
339	rewrite the query into the facts' vocabulary first.
340	
341	Manage the fact store:
342	
343	```sh
344	entire brain facts status --json
345	entire brain facts review                   # resolve queued merge/supersede proposals
346	entire brain facts promote --from <branch> --strategy keep-both
347	entire brain facts retract <fact-id>        # mark a fact no longer true (gc prunes later)
348	entire brain facts gc --force               # prune retracted/old-superseded; report orphans
349	```
350	
351	The fact store also ships an evaluation harness for measuring retrieval quality
352	(`facts eval-gen` builds a provenance/silver-labeled benchmark from the brain's
353	own sessions, `facts eval` reports retrieved items, token estimates, precision,
354	useful-per-1k, and recall only when labels exist for that retriever, and `facts
355	eval-compare` does a paired t-test with Holm correction and rejects non-proof or
356	different relevance sources unless `--allow-proxy-comparison` is explicit). Use `facts eval
357	--retriever facts|history|query|raw-sessions` to compare distilled facts against
358	history, unified query, and preprocessed session-chunk baselines before claiming
359	a quality lift.
360	Generated source-session fields give source-match credit for history/session
361	arms; they are provenance/proxy evidence, not recall labels. Task files with
362	`relevant` ids must set `label_source` (`human`, `judge_refined`, or
363	`provenance_silver`), and paired proof runs must share the same task-file and
364	brain-manifest hashes unless an override is called out.
365	The eval `query` arm is a read-only lexical unified baseline over local brain
366	layers; it does not write embedding caches or call an embedder. See
367	`docs/durable_facts_plan.md` for the full design.
368	
369	For semantic release checks, the `semantic` section of `entire brain status
370	--json` reports the provider/schema state, counts, file-language/symbol/relation
371	coverage, warning/failure details, freshness axes, and blind spots in one local
372	audit payload (`status --fail-on release` is the CI gate form). Treat that as audit evidence for the reported provider output, not a
373	global tree-sitter coverage claim; public semantic claims should name the covered
374	languages, relation types, freshness state, and benchmark or audit records behind
375	the claim.
376	
377	## Storage
378	
379	The parent Entire CLI supplies these directories:
380	
381	| Variable | Purpose |
382	|---|---|
383	| `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR` | Plugin config, including `brain.json`. |
384	| `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` | Durable brains under `repos/<repo-key>/`; workspaces under `workspaces/<name>/`. |
385	| `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` | Regenerable cursors under `repos/<repo-key>/`. |
386	| `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` | Cache data. |
387	| `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT` | Current git checkout when invoked inside a repo. |
388	
389	Repo keys come from the repository origin. For example,
390	`github.com/entireio/cli` becomes `gh/entireio/cli`.
391	
392	### Environment toggles
393	
394	Optional `ENTIRE_BRAIN_*` variables tune retrieval and diagnostics. All are
395	off/default unless set; none are required for normal use.
396	
397	| Variable | Default | Effect |
398	|---|---|---|
399	| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBEDDER` | (unset → Model2Vec) | Set to `ollama` to use the transformer embedder (EmbeddingGemma) for the vector arm instead of the bundled Model2Vec model. Falls back to Model2Vec with a stderr notice if a one-time startup probe finds the server does not return an embedding (unreachable, wrong model, or error response). See [Semantic embedder](#semantic-embedder-vector-arm). |
400	| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL` | `embeddinggemma` | Model name requested from the embed server when `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBEDDER=ollama`. |
401	| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBED_URL` | `http://localhost:11434/api/embed` | Embed endpoint (Ollama, or qmd's node-llama-cpp server). Must accept `{"model","input"}` and return `{"embeddings":[[…]]}`. |
402	| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_FACTS_BM25` | (unset → token-overlap) | `1`/`true`/`yes`/`on` switches the facts **lexical** arm to FTS5 BM25. Experimental; measured at parity with the default scorer, kept for A/B'ing the lexical engine. |
403	| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_MCP_DEBUG_LOG` | (unset) | Path to a file the stdio MCP adapter appends frame-level debug lines to. Diagnostics only. |
404	
405	## Development
406	
407	For development without installing:
408	
409	```sh
410	go run ./cmd/entire-brain --help
411	```
412	
413	When running outside the Entire CLI, set plugin directories explicitly or allow
414	the XDG fallbacks:
415	
416	```sh
417	ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" \
418	ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" \
419	ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" \
420	ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" \
421	  go run ./cmd/entire-brain doctor
422	```
423	
424	Usual mise tasks:
425	
426	```sh
427	mise run fmt         # gofmt -s -w .
428	mise run lint        # go vet, gofmt check, go mod tidy check, shellcheck
429	mise run test        # go test ./...
430	mise run test:ci     # go test -race ./...
431	mise run test:phase1 # deterministic Phase 1 semantic suite
432	mise run build       # build ./entire-brain
433	mise run build-all   # cross-build common targets
434	mise run check       # lint, race tests, Phase 1 tests, and cross-builds
435	```
436	
437	GitHub Actions runs generic tests and the deterministic Phase 1 semantic suite
438	on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

# Entire Brain

Entire Brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI. It builds a local,
inspectable "brain" for a repository — and this is the fastest way to understand
what it does, how to install it, and how humans and agents actually use it.

## What This Is

Entire is a Git-native platform for AI-assisted software work. Its base layer is
session capture: `entire-cli` installs Git and agent hooks for supported coding
agents, records prompts, transcripts, tool activity, files touched, token usage,
and checkpoint metadata, then stores that context on a dedicated Entire-managed
ref (`entire/checkpoints/v1`) instead of mixing it into normal code history. A
checkpoint is the retained link between an agent session and the commit or
intermediate work state it produced.

`entire-sem` and `entire-brain` add the local reasoning layer on top of that
captured history. `entire-sem` is the semantic provider: it parses source code
locally and emits versioned code-structure records and semantic diffs.
`entire-brain` consumes those records plus Entire sessions, checkpoint history,
docs, runtime traces, durable facts, and pattern evidence into a local
repository brain.

The result is a local memory system for humans and agents. Humans install,
refresh, and curate the brain. Agents consume it through configured hooks, MCP
tools, file-based intake instructions, or direct JSON commands when MCP is not
available. The practical effect is that an agent can start work with retained
context, freshness signals, semantic navigation, prior decisions, likely tests,
and known failure modes instead of rediscovering them from scratch.

The plugin binary is named `entire-brain` and is invoked through Entire as
`entire brain`.

## Install

Prerequisites:

- Entire CLI installed and available as `entire`
- Entire already enabled in the repository you want to use
- The target agent hooks already installed for that repository
- Git
- Go 1.26 toolchain for `entire-brain`
- A cgo-capable compiler/toolchain for `entire-sem`

### 1. Clone the repositories

Clone `entire-sem` and `entire-brain` side by side. The directory names matter:
`scripts/install.sh` expects `entire-sem` to be the sibling checkout next to
`entire-brain`.

```sh
cd /path/to/your/source-directory

git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-sem.git
git clone https://github.com/ashtom/entire-brain.git
```

### 2. Install the plugins

Run the installer from the `entire-brain` checkout:

```sh
cd /path/to/your/source-directory/entire-brain
scripts/install.sh
```

This builds and installs both plugins, writes the default `entire-brain`
configuration file, then runs `entire brain doctor`. `entire-brain` uses a
pure-Go default build; `entire-sem` uses tree-sitter native parser bindings, so
its local source build needs cgo.

Other install paths:

- `scripts/install-local.sh` — one-command local source install of just this plugin.
- `mise install && mise run check && mise run build && entire plugin install ./entire-brain` — build without the sibling `entire-sem` step.
- `scripts/release.sh` — local release archives with `SHA256SUMS`.

See [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md) for target, cgo, and shared
baseline details.

Verify:

```sh
entire sem version
entire sem doctor --json
entire brain version
entire brain doctor
entire plugin doctor
```

If `doctor` reports the semantic provider is missing, check that `entire-sem`
and `entire-brain` were cloned side by side with the names above.

### 3. Build the deterministic brain

Run the first refresh in the Entire-enabled repository you want agents to work in:

```sh
cd /path/to/your/repo

entire brain refresh --agent none
entire brain status
```

The semantic refresh refuses a dirty worktree by default. Run it on a clean
checkout, or use the advanced `entire brain refresh index --worktree` path only
when you intentionally want the current uncommitted state indexed. Worktree-
backed semantic indexes are rejected by bundle export.

`--agent none` keeps the first build deterministic and token-free, with no
hosted-model calls. Refresh exports captured sessions, builds the local
history/doc indexes, asks `entire-sem` for a semantic snapshot, and stores the
derived brain under Entire's local plugin data directory.

At this point the brain can answer from captured history, docs, semantic code
structure, runtime traces, patterns, and any existing durable facts. It has not
yet extracted new durable facts from retained sessions.

### 4. Distill durable facts

Distillation is the egress-gated agent step that turns captured sessions into
durable project knowledge: decisions, constraints, preferences, gotchas,
conventions, and invariants.

```sh
entire brain distill --dry-run --json                                  # estimate cost first
entire brain distill --agent codex --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low   # extract
entire brain facts status --json
entire brain facts tree --depth 1
```

Distillation sends redacted transcript chunks to the selected agent unless you
use a local loopback agent such as Ollama. It is incremental and cached:
unchanged sessions are skipped, near-duplicate facts are reconciled against the
branch's existing facts, and low-confidence merge/supersede decisions are queued
for `entire brain facts review`.

For active repos, keep the brain current with the watcher — deterministic
refreshes are free; token-spending work is opt-in and separately gated:

```sh
entire brain watch                                                                    # deterministic refresh only (NO tokens)
entire brain watch --distill --distill-every 24h --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low --budget 1
```

If you also want generated seed summaries, run refresh with an agent instead of
the deterministic seed path (`entire brain refresh --agent auto --seed-model
gpt-5.4-mini --seed-effort low`). Seed synthesis orients an agent on the
repository; durable facts are branch-scoped retained knowledge — the two are
separate.

## How Agents Use The Brain

Agents rely on a capture layer plus four consumption surfaces. The capture layer
produces the raw material; the consumption surfaces are how an agent actually
queries or receives brain context. Which surface matters depends on the agent
client and how the repository is configured.

### Capture layer: Entire hooks produce the raw material

`entire-cli` installs lifecycle hooks for agents such as Claude Code, Codex,
Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, and Pi. Those hooks
start and stop sessions, capture prompts and transcripts, track changed files,
record subagent work where the agent exposes it, and attach checkpoint metadata
to commits. This is background infrastructure: the agent does not remember to
save a transcript, and the human does not paste context into the brain.

If an agent is not seeing Entire context at all, check the base Entire
integration first, not the brain (`entire status`, `entire agent`).

### 1. MCP is the preferred agent tool surface

For agents that support MCP, register `entire brain mcp` as a local stdio MCP
server. It opens no network listener and wraps the local brain's JSON contracts
as tools. Once MCP is available, an agent should call MCP tools instead of
shelling out to the CLI. The normal first call is `brain_brief`, then targeted
follow-ups:

- `brain_brief` for task-shaped context, history hits, likely files, and tests
- `brain_status` to check freshness, coverage, and blind spots
- retrieval tools such as `brain_query` and `brain_get` for facts, docs, history
- semantic tools such as `brain_code`, `brain_context`, `brain_impact`, and
  `brain_tests` for code navigation and validation planning
- review, workspace, and pattern tools such as `brain_regressions`,
  `brain_workspace_graph`, `brain_workspace_review`, and `brain_patterns` when
  the task calls for them

Some MCP tools write local state (for example `brain_ingest_traces` persists
runtime edges as `RUNTIME_TRACE` facts); pattern MCP tools are read-only. The
MCP and CLI surfaces are intentionally close but not perfect mirrors — prefer the
native surface your agent client has, then translate only when needed. See
[docs/semantic_mcp_guide.md](docs/semantic_mcp_guide.md) for the full tool surface.

### 2. Intake instructions are the file-based fallback

When MCP is not available, an agent can use the brain through the intake
instructions in `templates/`. The templates tell the agent to locate the brain
with `entire brain path "$PWD"`, then read staged context instead of blindly
opening everything: `README.md` and `manifest.json` in the brain directory, seed
files under `seed/agent/`, `seed/history-gaps.md` when present, and only
task-relevant transcripts selected from the manifest. Treat gaps as uncertainty
rather than inventing rationale.

### 3. Direct CLI is a compatibility surface

For clients without MCP, direct `entire brain ... --json` calls are the
compatibility surface (humans and scripts use the same commands). Treat it like a
tool API, not an invitation to run a long command tour:

```sh
entire brain status --json
entire brain brief "<task>" --json
# then the smallest next question:
entire brain query "<decision or prior-work question>" --json
entire brain inspect code "<symbol or concept>" --json
entire brain inspect tests "<symbol-or-id>" --json
entire brain inspect regressions "<task or invariant>" --location-only --json
```

Prefer `query` for broad facts/history/docs, `search` for exact terms, semantic
`inspect` subcommands for code-graph questions, and `get`/`multi-get` when a
prior result returned an id. Don't broaden into repo-wide text search until the
brain's targeted context has been used.

### 4. Hidden hooks deliver context at the moment of relevance

`entire-brain` also has a hidden hook surface for harness integrations. These are
not installed by base Entire enablement; a harness must be configured to invoke
them (for example Claude Code `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` hooks). They surface a
small, high-confidence fact exactly when it matters — facts anchored to a file
before editing it, gotchas after a failed command, optional one-session refresh
after a session ends. The contract is intentionally quiet: with no relevant
fact, no local brain, or an environment problem, the hook exits successfully with
no stdout output, so it never breaks the agent workflow.

## Usage Scenarios

The examples name the preferred MCP tool when there is one. Agent clients without
MCP should use the equivalent `entire brain ... --json` command.

### Orient an agent on a new task

Start by asking for task-shaped context, not a generic summary. The normal tool
is `brain_brief` — it returns freshness, likely files and symbols, relevant
history, durable facts, likely tests, and blind spots. Use it before broad shell
search. For repo-level orientation instead of task-specific, use `overview`
(`entire brain overview --json`): a compact project map of stack signals,
entrypoints, commands, key documents, and recent decisions.

### Keep the brain fresh

Freshness is part of every answer — a stale index, missing provider, dirty-
worktree mismatch, or parser blind spot changes how much an agent should trust
the brain. Agents check freshness through `brain_status`/`status --json` before
relying on semantic answers; if unsafe, an agent with write permission can
request a refresh, otherwise it reports the limitation and falls back to direct
inspection.

```sh
entire brain status
entire brain refresh --agent none
entire brain watch
```

When semantic artifacts are out of sync or damaged, use the maintenance paths
instead of deleting the whole brain (`refresh index`, `repair`, `reset
--semantic-only --force`). Use `refresh index --worktree` only when you
intentionally want uncommitted state indexed; exported bundles reject
worktree-backed semantic indexes.

### Continue or explain prior work

When the question is "why is this like this?", "what did the previous agent
try?", or "where did this session leave off?", search the history and facts
layers — `brain_query`/`brain_search`, then `brain_get` for specific ids. This is
the main reason Entire capture matters: the original prompt, attempts,
validation, correction, and rationale survive the code diff and become available
to the next agent.

### Ask across facts, history, and docs

When the question is not tied to one symbol, use the unified retrieval layer.
`query` is the hybrid path (lexical + vector, RRF) over durable facts, indexed
history, and docs; `search` for exact keywords, `vsearch` for semantic matches,
`get`/`multi-get` when a result returns an id. Every result carries an `id`.

```sh
entire brain query "how does checkpointing work" --json
entire brain search "checkpoint" --json
entire brain vsearch "preventing data races" --json
entire brain get fact:<id> --json
```

For durable facts specifically, `recall` retrieves by keyword + taxonomy + code
locus, scoped to the current branch; `recall --expand` is an agent-assisted
query-expansion path, so it sits behind the same egress judgment as other agent
calls.

### Navigate code by meaning

When a task depends on structure rather than text, use the semantic tools:
`brain_code`/`brain_search_code` to find candidate symbols, then `brain_context`,
`brain_impact`, and `brain_tests`. This is where `entire-sem` matters — it is the
local parser/provider that gives the brain the graph the agent queries. Semantic
depth is language-dependent: parser-backed extraction covers the semantic
language set; many recognized filetypes are inventory-only, where you should
prefer text retrieval and lower confidence in impact/context answers.

```sh
entire brain inspect code "ValidateToken" --json         # find a symbol in the graph
entire brain inspect context "ValidateToken" --json      # relation-aware context
entire brain inspect impact "ValidateToken" --json       # impact set via typed relations
entire brain inspect tests "ValidateToken" --json        # test suggestions
entire brain inspect graph-schema --json                 # relation/schema inventory
entire brain inspect graph-ui semantic-graph.html        # local static graph explorer
entire brain inspect trace-path "<caller>" "<callee>" --json
entire brain inspect dead-code --json
entire brain inspect boundaries --kind tool --json
entire brain inspect changes --json                      # map the working-tree diff to symbols
```

### Review risk without a clean diff

For long sessions, manual edits, or suspected regressions from memory, use
diff-less regression review — `brain_regressions`/`brain_review`. It compares the
current working tree against what session history asserts the code used to be and
flags suspected regressions (`file:line`, expected vs current, confidence,
provenance). Prefer `--location-only` first for a fair investigation: it points
to suspected files and lines without handing over the expected answer text.
`entire brain review --json` emits a versioned `reviewReport` contract; see
[docs/diffless_review_seam.md](docs/diffless_review_seam.md).

### Connect runtime evidence to source

When static structure is not enough, import runtime trace edges with
`brain_ingest_traces` / `inspect ingest-traces`. The brain compares runtime edges
with known static relations, persists them as `RUNTIME_TRACE` graph facts, and
makes them available to graph-schema, trace-path, and brief/context flows —
useful for incidents and performance work where "what actually happened?" matters
more than "what could call this?"

### Work across multiple repositories

Use workspaces when behavior crosses repository boundaries. Humans create and
refresh the workspace; agents consume it through MCP workspace tools or direct
workspace CLI commands. The workspace brain keeps member repos local and builds
cross-repo contracts and graph edges from their existing local brains.

```sh
entire brain workspace create platform
entire brain workspace add platform ../api --name api
entire brain workspace add platform ../web --name web
entire brain workspace refresh platform --full
entire brain workspace inspect context platform "checkout" --json
entire brain workspace inspect impact platform "checkout" --json
entire brain workspace review platform "checkout regression" --json
```

### Preserve durable project knowledge

Durable facts are short, provenance-anchored statements about decisions,
constraints, preferences, pitfalls, and standing rules. Humans write them
directly when they know the rule; agents distill candidates from captured
sessions when explicitly asked. Facts have a lifecycle: review queued
merge/supersede proposals, promote branch facts that should carry forward,
retract facts that are no longer true, and garbage-collect stale retractions.

```sh
entire brain remember "Prefer table-driven tests for parser edge cases" --path preferences.tests
entire brain distill --agent codex --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low
entire brain facts review
entire brain facts promote --from <branch> --strategy keep-both
entire brain facts retract <fact-id>
entire brain facts gc --force
entire brain inspect blame <fact-id> --json
```

### Extract reusable agent skills

Skill extraction forms skills only from accepted deep dossiers: verified evidence
that a pattern is non-obvious and useful to future agents (recurring task
patterns, verified themes, corrected/failed episodes, durable gotchas and
conventions, cross-repo families). A human or explicitly authorized automation
runs the egress-gated verification and formation; refresh, watch, brief, query,
MCP reads, and workspace reads do not silently call it.

```sh
entire brain patterns
entire brain patterns verify --deep
entire brain patterns skills            # list formable proposals
entire brain patterns skills form <id>  # preview evidence + generated SKILL.md
entire brain patterns skills form <id> --yes
```

`form <id>` previews the evidence, generated `SKILL.md`, and destination without
writing; if no accepted deep dossier exists it refuses and tells you to verify
first (it never falls back to shallow evidence). `--yes` writes the skill;
existing files require `--force`. Generated skills target the cross-agent
`standard` destination (`.agents/skills/`) by default; use
`--target claude-code|codex|factoryai-droid|all` for an agent-specific
destination.

### Measure brain quality

The brain includes evaluation harnesses for maintainers who need evidence that a
retriever or fact layer is actually helping — not required for everyday use, but
the right surface before claiming a quality lift.

```sh
entire brain facts eval-gen > facts-tasks.json
entire brain facts eval --tasks facts-tasks.json --retriever facts --json > facts-eval.json
entire brain facts eval-compare --a <before.json> --b <after.json>
entire brain bench semantic .
entire brain status --json
```

`facts eval-compare` runs a paired t-test with Holm correction and rejects
non-proof or mismatched relevance sources unless `--allow-proxy-comparison` is
explicit. Treat the `semantic` section of `status --json` as audit evidence for
the reported provider output (`status --fail-on release` is the CI gate form),
not a global coverage claim; public semantic claims should name the covered
languages, relation types, freshness state, and benchmark records behind them.

### Tune retrieval

The default vector arm uses a bundled, pure-Go Model2Vec static model — zero
config, offline. For higher semantic recall, opt into a transformer embedder
(EmbeddingGemma-300M) served by Ollama or a compatible loopback endpoint:

```sh
ollama pull embeddinggemma
ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBEDDER=ollama entire brain query "preventing data races" --json
```

It measured about +14% useful-facts-per-1k-tokens over Model2Vec on the facts
eval, driven mostly by reachability (it surfaces conceptually related facts that
share no query term). The embedder is chosen once, on first use: if the opt-in is
set but the server does not return an embedding, the brain falls back to
Model2Vec with a one-line stderr notice. Switching embedders re-namespaces the
vector cache, so the two never mix. Changing the embedder changes retrieval
behavior, not the underlying source of truth.

## Privacy And Egress

Default brain artifacts are local and inspectable. Deterministic refresh,
semantic indexing, local history indexing, and MCP tool calls do not require a
hosted model, and the MCP adapter is stdio-only.

Some operations perform network egress, either by sending selected context to a
model or by fetching over the network:

- a configured `checkpoint_remote` lets `refresh` (and its `sessions` export
  stage) `git fetch` checkpoint history into a throwaway temp repo — network
  egress, not a hosted-model call, skipped under no-egress mode
- seed synthesis during `refresh --agent auto`
- fact distillation with `distill --agent ...`
- query expansion with `recall --expand`
- pattern verification and skill synthesis
- judged evaluation commands

Use `--agent none`, `--dry-run`, local loopback Ollama, or
`ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS=1` / `ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY=1` when the repo must stay
strictly local. No-egress mode enforces locality for no-agent, dry-run, and
loopback-Ollama paths by validating URLs, redirects, and resolved dial targets. A
custom `--agent command` runner is a trusted local command and is not enforceably
loopback-only; no-egress mode cannot stop that runner from making its own network
calls.

Remember that base Entire session capture stores transcripts and metadata on the
repository's `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch — anyone with access to that branch
can read captured prompts, tool activity, and retained transcript data. Entire
redacts detected secrets before writing checkpoint metadata, but redaction is
best-effort and does not cover every local working artifact. Entire also writes
temporary shadow branches such as `entire/<short-hash>` whose code-file snapshots
are raw, unredacted blobs of the working tree; Entire does not push shadow
branches — do not push them manually, or unredacted source could reach the
remote. Review the Entire CLI security and privacy guide before enabling Entire
on sensitive or public repositories.

## Storage And Configuration

The parent Entire CLI supplies the plugin directories that make the brain durable:

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR` | Plugin config, including `brain.json`. |
| `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` | Durable brains under `repos/<repo-key>/`; workspaces under `workspaces/<name>/`. |
| `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` | Regenerable cursors under `repos/<repo-key>/` (for example watcher state). |
| `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` | Cache data. |
| `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT` | Current git checkout when invoked inside a repo. |

Repo keys are derived from the repository origin. For example,
`github.com/entireio/cli` becomes `gh/entireio/cli`.

### Environment toggles

Optional `ENTIRE_BRAIN_*` variables tune retrieval and diagnostics. All are
off/default unless set; none are required for normal use.

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBEDDER` | (unset → Model2Vec) | Set to `ollama` for the transformer embedder (EmbeddingGemma) on the vector arm. Falls back to Model2Vec with a stderr notice if a one-time startup probe finds the server returns no embedding. |
| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL` | `embeddinggemma` | Model requested from the embed server when `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBEDDER=ollama`. |
| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBED_URL` | `http://localhost:11434/api/embed` | Embed endpoint (Ollama, or qmd's node-llama-cpp server). Must accept `{"model","input"}` and return `{"embeddings":[[…]]}`. |
| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_FACTS_BM25` | (unset → token-overlap) | `1`/`true`/`yes`/`on` switches the facts lexical arm to FTS5 BM25. Experimental; measured at parity, kept for A/B'ing the lexical engine. |
| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS` / `ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY` | (unset) | Strict local-only mode; enforces locality for no-agent, dry-run, and loopback-Ollama paths. |
| `ENTIRE_BRAIN_MCP_DEBUG_LOG` | (unset) | Path the stdio MCP adapter appends frame-level debug lines to. Diagnostics only. |

## Development

Run without installing:

```sh
go run ./cmd/entire-brain --help
```

When running outside the Entire CLI, set the plugin directories explicitly or
allow the XDG fallbacks:

```sh
ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" \
ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" \
ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" \
ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" \
  go run ./cmd/entire-brain doctor
```

Usual mise tasks:

```sh
mise run fmt         # gofmt -s -w .
mise run lint        # go vet, gofmt check, go mod tidy check, shellcheck
mise run test        # go test ./...
mise run test:ci     # go test -race ./...
mise run test:phase1 # deterministic Phase 1 semantic suite
mise run build       # build ./entire-brain
mise run build-all   # cross-build common targets
mise run check       # lint, race tests, Phase 1 tests, and cross-builds
```

GitHub Actions runs generic tests and the deterministic Phase 1 semantic suite on
Linux, macOS, and Windows.

### Endpoint + middleware
`POST /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/artifacts`, registered via `teamOp` with `writeGate = [requireAuth, requireRepoPush]` (push = write gate, fail-closed authz-before-existence). `op.MaxBodyBytes = maxBrainArtifactBytes` (256 MiB const) set on THIS op only, before `huma.Register` — teamOp's 1 MiB default is untouched elsewhere. ### JSON body shape
```go
type BrainArtifact struct {
    Kind   string `json:"kind"`
    Ref    string `json:"ref"`
    Digest string `json:"digest,omitempty"`
    Data   []byte `json:"data"`   // base64 on the wire
}
// Body: { "artifacts": [ ... ] }   (json:"artifacts")
// Output Body: { "published": int } (json:"published")
```

### Slug resolution
`brainSlugResolver.Resolve` reverses the repo store (`GetRepoMeta` → `full_name` "owner/repo"), then renders `"gh/" + wireRepoPath(fullName)`. `wireRepoPath` normalizes EACH `/`-component via `safeRepoPathComponent`: lowercase → `regexp [^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+` → `-` → `strings.Trim("-._")`, byte-identical to entire-brain (`acme/.github` → `gh/acme/github`). Unknown repo / empty full_name / empty path → `""` → handler 404, nothing stored. The handler keys every `BrainKey` by the slug (never the ULID). Manifests additionally must have `ManifestRepoKey == slug` or 422.

### Handler taxonomy
Pass 1 (validate, store nothing): empty bundle / unknown kind / empty ref / duplicate `(kind,ref)` → 400; `VerifyDigest` + `ValidateManifest` + manifest repo_key check → 422. Pass 2 (store): fresh `NewValidatingStore(encStore{deps.Brain.enc})` per publish, `vs.Expect(key,digest)` armed immediately before each `Put` (Validating → Encrypting → object store); Put overwrites (idempotent). nil publisher → 503; storage/crypto fault → 500; gate → 401/403/404.
