## Build — `internal/brainbuild/`

### 1. Branch policy (policy.go) — "M1.6"
- Local input type `RefEvent{ RefOp, RefName string; IsDefaultBranch bool; OldTarget, NewTarget string }` (mirror entiredb refevents shape but define LOCALLY — no hard dep). `ActionKind` enum + `BuildAction{ Kind; Base, Head, Branch string }`.
- Pure `Decide(RefEvent) BuildAction` per ADR-P1-C: non-branch ref (tags/notes/PR/HEAD/checkpoint) → `Ignore`; feature-branch create/update/force_update → `PublishOverlay{Base:OldTarget, Head:NewTarget, Branch}` (empty base on a fresh create); feature-branch delete → `GCOverlays{Branch}`; default-branch create or force_update (history rewrite, no promotable lineage) → `UpdateBaseline{Commit:NewTarget}`; default-branch normal update (merge landing) → `PromoteOverlay{Base:OldTarget, Head:NewTarget}`; default-branch delete / unknown → `Ignore`. Document the merge-vs-direct-push inference (drawn from the ref op).

### 2. Worker (worker.go) — "M1.6"
- Seam interfaces: `RefEventSource` (Subscribe → channel; real NATS deferred), `BrainBuilder` (Build → a `Bundle`; real runner deferred), `Publisher`, `Promoter`, `OverlayGC`. `Bundle` carries the built artifacts + `Branch`.
- `Worker.Handle(ctx, RefEvent)` = `Decide` → dispatch to the right seam. `Run` drains the source channel; a seam error doesn't kill the loop; respects ctx cancel. NATS + runner seams stay interface-only (deferred infra) — document that clearly.

### 3. Store-facing seams (store_seams.go) — "M1.6c" (all keyed by SLUG; concurrency-hardened)
- `RepoSlugResolver` interface (`Resolve(ctx, repoID)(slug, err error)`). ALL seams resolve `repoID`(ULID)→slug ONCE at the top and key EVERY `BrainKey` by the slug (never the raw repoID) — matches the M1.5 endpoint's keying. Fail-closed: unresolvable/empty slug → error, nothing stored/shredded.
- `StorePublisher` over `*brainstore.EncryptingStore` (+ an object-store adapter if EncryptingStore isn't a full Store — mirror how the M1.5 endpoint composes Validating→Encrypting): `Publish(ctx, repoID, Bundle)` stores each artifact (validate over plaintext then seal) under its `BrainKey`. For a `KindOverlay` artifact, **record the branch→overlay-coordinate mapping** in the `OverlayBranchIndex` AND take the coordinate lock around Put+Record (see below). Idempotent.
- `StorePromoter.Promote(ctx, repoID, base, head)`: read the overlay at `KindOverlay@"base..head"`, re-store its content as `KindSnapshot@head` (the store has no explicit baseline pointer — a commit's baseline IS its snapshot). Missing overlay → `ErrNotFound`.
- `StoreOverlayGC.GC(ctx, repoID, branch)(retired int, err error)`: look up the branch's overlay refs from the index; for each ref, **hold the coordinate lock, then `RetireRef`, then best-effort tag** (see the lock + RetireRef design). Return the count retired.

### 4. OverlayBranchIndex (overlay_branch_index.go + _pg.go + migration 037) — atomic retirement, no over-reap
- Migration `037_brain_overlay_branches.sql`: `brain_overlay_branches(repo_key TEXT, branch TEXT, overlay_ref TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(), PRIMARY KEY(repo_key,branch,overlay_ref))` + index `(repo_key, overlay_ref)` (for the cross-branch refcount) — mirror migration conventions (search_path, GRANT ... TO repo_rw, goose up/down).
- Interface: `Record(ctx, repoKey, branch, overlayRef) error`; `Overlays(ctx, repoKey, branch)([]string, error)` (the branch's refs snapshot); `RetireRef(ctx, repoKey, branch, overlayRef)(shreddedVersion string, shredded bool, err error)`. Provide `MemOverlayBranchIndex` (mutex) + `PgOverlayBranchIndex` (pgxpool).
- **RetireRef is the load-bearing atomic op — do EXACTLY this (Pg):** ONE transaction: `DELETE` the `(repo_key,branch,overlay_ref)` row; `SELECT count(*) FROM brain_overlay_branches WHERE repo_key=$1 AND overlay_ref=$2` (siblings on OTHER branches); if the remaining count is 0, `DELETE FROM brain_deks WHERE repo_key=$1 AND kind='overlay' AND ref=$2 RETURNING ciphertext_version` (the crypto-shred — index-row delete and DEK delete COMMIT together, so a failure rolls both back → no de-index-without-shred). Return `(version, shredded, nil)`. **Refcount prevents over-reap**: a coordinate shared by two branches (same base..head) is only shredded by the LAST branch to retire it. Mem mirrors this atomically under one mutex (delete index row → count siblings → if 0 delete the DEK via the shared DEKStore → return). After RetireRef returns `shredded`, GC best-effort tags the versioned object `state=unshared` (outside the tx — S3-only, swallowed on error; DEK already gone = safe).

### 5. CoordinateLocker (coordinate_lock.go) — symmetric, no deadlock
- `CoordinateLocker` interface `WithLock(ctx, key string, fn func(ctx) error) error`. `MemCoordinateLocker` = refcounted keyed mutex. `PgCoordinateLocker` = holds `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(key,0))` in a short tx on a **DEDICATED pool** (a separate small pgxpool, e.g. 4 conns, created from the same DSN — so holding a lock connection NEVER starves the work pool). Provide `NewPgCoordinateLocker(ctx, workPool)(*PgCoordinateLocker, error)` + `Close()`; thread ownership through `NewStoreWorker`/`NewStoreSeams` (return an `io.Closer`) so the caller closes it — no dangling pool.
- **The invariant (state it in a comment + honor it):** NO party pins a WORK-pool connection while blocked waiting on the coordinate lock. BOTH `StorePublisher.Publish` (around Put+Record) and `StoreOverlayGC.GC` (around each RetireRef+tag) acquire the SAME advisory-lock key `BrainKey{slug, KindOverlay, ref}.String()` on the DEDICATED lock pool FIRST (holding no work conn), THEN do their work-pool work (RetireRef's tx, Publish's Put/Record). Because pg advisory locks are DATABASE-scoped by key (independent of pool), a Publish and a GC of the same coordinate mutually exclude even though they lock via different pools. Different coordinates never contend. This eliminates: the GC↔Publish cross-pool circular wait (no work conn held while awaiting the lock), the concurrent-publish-vs-GC data loss (they serialize), and Publisher-vs-Publisher work-pool starvation.

## Tests (`internal/brainbuild/`)

- worker: Handle dispatches each ActionKind to the right seam (fakes); Run loop survives a seam error + respects cancel.
- seams (Mem stack — EncryptingStore over a mem object store + MemDEKStore + snapshotcrypt local cipher + MemOverlayBranchIndex + MemCoordinateLocker + fake slug resolver): Publish stores + records overlay + keys by resolved slug (not ULID); Promote makes head baseline-resolvable; **over-reap regression** (two branches record the SAME overlay coord → GC(branchA) does NOT shred it while branchB still references it; GC(branchB) then shreds); **shred-fail leak regression** (inject a DEK-delete failure when remaining==0 → the index row survives for retry); a design test that the coordinate lock is held BEFORE any RetireRef work and Publisher/GC use the same key. content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

## D. Synthesis — natural M2 architecture

**(a) Sync granularity: whole facts-blob per branch is what the substrate gives for free; per-fact is what the merge model needs.** M1 stores facts as one opaque blob per `(repo, KindFacts, ref)` (B.6) with a client-chosen ref. But the local merge model (A.2, A.5) operates on individual content-addressed fact records. The reconciling tension: **sync/transport at blob granularity, but merge at record granularity.** The natural resolution — key each branch's facts blob by a stable ref (e.g. `facts/<branch>`), and have the merge worker unpack the blob into `factRecord`s (A.1 NDJSON is already the wire format), reconcile at the `fact:<hash>` id level (A.5), re-seal one merged blob, and advance the ref. The server stays blob-oblivious; a worker owns record-level semantics.

**(b) Merge model: reuse the LOCAL reconcile logic server-side, gated by CAS. Do NOT build a CRDT.** The keep-both / merge / supersede / low-confidence-review decision engine already exists and is battle-tested (`applyFactActions` `facts_merge.go:58-108`, `promoteFacts` `facts_admin.go:89-130`). Cross-member merge is structurally identical to cross-**branch** promote (A.3) — different source of facts, same conflict rule (active + shared-path + different-id) and same three strategies. **The recommendation: lift `promoteFacts`/`applyFactActions` into a member-merge that treats "member B's facts" like "branch B's facts", defaulting to keep-both + review-queue.** entiredb offers no causal-merge (C.11), so the merge intelligence must come from the brain layer, not the DB. CAS (C.8) provides the atomic conflict-detectable advance around it; last-writer-with-provenance is the fallback only for the low-value case, not the model.

**(c) Stable fact identity for cross-member dedup/supersede: ALREADY EXISTS and is sufficient.** `factRecordID` (A.5) is a normalized content hash, unsalted by machine/branch/session — the same fact authored on two members produces the same `fact:<hash>`. Cross-member dedup is a map lookup on this id; provenance union (already implemented in `upsertFact`/`unionFactAnchors`) merges the anchor sets. **No new identity primitive needed.** One caveat to design around: provenance anchors (`SessionID`, `CheckpointID`, `Transcript` path) are inherently local — cross-member merge must treat unmergeable anchors as opaque provenance to union, not to resolve.

**(d) Atomic conflict-detectable fact-set advance: `refstore.CheckAndSetReference` (C.8).** Model a branch's fact-set as a ref whose value is the git-OID/CID (C.12) of the sealed merged blob. A member's sync = CAS from old-blob-CID to new-blob-CID. Concurrent members racing the same branch → one wins, the loser gets `ErrReferenceHasChanged` and retries the merge against the new tip (read-merge-CAS loop). The RSL (C.9) optionally provides the signed, ordered, auditable log of who advanced the fact-set when; the outbox→NATS feed (C.10) is what wakes the sync worker. This is a clean mapping onto existing primitives.

**Missing primitives that M2 must build:**
1. **A fact-set ref convention + CID binding** — no `KindFacts`↔ref-CAS wiring exists today (M1 refs are opaque strings, C.8 CAS operates on git refs; the bridge between `brainstore` blobs and `refstore` CAS is absent). **Biggest unknown — needs a spike.**
2. **A server/worker-side record-level merge engine** — the brain's `applyFactActions`/`promoteFacts` live in the CLI package (`internal/cli`), not in a shared library; they must be extracted into a reusable package callable server-side or in a sync worker.
3. **Cross-member conflict resolution UX** — the local review queue (`proposals.ndjson`, A.4) is single-user; cross-member keep-both proposals need an owner/routing model.
4. No fact/merge-set CID content type (C.12) — minor, may reuse `CidTypeGitObject`.

**Natural sub-milestones (5):**
- **M2.1 — Fact-set identity & ref binding.** Define the branch fact-set ref convention, bind it to a content-addressed merged blob (CID, C.12), and wire `KindFacts` publish (B.7) to advance a ref via `CheckAndSetReference` (C.8). Spike-first (missing primitive #1).
- **M2.2 — Extract the merge engine.** Lift `applyFactActions`/`promoteFacts`/`upsertFact` (A.2, A.3) out of `internal/cli` into a shared, server-callable package operating on `factRecord` NDJSON. Pure refactor, no behavior change.
- **M2.3 — Sync worker.** Consume `repo_refs_v1` outbox events (C.10), fetch peer fact-blobs, run the read-merge-CAS loop (M2.1 + M2.2), retry on `ErrReferenceHasChanged`.
- **M2.4 — Cross-member conflict/review model.** Extend the keep-both review queue (A.4) to a multi-member owner/routing model; decide default strategy (keep-both) and confidence handling across members.
- **M2.5 — Signed audit + provenance.** Log fact-set advances through the RSL (C.9) for signed, ordered, verifiable cross-member history; ensure provenance anchors union correctly and local-only anchors stay opaque.

The substrate strongly favors **transport-at-blob / merge-at-record, reusing the brain's own promote/reconcile engine, gated by entiredb CAS, with identity already solved by the content-hash fact id.** The one genuine build-from-scratch risk is the blob↔ref-CAS binding (M2.1) — everything else is extraction or composition of existing, working primitives.</result>

## Substrate verdict (grounded — see substrate map)
| Layer | What exists | Verdict for M2 |
|---|---|---|
| Local fact record | `factRecord` NDJSON, per-branch file (`entire-brain/internal/cli/facts.go:85`) | wire format already = transport format |
| **Cross-machine identity** | `factRecordID` = `fact:<sha256(normText+paths)[:12]>`, **unsalted by machine/branch** (`facts.go:142`) | **cross-member dedup = map lookup. No new identity primitive.** |
| Merge engine | `applyFactActions` (keep-both<0.75 / merge / supersede), `promoteFacts` (prefer-target/-source/keep-both), review queue (`facts_merge.go:58`, `facts_admin.go:89`) | **cross-member merge ≈ cross-branch promote. Reuse, don't rebuild.** |
| M1 fact storage | whole facts.ndjson blob per `(repo, KindFacts, ref)`, client-chosen opaque ref (`brainstore/store.go:44`, `httpapi/brain.go`) | transport at blob; unpack→merge at record |
| CAS advance | `refstore.CheckAndSetReference(ctx,repoID,new,old)` → `ErrReferenceHasChanged` (`entiredb/refstore/store.go:40`) | **the atomic, conflict-detectable fact-set advance** |
| Signed log | `rsl.AppendReferenceEntries` (SSH-signed, ordered, single-writer) (`entiredb/rsl/append.go:18`) | signed audit of who advanced facts when |
| Change feed | `refevents.Outbox.Emit` → `repo_refs_v1.<repoID>` NATS (`entiredb/refevents/outbox.go:176`) | wakes the sync worker |
| CRDT / causal-merge | **ABSENT** (confirmed) | merge intelligence comes from the brain layer, NOT the DB — CAS is last-writer-wins gated by compare-and-swap |

## Core decisions (ADRs this milestone forces)
- **ADR-P1-E — merge-execution locus.** Where does record-level merge run? Options: (a) entire-api server imports the brain merge lib; (b) **runner runs the `entire brain` CLI** (mirrors M1.6's runner model). **Decision: (b).** entire-brain is cgo/SQLite-heavy; importing it into the API server is heavy coupling. M1.6 already stands up runners that run `entire brain refresh`. The sync/merge runs on a runner via a new CLI verb; entire-api stays thin (store + CAS + event feed only). This keeps the API server free of the brain's build deps and matches the established build-on-push arch.
- **ADR-P1-F — fact-set ref binding.** The M1 store keys facts by an opaque client-chosen `ref`. M2 binds a branch's fact-set to a **content-addressed ref** whose value is the CID of the sealed merged blob, advanced by `CheckAndSetReference`. The bridge between `brainstore` blobs and `refstore` CAS does not exist today → **M2.1 spike.**
- **ADR-P1-G — cross-member conflict default.** Default strategy = **keep-both + review-queue** (never silently drop a member's fact), with the content-hash id collapsing exact dups automatically and provenance unioned. -- +goose Up
-- brain_overlay_branches — the branch→overlay-coordinate index brainbuild's
-- on-push pipeline uses to retire exactly the overlays a deleted feature branch

-- A feature-branch publish Records one row per overlay it stored:

-- "base..head" (the same ref the ciphertext + its brain_deks row are keyed under).
-- A branch delete retires every row for that (repo_key, branch). Because two
-- branches can independently publish the SAME base..head coordinate, an overlay's
-- DEK (in brain_deks) is shredded only when the LAST branch referencing it
-- retires: RetireRef DELETEs this branch's row, counts the siblings still
-- referencing overlay_ref, and — iff none remain — DELETEs the brain_deks row in

-- +goose Up
-- brain_fact_refs — the moving per-branch HEAD of a repo's durable fact-set.
--
-- Unlike brain_overlay_branches (037), which is an append-only refcount over
-- IMMUTABLE overlay coordinates, a fact-set head MOVES: every cross-member merge
-- advances a branch from its old fact-blob ref to a new one. Multiple members can
-- race to advance the SAME (repo_key, branch), so the advance is a compare-and-swap
-- — the caller supplies the ref it merged against and the ref it produced, and the
-- swap lands only if current_ref still equals the expected old ref. A mismatch
-- means a concurrent member advanced first; the caller re-reads this head and
-- re-merges (the read-merge-CAS sync loop). One row per (repo_key, branch).
--
-- current_ref is content-addressed: facts-<sha256(canonical merged NDJSON)>, the
-- same logical ref the merged facts ciphertext + its brain_deks row (036) are keyed
-- under. It is stable across re-seals (a fresh DEK per seal changes the ciphertext,
-- not this plaintext-content ref) and changes iff the merged fact-set changes.
--
-- No DELETE grant: heads MOVE, they do not retire. Crypto-shredding a superseded
-- fact blob's DEK is brain_deks' job (036, already granted DELETE), driven by the
-- sync/GC path — not by this pointer table.
--
-- search_path is set here, not inherited: on an existing DB goose runs only this
-- migration, so 001_init's `SET search_path TO repo, public` never executes in this
-- session and a bare table name would resolve against the default path.
SET search_path TO repo, public;

CREATE TABLE brain_fact_refs (
    repo_key    TEXT NOT NULL,
    branch      TEXT NOT NULL,
    current_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    version     BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (repo_key, branch)
);

-- 001's schema default privileges grant repo_rw SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE; the CAS
-- advance is a create (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) or a conditional UPDATE,
-- so those defaults suffice. No DELETE is granted — this table's rows are never
-- deleted (a head only ever moves).

-- Debug-readable view matching the *_readable convention: a fact-set head is a
-- content ref + version, no secret material, so expose every column.
CREATE VIEW brain_fact_refs_readable AS
    SELECT repo_key, branch, current_ref, version, updated_at
    FROM brain_fact_refs;

-- +goose Down
SET search_path TO repo, public;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS brain_fact_refs_readable;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS brain_fact_refs;

# Audit loop: fix until genuinely clean

Loop review then fix then re-verify until the code is clean from BOTH a normal reviewer's view and an adversarial bug-hunter's view. Do not stop at the first clean read. Stop only after two consecutive full passes find nothing new and build/lint/tests are green.

## Scope
Default to the current branch's diff vs the base branch (main). If the user names a file, package, or PR, scope to that. State what you are auditing before you start.

## The loop

Run these every iteration:

### Pass A: normal review lens
Read it like a careful reviewer.
- Correctness: does it do what it claims? Off-by-one, inverted conditions, missing cases, wrong defaults.
- Error handling: unchecked errors, swallowed failures, missing early returns, ignored return values.
- Maintainability: dead code, duplication, unclear naming, leftover debug, TODOs left in.
- Consistency: matches the surrounding code's patterns and the repo's conventions.

### Pass B: bugbot / adversarial lens
Now try to break it.
- Edge cases: empty, nil, zero, negative, very large, unicode, whitespace, duplicate, out-of-order.
- Concurrency: races, unsynchronized shared state, goroutine/promise leaks, deadlock.
- Resources: unclosed files/conns/handles, unbounded growth, missing timeouts/contexts.
- Security: injection, path traversal, secrets in code or logs, auth/authz gaps, unsafe deserialization, SSRF.
- Bad assumptions: stale cache, partial failure, reordering, retries that double-apply.
- For each suspected bug, construct the concrete failing input before claiming it.

### Fix
Fix everything found. Keep diffs minimal and targeted. Add or adjust a test for each real bug so it cannot regress.

### Verify the committed state
Run the repo's build + lint + full test suite. Confirm green on the actually-committed/staged tree, not an unsaved buffer. A "reset --soft then commit" or a stash can silently leave the fix out of the commit, so diff `git show HEAD` if in doubt.

### Re-loop
Go back to Pass A on the fixed code. A fix can introduce a new bug. Keep going.

## Stop condition
Exit only when a full Pass A + Pass B finds nothing new TWICE in a row AND build/lint/tests pass. Then report: what was found, what was fixed, and the verified final state.

## Rules
- Never declare clean on a single pass. The subtle bugs surface after the obvious ones are gone.
- Default to skepticism. If you cannot fix something safely because it needs a design decision or a benchmark you cannot run, stop and surface it instead of guessing.
- Report honestly: separate "fixed and verified" from "found but could not verify."
- For a large surface, fan out: review independent areas in parallel, then verify each finding adversarially before trusting it.

## Invariant 1 — Server↔runner contract match: **VIOLABLE (integration gap + one real drift)**

**There is no real HTTP adapter implementing `factsync.Server`.** Grepping entire-brain, the only implementors of the `Server` interface (`sync.go:45-48`) are the test doubles `fakeServer` and `conflictOnceServer` (`sync_test.go:32,43,212,225`). Nothing calls `GET/POST …/brain/facts`, nothing decodes huma's `BrainFactsCurrentOutput`/`BrainFactsAdvanceOutput`, and nothing maps 409→`ErrConflict` or `unchanged:true`→`ErrNoChange`. So the contract "match" the milestone rests on is asserted by a hand-written fake, never validated against the real endpoint's JSON encoding. **Severity: HIGH** as an integration-completeness gap — the runner and API cannot actually talk yet, and the riskiest unwritten line is the `200 {unchanged:true}` → `ErrNoChange` mapping (`brain_facts.go:139-156`): if the future adapter returns `nil` there instead of `ErrNoChange`, `Sync`'s `case err == nil` reports `Published:true` for a no-op.

Where the fake *does* encode the contract, I checked it line-by-line against `FactSetStore` and the CAS semantics **match exactly**:
- `newRef==oldRef`→`ErrNoChange` is checked **first, before store/CAS** in both (`fact_sync.go:111-115` ↔ `sync_test.go:45-47`) ✓
- CREATE (`oldRef==""`): fake's `oldRef != cur` with `cur="" when !found` is equivalent to `MemFactRefIndex.Advance`'s "conflict if exists" and the Pg `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING` (`fact_ref_index.go:100-110`, `fact_ref_index_pg.go:79-85`) ✓
- UPDATE: fake's `oldRef != cur` ≡ Pg `UPDATE … WHERE current_ref=oldRef` / Mem `!exists || cur.ref!=oldRef` ✓
- `found=false`-on-empty consistent across `Current`, endpoint, fake, and the runner's `if found && len(plaintext)>0` guard (`sync.go:83`) ✓

**One concrete fake-vs-real drift (Severity: MED).** `FactSetStore.Advance` hard-rejects empty plaintext (`fact_sync.go:103-105`), and the endpoint rejects `len(data)==0` with 400 (`brain_facts.go:123-125`). `fakeServer.Advance` has **no such check** — it happily stores an empty blob. This is reachable: a member whose merged set is empty (no local facts, or all local facts non-active — `Promote` skips `Status!=active`, `admin.go:94`) syncing into an empty head produces `Promote([],[])==nil` → `WriteNDJSON` writes zero bytes → `Advance(oldRef="", emptyBytes)`. Against the real server that's a 400/500 hard error out of `Sync`; against the fake it "succeeds." The test suite cannot catch this because the fake masks it.

## Invariant 2 — full audited advance path (store→CAS→audit): **VIOLABLE (audit completeness, Severity: MED-HIGH)**

Store-then-CAS ordering is correct: blob is `enc.Put` before `refs.Advance` (`fact_sync.go:117-124`), so a lost CAS orphans a harmless content-addressed blob — **HOLDS**. Audit is CAS-then-audit and never records a non-committed advance (`Append` is called only after the conflict/error returns, `fact_sync.go:138`) — the "false entry" direction **HOLDS**.

**The "missed one it DID commit is a detectable gap" claim does NOT hold.** The CAS (`PgFactRefIndex.Advance`) and the audit `Append` run in **separate transactions** (`fact_advance_log_pg.go:50-88`). If the CAS commits (head moves to vN) and the append then fails/crashes, the error is surfaced to the caller (good) — but the audit row for vN is **permanently absent**, and on the runner's retry it re-reads head=vN, merges to no change, gets `ErrNoChange`, and never re-attempts an advance, so vN is never audited. Now the killer: **`Verify` does not detect the gap.** Both `MemFactAdvanceLog.Verify` (`fact_advance_log.go:135-144`) and `PgFactAdvanceLog.Verify` (`fact_advance_log_pg.go:118-133`) only check `prev_hash` linkage and `entry_hash` recompute — **neither checks version contiguity or count**. The chain `v1,v2,v3,v4,v6` links perfectly (v6's `prevHash` = v4's `entryHash`, since v5 was never written) and `Verify` returns `ok=true`. Migration 039 adds **no `UNIQUE(repo_key,branch,version)`** and no contiguity constraint (`039_brain_fact_advances.sql:29-42`). So the design comment "the version gap makes it independently detectable" (`fact_sync.go:135-137`) is an **overclaim**: the data (head.version=6 vs audit max/count=5) *could* be reconciled, but no shipped code does it, and the feature's own integrity check passes clean. Head durability is fine; the tamper-evident **audit** has a blind spot exactly at the partial failure it claims to cover.

## Invariant 3 — no-silent-drop across the runner chain: **HOLDS**

`SanitizeForEgress` allocates `out` at `len(records)` and copies every record (`egress.go:29-34`); `sanitizeAnchors` only zeroes `Transcript` and `Line` (`egress.go:44-46`). It touches no field feeding identity: `RecordID = sha256(NormalizeText(text) + "\x00" + join(sortedPaths))` (`identity.go:32-35`) — provenance-free. So sanitize cannot drop a fact or change a `RecordID`, and two members who learned the same fact still produce the same id → dedup via `Promote`/`Upsert` `IndexOf` (`admin.go:98`, `dedup.go:33`). Enforced and tested (`egress_test.go:51-53,68-77`). **HOLDS.**

## Invariant 4 — egress↔review interaction: **HOLDS**

- **`internal/cli/mcp.go:51` `newMCPCommand`** → **`mcp.go:62` `runMCP`**: the only MCP server. It is a **stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 loop** — reads framed messages from stdin, writes to stdout. Two framing modes: LSP-style `Content-Length` and NDJSON (`mcpFrameContentLength`/`mcpFrameJSONLine`, `mcp.go:27-30`; read at `readMCPMessage` `mcp.go:1090`, write at `writeMCPMessage` `mcp.go:1144`).
- Dispatch: **`mcp.go:199` `dispatchMCPMessage`** handles `initialize` / `tools/list` / `tools/call` (serverInfo name `"entire-brain"`, `mcp.go:207`). Panic-isolated per request (`handleMCPMessage`, `mcp.go:179`).
- **There is NO HTTP/SSE/streamable transport.** Transport is stdio-only, invoked as `entire-brain mcp` (registered via `.mcp.json` at repo root). This is the surface M3 must re-expose over a remote transport.

### A.2 — Tool surface (33 tools)
All defined in **`mcpToolDefinitions()` `mcp.go:235-433`**, dispatched in **`handleMCPToolCall` `mcp.go:436-765`**. Every tool returns text JSON (`mcp.go:764`). Grouped by backend (see A.3):

**Facts/history/docs retrieval (read the on-disk brain dir):**
- `brain_query` (hybrid RRF, `mcp.go:518` → `runRetrieve modeHybrid`), `brain_search` (lexical, `:523`), `brain_vsearch` (vector, `:528`), `brain_get`/`brain_multi_get` (fetch by prefixed id `fact:|history:|doc:|pattern:|theme:`, `:533`/`:545` → `runGet`), `brain_brief` (task packet, `:507`), `brain_status`/`brain_index_status` (`:462`).

**Semantic graph tools (read the SQLite semantic DB):**
- `brain_context` (`:556`), `brain_impact` (`:561`), `brain_changes`/`brain_detect_changes` (`:571`), `brain_code`/`brain_search_code` (`:573`), `brain_search_graph` (`:578`), `brain_query_graph` (`:589`), `brain_get_graph_schema`/`brain_get_architecture` (`:594`), `brain_get_code_snippet` (`:596`), `brain_trace_path` (`:607`), `brain_dead_code` (`:632`), `brain_tests` (`:645`), `brain_boundaries` (`:650`), `brain_ingest_traces` (`:634`, write).

**Regression/review (semantic DB + facts):** `brain_regressions` (`:666`), `brain_review` (`:676`), `brain_workspace_regressions/graph/review` (`:686-717`, multi-repo local).

**Pattern corpus:** `brain_patterns` (`:736`), `brain_patterns_status` (`:752`).

**Local admin/index (NOT servable remotely — mutate local disk / spawn indexer subprocess):** `brain_index_repository` (`:468`), `brain_list_projects` (`:498`), `brain_delete_project` (`:500`).

### A.3 — Query backend per tool (determines hosted-direct vs rebuild)
Two on-disk backends under the brain dir:
1. **Flat artifacts (ARE in the hosted store)** — `facts.ndjson` (`internal/cli/facts.go:23`, per-branch via `factsFileRelPath`), `manifest.json` (`export.go:27`), the history index/source and docs (written by `writeBrainHistoryIndexAndSourceLocked`, `export.go:326`), plus the overlay. `runGet` reads these directly from `brainDir` (`retrieve_cmd.go` `getUnifiedBatch(brainDir, branch, ids)`).
2. **Regenerable SQLite semantic DB + vector/FTS indexes (NOT in the hosted store)** — opened via the purego sqlite driver (`sqlite_driver_purego.go`, `semantic.go`, `doc_fts.go`, embeddings via `embed_vec_purego.go`). All `brain_*graph*/code/context/impact/trace/dead_code/boundaries/tests` tools hit this. Rebuilt locally via index/repair; **the hosted store never keeps it** (M1 publishes only 4 kinds — `snapshot, overlay, facts, manifest` — `publish.go:48-53`, matching `brainstore.Kind*`).

**Consequence:**
- Servable **hosted-direct** from M1/M2 blobs: `brain_get`/`brain_multi_get`, `brain_search` (facts token-overlap), `brain_status`/`brain_patterns_status` (manifest) — pure reads over facts/snapshot/manifest.
- Need the **regenerable SQLite** (server-side rebuild from snapshot+facts via repair, or defer): all semantic-graph tools, plus `brain_query`/`brain_vsearch` whose ranking uses the FTS/vector index.

### A.4 — Existing hosted/remote brain client in entire-brain
- **`internal/factsync/httpserver.go` `HTTPServer{BaseURL, Token, Client}`** is already a full hosted-brain HTTP client — it drives `GET/POST /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/brain/facts[/advance]` with a bearer token, in lockstep with entire-api's `brain_facts.go` (M2). `Current`/`Advance` decode base64 `[]byte`. **This is the exact client an MCP tool would reuse to pull the hosted fact-set.**
- **`internal/brainwire/version.go`**: remote `brain_schema_version` negotiation (rejects a remote newer than local) — a wire-contract seam already anticipating a hosted brain.
- **Egress gating**: `internal/cli/agent_policy.go:14` `brainNoEgressMode()` (`ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS`); `internal/factsync/egress.go`. A remote MCP consumer path must respect these.
- No hosted client exists for snapshot/semantic reads (only facts) — consistent with B.8.

---

## B. The REMOTE transport + hosting substrate (entire-api)

### B.5 — Does entire-api host MCP today? **No.**
Every `mcp`/`MCP` hit in entire-api is analytics (`internal/analysis/metrics.go` counting `mcpServersUsed` in checkpoints) — **not a transport**. There is no JSON-RPC/SSE/streamable-http/tools-call surface anywhere. **M3 must introduce the MCP transport from scratch** (the bigger lift).

### B.6 — HTTP router + how authed brain routes mount
- Stack: **chi mux + huma v2 via `humachi`** adapter. `newRouter` (`internal/httpapi/router.go:292`) builds a chi mux, wraps `apiMux := chi.NewMux()` with `humachi.New(apiMux, cfg)` (`:327-328`), mounts it at `APIBase` (`/api/v1`, `:329`).
- `NewActivityAPIRouter` (`router.go:340`) registers all services on the one huma API, including **`registerBrain(r.API, repoDeps)` `router.go:357`** and **`registerBrainFacts(r.API, repoDeps)` `router.go:358`**.
- Route helper: **`teamOp` `internal/httpapi/repos.go:23`** — `huma.Operation` with `apiPrefix + path`, security schemes, and a middleware slice.
- M2's facts endpoints: **`registerBrainFacts` `brain_facts.go:169`** — `GET /repos/{repo_id}/brain/facts` (readGate) and `POST /repos/{repo_id}/brain/facts/advance` (writeGate), both via `huma.Register(api, teamOp(...), handler)`.
- **An MCP transport can mount two ways**: (a) as a huma operation `POST /repos/{repo_id}/brain/mcp` for a JSON-RPC-over-HTTP / streamable-http endpoint carrying the same middleware gates; or (b) a raw chi route on `r.Mux` for SSE (bidirectional streaming outside huma's request/response shape). Both share the same mux.

### B.7 — Auth + per-repo/member scoping (fully reusable)
- **`requireAuth` `router.go:405`** → **`auth.Authenticator.Authenticate` `internal/auth/auth.go:63`** — bearer JWT (`bearerAuth` security scheme, `router.go:315`; jwks-based). Stashes `Identity` + raw bearer in ctx.

- **Slug scoping**: `RepoSlugResolver` (`brain.go:43`) resolves the `{repo_id}` ULID → wire slug; `FactSetStore` keys every blob/CAS under the resolved slug and fails closed with `ErrUnresolvedRepo` (`store_seams.go:42`).
- **A remote MCP call reuses this unchanged**: a member's runner/session bearer (same token `factsync.HTTPServer` already sends) + `requireAuth` + `requireRepoAccess` on `{repo_id}`. Read tools gate on pull; the repo scope is the natural per-repo boundary; the caller identity is the per-member boundary.

### B.8 — Existing hosted READ path to sit MCP tools on

---

No MCP transport exists in entire-api. The minimal, lowest-risk shape: a **JSON-RPC-over-HTTP MCP endpoint** — `POST /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/mcp` — registered via `teamOp` with `[requireAuth, requireRepoAccess]`, handling `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call`. # Plan: P1.M3 — Remote MCP transport for the hosted brain

## Context
P1.M1 (server brain store) + P1.M2 (durable-fact sync) are built + DB-tested on clones, unmerged. **P1.M3 exposes the hosted/shared brain over a REMOTE MCP transport** so a team member's agent can QUERY the shared brain remotely — the consume/serve side, feeding P2's "one MCP surface." (P1.M4 after = brain auth/tenancy.)

**Governing constraint (unchanged):** no new infrastructure; build in durable clones on branches; **no merge to prod (io/hq)** until approved.

## Substrate verdict (grounded — see M3 substrate map)
| Layer | Reality | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| entire-api MCP transport | **NONE exists** (only analytics counters) | M3 must ADD the transport |
| Local brain MCP surface | stdio JSON-RPC 2.0, 33 tools (`entire-brain/internal/cli/mcp.go:199`) | lift the JSON-RPC dispatch; drop stdio framing |
| Facts-backed tools | serve DIRECTLY from M2 `FactSetStore.Current` (decrypted NDJSON) | the M3 target surface |
| Semantic/graph tools | need the regenerable SQLite (hosted store does NOT keep it) | **defer** (server-side rebuild worker) |
| Router + auth | chi+huma; `requireAuth`+`requireRepoAccess`+slug resolver (`httpapi/router.go`, `authz.go`) | reuse wholesale |
| Remote brain client | only a facts-sync client (`factsync.HTTPServer`) | generalize into an MCP client |

## ADRs
- **ADR-P1-H — transport = JSON-RPC-over-HTTP, single authed POST endpoint** `POST /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/mcp` (not SSE/streamable). Minimal, fully DB-testable, proves the seam; the JSON-RPC dispatch (initialize/tools/list/tools/call) lifts near-verbatim from the local mcp.go with huma owning the HTTP frame. SSE only if a concrete streaming client demands it — deferred.
- **ADR-P1-I — remote tool surface = curated READ-ONLY facts subset**: `brain_search`, `brain_get`, `brain_multi_get`, `brain_status`. Semantic/graph/vector tools deferred (need SQLite rebuild). Mutating/local tools (`brain_index_repository`, `brain_delete_project`, `brain_ingest_traces`) NEVER remote.
- **ADR-P1-J — hosted reads + auth**: facts via M2 `FactSetStore.Current`; a minimal server-side facts query engine (parse NDJSON → token-overlap search + get-by-id) executes tools server-side. `requireAuth` (bearer JWT) + `requireRepoAccess` (SpiceDB pull) + slug resolver — no new auth primitive. The query engine reimplements a faithful-enough facts search in entire-api (it cannot import the cgo-heavy brain); exact ranking parity with the local brain is a later refinement.

## Sub-milestones (todos)
- [ ] **M3.1 — MCP transport seam + facts search** *(entire-api)*. `POST …/brain/mcp` JSON-RPC endpoint (initialize + tools/list + tools/call dispatch), `requireAuth`+`requireRepoAccess(pull)`; a minimal `brainquery` engine (Search over fact-set NDJSON) + the `brain_search` tool over `FactSetStore.Current`. DoD: an authed JSON-RPC `tools/call brain_search` returns ranked hosted facts; `initialize`/`tools/list` correct; unknown method → -32601, tool error → -32000; pull-gated (a non-member is 403). DB/handler-tested. `/audit` clean ×2.
- [ ] **M3.2 — remaining facts tools** *(entire-api)*. `brain_get`/`brain_multi_get` (fetch `fact:<id>` from the fact-set) + `brain_status` (fact counts/branches). DoD: each tool round-trips over the hosted fact-set; a missing id is a clean not-found, not a panic. `/audit` clean ×2.
- [ ] **M3.3 — remote brain MCP client** *(entire-brain)*. Generalize `factsync.HTTPServer` into a hosted-brain MCP client: `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call` over HTTP with bearer auth, `brainwire` schema-version negotiation, `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS` respected. DoD: the client drives the endpoint over a real HTTP round-trip (httptest) — list tools + call brain_search against the hosted fact-set and parse results. `/audit` clean ×2.

# P1.M3 Cross-Piece Integration Audit — Remote MCP Transport (hosted brain)

Seam read: entire-api `brain_mcp.go` + `brainquery/query.go` + `router.go`/`authz.go` (server) vs entire-brain `hostedbrain/client.go` + `brainwire/version.go` + `cli/agent_policy.go` (client). Branches as specified; nothing merged.

## Invariant 1 — Client↔server wire contract — **HOLDS**

Line-by-line, both directions match:

**Request (client→server).** Client sends `{jsonrpc:"2.0", id:1, method, params}` (client.go:97). Server `BrainMCPInput.Body` decodes `jsonrpc/id/method/params` with `id` kept as `json.RawMessage` and echoed verbatim (brain_mcp.go:46-54, :87). `id:1` (number) round-trips as raw `1`. Match.
- `tools/call` params: client sends `{name, arguments}` (client.go:184); server `mcpToolCallParams{Name, Arguments{Query,ID,IDs,Limit,Branch}}` (brain_mcp.go:178-187). Client arg keys — `query`/`branch`/`limit` (Search, client.go:207-213), `id`, `ids` — map exactly onto the server json tags `query`/`id`/`ids`/`limit`/`branch`. Match.

**Response (server→client).**
- `initialize`: server emits `result.serverInfo{name,version,brainSchemaVersion}` (brain_mcp.go:93-97); client decodes `result.serverInfo → ServerInfo{name,version,brainSchemaVersion}` (client.go:53-57,145-147). The negotiated key `brainSchemaVersion` is byte-identical on both sides. **HOLDS** (explicitly the field the task flagged).
- `tools/list`: server `result.tools[]{name,description,inputSchema}` (brain_mcp.go:134-175) vs client `Tool{name,description,inputSchema}` with `inputSchema` as `json.RawMessage` (client.go:60-64). Match.
- `tools/call`: server `result.content[]{type,text}` (mcpTextResult, brain_mcp.go:277-279) vs client `content[].text`, reads `content[0].Text` (client.go:188-200). Match.

**Search projection** (the one the task singled out): server `brainquery.Result{Fact Fact json:"fact"; Score int json:"score"}`, `Fact{id,paths,kind,text,status}` (query.go:29-41) vs client `SearchResult{Fact json:"fact"; Score json:"score"}`, `Fact{id,paths,kind,text,status}` (client.go:68-79). Field names, nesting, and types are identical. **HOLDS.**

## Invariant 2 — Schema negotiation — **HOLDS**, with a MED drift-process risk

Both constants are `"1.0"` today: `hostedBrainSchemaVersion` (brain_mcp.go:38) and `brainwire.BrainSchemaVersion` (version.go:20). Same major. Negotiation is correct in all three branches:
- Incompatible major → `CheckCompatibility` returns `ok=false, err` (version.go:49-54); client hard-fails on either `cerr != nil` or `!ok` (client.go:154-159). Rejects. ✔
- Newer minor → `ok=true, warn` (version.go:56-61); client returns `warn` and proceeds (client.go:160-162). ✔
- Server omits field → client only negotiates when `v != ""` (client.go:152); empty is accepted with no check (older-server tolerance). ✔ (Server always emits, so this is client robustness only.)

**Drift risk (MED, process not code):** the two `"1.0"` consts live in separate Go modules (`github.com/entirehq/entire-api` vs `github.com/ashtom/entire-brain`) with no shared source and no cross-repo CI assertion binding them. An *honest* major bump is caught at runtime (hard error — good). The residual hole is a *breaking change mislabeled as a minor bump* on the server: negotiation would accept it with only a warning and the tolerant reader would silently drop/misread fields. Not exploitable via the wire; it is a release-discipline gap. Recommend a contract test or shared constant.

## Invariant 3 — Egress gate completeness — **HOLDS**

Every network-reaching method funnels through `rpc()`, which is the single chokepoint that checks `noEgress()` first (client.go:93-96). `Initialize`/`ListTools`/`CallTool` all call `rpc()` (client.go:141,167,184); `Search` reaches the network only via `CallTool` (client.go:214). There is **no** method that constructs an `http.Request` outside `rpc()` — the only `http.NewRequestWithContext` in the file is inside `rpc` (client.go:106). Fail-closed on `ErrNoEgress` before any I/O.

**Fail-closed parity with the CLI:** client `toggleOn` false-set = `{"", "0","false","no","off","disable","disabled"}`, everything else → true (client.go:236-243). CLI `securityToggleEnabled` has the identical false-set and returns true for the canonical trues plus *any unrecognized value* (agent_policy.go:32-45). Outcomes are identical for every input — including the key case (an unrecognized/typo'd value → **on**). The only divergence is cosmetic: the CLI emits a dedup'd stderr warning; the client does not. Behavior matches. **HOLDS.**

## Invariant 3b — Auth/scope end-to-end — **HOLDS**

Endpoint is gated `requireAuth + requireRepoAccess` (brain_mcp.go:285), and `requireRepoAccess` = `permRepoRead` (pull) enforced on the `{repo_id}` **path param** (authz.go:44,66 — `hctx.Param("repo_id")`). The handler serves facts from that same path param: `brainMCP(...in.RepoID)` → `hostedFacts(ctx, deps, repoID, branch)` (brain_mcp.go:102,209,259-260). The client puts `repoID` in the URL path (client.go:105), so the repo it can reach is exactly the one the bearer is authorized to pull. `branch` is a tool argument (client.go:208-209) but only selects a fact-set head *within that already-authorized repo* (`deps.Facts.Current(ctx, repoID, branch)`, brain_mcp.go:260) — it cannot cross the repo boundary. Client cannot smuggle an unauthorized repo (path is authz'd) or escape the repo via branch. **HOLDS.**

## Invariant 4 — Error propagation — **HOLDS** (one LOW ergonomics note)

- **JSON-RPC errors (-32000/-32601)** ride a 200 body `{error:{code,message}}` (brain_mcp.go:103-109, :253). Client decodes `out.Error` and returns it as `*jsonrpcError` (client.go:123-132) — surfaces as a hard error, never a silent empty result. ✔
- **HTTP non-200 (401/403 from middleware, 503 nil-store at brain_mcp.go:84-85)** short-circuit *before* JSON-RPC decoding: `rpc` checks `resp.StatusCode != 200` first and returns `unexpected status <status>: <body>` (client.go:119-122). So a **huma error envelope** (`{title,status,detail}`) is never fed to the `{result,error}` decoder — it is captured as the status-line + raw body string. No mis-decode, no silent zero-value. ✔
- **found:false vs errored:** a miss is a *successful* result — `mcpTextResult({found:false,id})` (brain_mcp.go:228), delivered as a normal content/text block; a tool failure is a JSON-RPC error (brain_mcp.go:207,218,253). The client distinguishes them structurally: `CallTool` returns text for the former, a returned error for the latter. ✔

**LOW:** all non-200s collapse into one untyped `fmt.Errorf` string (client.go:121). The status *code* is embedded in the message (`resp.Status`), so 401 vs 403 vs 503 are textually distinguishable but not programmatically — a caller cannot `errors.Is`/switch on "auth denied" vs "brain not configured" without string matching. Fine for logging; awkward for retry logic.

## Invariant 5 — Result fidelity round-trip — **HOLDS**, with a LOW consumption gap

**Double-encode round-trips.** `brain_search` → `brainquery.Search` → `[]Result` → `json.Marshal` into the `text` field (brain_mcp.go:213,272-279) → client `CallTool` returns `text` → `Search` does `json.Unmarshal([]byte(text), &[]SearchResult)` (client.go:214-225). Field tags are identical (Invariant 1), so `Fact{id,paths,kind,text,status}` and `score` survive intact. Empty result: `Search` returns nil `[]Result` → marshals to `"null"` → client unmarshals `"null"` into nil slice, no error (client.go:218-225). Round-trips cleanly. **HOLDS.**

**Gap (LOW):** only `brain_search` has a typed client wrapper (`Search` → `[]SearchResult`). `brain_get` (`{found,fact}` / `{found:false,id}`), `brain_multi_get` (`{facts,missing}`), and `brain_status` (`{branch,active,superseded,retracted,total}`) — all produced by the server (brain_mcp.go:226-250) — have **no** typed decoder on the client. They are reachable only through the generic `CallTool`, which hands back the raw JSON text for the caller to unmarshal by hand. Not a correctness break (the transport carries them; the shapes are consistent), but the client side of M3 is asymmetric: three of four advertised tools have no first-class consumption path. Worth a follow-up so remote callers aren't hand-rolling `json.Unmarshal` against server-owned shapes (which reintroduces the exact drift Invariant 1 was designed to prevent).

---

# P1.M4 substrate map — Brain auth / tenancy (multi-tenant, SpiceDB-gated)

Repo: entire-api @ `m3-remote-mcp` (M1+M2+M3 present). SpiceDB schema lives in **entiredb**, not here.

## 1. The auth/authz stack the brain rides

- **AuthN** — `internal/auth/auth.go`: `Authenticator` (bearer-only JWT, audience-pinned to the cell's jurisdiction, `scope=openid`) → `Identity{AccountID, Handle, HomeJurisdiction, Provider, ProviderUserID}` (auth.go:29-35, 63-73). No cookie path.
- **AccessChecker** — `internal/auth/access.go:45-116`. `HasPermission(ctx, resourceType, resourceID, permission) (bool, error)` (access.go:102-116) → `reader.Can(...)`. Subject is **always** derived from the verified Identity (`access.go:90-92`), never from request input — no confused-deputy surface.
- **SpiceDB client** — `internal/authz/reader.go`: `Reader.Can` checks at minimize_latency, then re-checks fully-consistent on a deny (reader.go:64-73). `Reader.List` enumerates (reader.go:78-102).
- **The gate** — `internal/httpapi/authz.go:121-137` `checkRepoPermission` → `ac.HasPermission(ctx, "repo", repoID, permission)` (authz.go:122), authz-**before**-existence (deny → 403, Core error → 503, missing repo → 404, so a denied caller never learns the repo exists).

**Resource types HasPermission accepts today: only `"repo"` and `"project"`.** `toResourceType` (access.go:267-276) hard-rejects anything else (fail-closed) — even though the vendored `vocab.go:7-13` *defines* `OrgType`, `TeamType`, `PlatformType`. `toAction` (access.go:279-292) accepts pull/push/manage/view. **No `org`/`team`/`tenant`/`brain` resource type is reachable from entire-api's AccessChecker.** Brain rides `("repo", id, "pull"|"push")` exclusively.

## 2. Tenancy / org / workspace model

- **In entire-api's own store: none above the repo except `project`.** `Repo` struct has `OwningProjectID` (store.go:341, column `owning_project_id` store.go:538). No org/tenant/workspace table or column. `Jurisdiction` (us/eu) is **geographic region placement, not tenancy** (store.go, repo_aggregates.go:310).
- **The org/tenant hierarchy lives in the SpiceDB schema in entiredb** (`core/authz/schema.go`): `platform > org > team/project > repo`. `org` (schema.go:45): owner/admin/member relations. `project` has `relation owner_org: org` and `permission read = write + reader` cascading via `owner_org->view`. `repo` (schema.go:33) has `relation project: project`; **`permission pull = push + reader + project->read + platform->read_any_repo + public_viewer`**. So a repo's read permission *transitively* includes its project's org's viewers.
- **Brain is scoped per-REPO only.** Every artifact/fact key is prefixed by the resolved wire-slug (`brainstore.BrainKey.RepoKey = slug`; brain.go:195, fact_sync.go:90,125). No org-shared or workspace-shared brain scoping exists.

**Consequence:** the multi-tenant hierarchy already exists at the schema layer and is *transitively enforced* through repo pull/push. M4 does not need to invent org primitives to isolate per-repo. Org-*scoped* (cross-repo shared) brains would be genuinely new.

## 3. Multi-tenant isolation today — how X's brain can't return Y's data

Two independent, fail-closed layers, both keyed on the **same** `{repo_id}` path param:

- **(a) authz gate** — `checkRepoPermission` (authz.go:121-137): SpiceDB `HasPermission("repo", repo_id, pull|push)`. Registered by every brain route (see §5).
- **(b) slug-keyed store** — `RepoSlugResolver.Resolve(repo_id)` → wire slug (real impl `server/brain.go:34`, over the repo store reverse lookup). `FactSetStore` resolves the slug **once per op and fails closed with `ErrUnresolvedRepo`** (fact_sync.go:79-85); every blob/head row keyed by slug, never the ULID. Publish additionally binds the manifest: `repoKey != slug → 422` (brain.go:181-183) — a manifest naming another repo can't be stored under this slug.

Subject is the verified Identity, not request input (access.go:90-92) → no cross-tenant spoof. Slug is derived from the repo's own `full_name`; a slug collision across two ULIDs is the one theoretical cross-contamination vector and is **not** guarded by an explicit test.

**Isolation is fully ENFORCED but thinly TESTED.** Existing tests cover the *gate denial* (brain_mcp_test.go:236-239 no-access → 403; brain_facts_test.go:197-199 pull-only → 403 on advance) and the manifest/slug mismatch (brain_test.go:169). **There is no test proving "caller authorized for X, data keyed under X, cannot surface Y's facts/artifacts across store+facts+mcp."**

## 4. The SpiceDB double used in tests

`internal/httpapi/repos_authz_test.go`:
- `fakeAuthz` (repos_authz_test.go:26-104): in-memory permissionClient with per-repo `pull/push/manage/list` sets + project `view` set; answers CheckPermission + LookupResources; `fail` flag → all RPCs error (drives the 503 fail-closed path).
- `fakeReader` / `fakeReaderRW` (repos_authz_test.go:109-118): build a real `authz.Reader` over `fakeAuthz` with pullable/pushable id lists.

**It models per-repo pull/push lists. It CAN express DENY** — a repo absent from the pull set returns `NO_PERMISSION` → 403 (exactly what brain_mcp_test uses). **It CANNOT express org/tenant membership** — `CheckPermission` only branches on object types `"repo"` and `"project"` (repos_authz_test.go:41-55); no `org` case. The per-repo isolation invariant M4 needs is fully drivable now; org-level checks would require extending this double.

## 5. Per-member roles — is there a distinct brain permission?

**No brain-specific role. Brain access == repo pull (reads) / repo push (writes).** Gate choices:
- `registerBrain` (publish) → `requireRepoPush` (brain.go:219).
- `registerBrainFacts` → GET `requireRepoAccess` (pull), advance `requireRepoPush` (brain_facts.go:170,177).
- `registerBrainMCP` → `requireRepoAccess` (pull) (brain_mcp.go:285).

This is the **deliberate, documented** model — brain_mcp.go:26-28: *"the repo is the boundary, the caller identity the member boundary."* A distinct brain permission (brain-reader/writer/admin) would require a **schema change in entiredb** (out-of-repo, deploy-time) and buys nothing unless product wants brain-read decoupled from repo-read. Not warranted for M4 unless that decoupling is an explicit product goal.

## 6. Where the SpiceDB schema lives

**Out of entire-api.** entire-api only *vendors a read client*: `internal/authz/reader.go` + `vocab.go` carry the header *"Vendored from entiredb core/authz @ PR #2018 … re-sync on merge."* Local, non-vendored additions in `internal/authz/local.go` (`AccountSubject`, the `List` permission const).

The **actual schema** (definitions, relations, permissions) is `entiredb/core/authz/schema.go`: `account/platform/org/team/project/repo`. The full **org→project→repo tenancy cascade already exists** (org schema.go:45, project `owner_org`, repo `project` relation). **There is NO `brain` definition** (`grep brain` → none). Adding a `brain` object or an org-scoped brain relation is a **schema change in entiredb → deploy-time, not buildable/provable on the entire-api clone.**

---

## 7. Synthesis (the read that drives the M4 plan)

**(a) Formalize-vs-new-primitives.** For **per-repo brains** (what M1–M3 built), the context's read is **CORRECT**: M4 is "formalize + test the per-repo isolation invariant + reuse the existing SpiceDB gates." The isolation is already enforced by two independent fail-closed layers (authz gate + slug-keying), and the org→project→repo multi-tenant hierarchy already exists in the SpiceDB schema and is transitively enforced through `repo.pull`/`repo.push`. **No new primitive is required to isolate tenants per-repo.** New primitives (a `brain` SpiceDB object, an org-scoped/shared brain, a distinct brain permission) are only needed if the product decision is org-shared brains or brain-access decoupled from repo-access — and each is a **net-new entiredb schema change that is deploy-time and NOT provable on this clone.**

**(b) Clone-buildable/testable now vs deploy-time.**

Buildable + provable on the clone (no Postgres, no real SpiceDB — drive `fakeReader`/`fakeReaderRW` + a fake `RepoSlugResolver`):
- **Cross-repo authz-gate isolation matrix** across all three surfaces (publish / facts current+advance / mcp): member-of-X (pull set `{X}`) hitting Y → 403; token-less → 401; pull-but-not-push → 403 on writes. (Partially exists; not systematic.)
- **Slug-keyed store isolation**: two-repo fake resolver (X→slugX, Y→slugY) proving facts/artifacts written under X never surface under Y at the `FactSetStore.Current/Advance` + `brainstore` level, plus `ErrUnresolvedRepo` fail-closed, plus manifest repo_key binding (brain.go:181).
- **Subject-binding / confused-deputy** invariant (spoofed account in body/path ignored; subject always from Identity) and a **slug-collision defensive guard** (two ULIDs → distinct slugs).

Deploy-time / out-of-repo (cannot be proven on the clone):
- The real SpiceDB schema — any `brain` object or org-scoped relation (`entiredb/core/authz/schema.go`).
- Org provisioning and real org→repo grants.
- (Trivial 1-line entire-api change to let `toResourceType` accept `"org"` — meaningful only once you check org-level perms, which per-repo brains don't need.)

**(c) Natural sub-milestones (each with clone-provable DoD):**
- **M4.1 — Cross-repo gate isolation matrix.** Table test over publish/facts/mcp: non-member → 403, token-less → 401, pull-only → 403 on writes. *DoD: one test file, all three brain surfaces, green.* (Assembling + filling gaps.)

- **M4.3 — Subject-binding + slug-collision hardening.** Prove the SpiceDB subject is always the verified Identity (request can't override); defensive collision guard. *DoD: spoofed account ignored; distinct ULIDs → distinct slugs.*
- **M4.4 — Tenancy model doc + scope decision (ADR).** Document that brain tenancy == repo tenancy riding the org→project→repo SpiceDB cascade; decide explicitly whether org-scoped brains / a distinct brain permission are in scope. *DoD: ADR merged; if out-of-scope, M4 closes here.*
- **M4.5 (conditional, only if org-scoped brains are wanted).** New primitive: entiredb schema `brain` object or org-keyed brain store + entire-api plumbing (`toResourceType "org"`, an org-slug resolver). *Deploy-time; not fully provable on the clone.*

**(d) Honest flag: M4 is largely ALREADY-ENFORCED-BUT-UNTESTED.** The isolation invariant is enforced today by two independent, fail-closed layers. If the product intent is per-repo brains (what M1–M3 built), **M4 collapses to a comprehensive isolation test suite + subject-binding hardening + a tenancy ADR** — a legitimate but **light** milestone (M4.1–M4.4). # Plan: P1.M4 — Brain auth / tenancy (multi-tenant, SpiceDB-gated)

## Context
P1.M1–M3 built the hosted brain (store, fact-sync, remote MCP), all authz-gated on repo pull/push. **P1.M4 is the last P1 milestone**: the multi-tenant guarantee. Substrate verdict (grounded): isolation is **already ENFORCED** by two independent fail-closed layers, riding the `org→project→repo` SpiceDB cascade that already exists in entiredb — but it is **thinly TESTED**. New primitives (org-scoped brains, a distinct brain permission, a `brain` SpiceDB object) are **entiredb schema changes = deploy-time**, not provable on this clone.

**So M4 = formalize + comprehensively test the isolation invariant + a tenancy ADR.** A legitimate but light milestone. Governing constraint unchanged: clone-only, **no merge to prod (io/hq)**.

## The two enforced layers (what M4 proves)
1. **Authz gate** — `checkRepoPermission` (`httpapi/authz.go:121`): SpiceDB `HasPermission("repo", repo_id, pull|push)`, subject always the verified Identity (`auth/access.go:90`, no confused-deputy), authz-before-existence (deny→403 before 404). Every brain route registers it (`registerBrain`/`registerBrainFacts`/`registerBrainMCP`).
2. **Slug-keyed store** — `RepoSlugResolver.Resolve(repo_id)→slug`; `FactSetStore`/`brainstore` key EVERY blob/head/DEK row under the slug, fail-closed `ErrUnresolvedRepo` (`brainbuild/fact_sync.go:79`); publish binds the manifest `repoKey==slug` (`httpapi/brain.go:181`). # 4. Brain tenancy is repo tenancy

Status: Accepted

## Context

The hosted brain (P1: a server-side, encrypted, content-addressed store of a
repo's durable artifacts — snapshots, fact-sets, overlays, manifests — reachable
over three surfaces: the publish endpoint, the fact-set sync endpoints, and the
remote MCP transport) is multi-tenant: many repos, many members, one deployment.
The question this ADR settles is what the tenant boundary *is* and how isolation
is enforced, so every brain surface treats it the same way and new surfaces
inherit it without re-deciding.

Two boundaries are in play:

- The **tenant** boundary — one repo's brain must never surface another's.
- The **member** boundary — within a repo, who may read vs. write the brain.

## Decision

**The brain's tenant is the repo. Brain access *is* repo access.**

- A read of the brain (fact-set `current`, MCP `tools/call`) requires repo
  **pull**; a write (publish, fact-set `advance`) requires repo **push**. There
  is no brain-specific permission — a member who can pull the repo can read its
  brain, and a member who can push can write it.
- The tenant boundary is the `{repo_id}` path param, enforced by the same
  `requireAuth` + `requireRepoAccess`/`requireRepoPush` middleware every other
  repo-scoped endpoint uses, resolving to SpiceDB `HasPermission("repo", id,
  pull|push)`. The subject is always the verified JWT `Identity`, never request
  input, so there is no confused-deputy surface.
- Multi-tenant *isolation* rides the existing entiredb authorization cascade:
  `repo.pull = push + reader + project->read + platform->read_any_repo +
  public_viewer`. A repo's brain is therefore readable by exactly the principals
  who can already read the repo — including, transitively, the repo's project's
  org viewers. The org→project→repo hierarchy already exists in the SpiceDB
  schema; the brain does not re-implement tenancy, it inherits it.

Isolation is held by **two independent, fail-closed layers**, either of which is
sufficient:

1. **Authz gate.** Every brain route denies a caller without the required
   permission on `{repo_id}` (403 before any existence check, so a denied caller
   never learns the repo exists).
2. **Slug-keyed storage.** The store resolves each repo ULID to its wire slug and
   keys every blob, CAS head, and DEK under that slug, failing closed
   (`ErrUnresolvedRepo`) on an unresolvable repo. Even if the gate were bypassed,
   one tenant's request resolves to its own slug and cannot address another's
   data. The publish path additionally binds the manifest (`repo_key` must equal
   the resolved slug, else 422).

## Out of scope (deferred, deploy-time)

These are deliberately excluded from P1.M4 because each is a change to the
SpiceDB authorization schema, which lives in **entiredb** (entire-api only
vendors a read client), and cannot be built or proven on the entire-api clone
alone:

- **Org-scoped (cross-repo shared) brains** — a team's brain spanning several
  repos. This needs a new `brain` object or an org-keyed brain store plus a
  distinct resolver, and an entiredb schema relation. The per-repo model above
  is the P1 shape.
- **A distinct brain permission** (brain-reader / brain-writer / brain-admin
  decoupled from repo pull/push) — only warranted if the product decides brain
  access should diverge from repo access. Until then, repo-permission-as-brain-
  permission is simpler and adequate.

## Assumptions

- Repo wire-slugs are unique per tenant (derived from the GitHub `full_name`,
  which GitHub enforces unique). A slug collision across two repo ULIDs is the
  sole theoretical cross-contamination vector and is outside the store's control;
  it would be a data-integrity fault in the repo→slug mapping, not a brain bug.

## Consequences

- New brain surfaces gate on repo pull/push and key by resolved slug — no new
  tenancy decision per surface.
- The isolation invariant is testable entirely on the clone (SpiceDB double +
  fake slug resolver): a cross-tenant caller is 403 on every surface, an
  unauthenticated caller 401, read never confers write, and one tenant's facts
  never surface for another at the store or MCP level. Those tests are the
  enforcement record for this ADR.
- If org-shared brains or a distinct brain permission are later wanted, they are
  additive: a new resource type and resolver, gated the same way, without
  changing the per-repo model documented here.

**Verdict: P1 built + tested on clones, all 4 milestones complete, nothing merged to prod.** Whole-stack fresh-DB test: **203 tests green** (entire-api 81 core `-race` + 24 httpapi, migrations 001→039; entire-brain 60 `-race` + 38 cli golden).

## What each milestone did + how verified

**M1 — Server-side brain store** (`entire-api m1-rebuild`)
Encrypted, content-addressed, authz-gated store mirroring the session-share stack: `brainstore` (Put/Get/List, per-object DEK, crypto-shred) + `brainbuild` store seams + publish endpoint. Migrations 036/037. *Verified: versioned-object atomicity, fail-closed GC, atomic refcounted shred, symmetric coordinate lock — all DB-tested `-race`.*

**M2 — Durable-fact sync + conflict/merge** (`entire-api m2-fact-sync`, `entire-brain m2-factmerge`)
CAS fact-set head (`brain_fact_refs`/038) + `FactSetStore` (seal+store+CAS) + `brain_facts` endpoints + tamper-evident audit log (`brain_fact_advances`/039); runner-side read-merge-CAS loop over the extracted `factmerge` engine, cross-member routing/resolve, egress redaction. *Verified: two-member convergence + dup-collapse + provenance-union + retry against real Pg AND real factmerge; chain tamper/gap/fork detection; no local-path leak.*

**M3 — Remote MCP transport** (`entire-api m3-remote-mcp`, `entire-brain m3-remote-mcp`)
Authed JSON-RPC-over-HTTP MCP endpoint (`brain_mcp`) serving curated read tools (`brain_search`/`get`/`multi_get`/`status`) server-side over the M2 fact-set via `brainquery`; entire-brain `hostedbrain.Client` with schema negotiation + egress gate + typed wrappers. *Verified: client↔server contract byte-for-byte, convergence over real HTTP, schema-major reject, all error classes.*

**M4 — Brain auth/tenancy** (`entire-api m4-brain-auth`)
The multi-tenant guarantee — proven, not newly built (isolation was already enforced by two fail-closed layers). Systematic isolation matrix (4 surfaces × cross-tenant/no-token/read≠write), slug-keyed store isolation (facts + all publish artifact kinds), MCP end-to-end, ADR-0004. *Verified: cross-tenant→403, unauth→401, one tenant's data never surfaces for another at gate OR store level.*

## Architecture (the composed P1 stack)
```
entire-brain runner/agent                    entire-api (hosted, multi-tenant)
─────────────────────────                    ─────────────────────────────────
factmerge (merge core) ──┐                   authz gate (repo pull/push, SpiceDB)
factsync (read-merge-CAS)─┼─HTTP(bearer)──▶  brain_facts  → FactSetStore ─┐
hostedbrain (MCP client) ─┘                  brain_mcp    → brainquery ────┼─▶ EncryptingStore
                                             brain publish→ brainbuild ────┘   (slug-keyed, DEK, shred)

```
**Decisions:** no new infra (ride the session-share stack); merge on the runner not server (ADR-E); Postgres CAS not entiredb refstore (F); keep-both default (G); JSON-RPC not SSE (H); facts-only remote tools (I); brain tenancy = repo tenancy (K).

what is p1

**P1 = Phase 1 of the Semantic Reasoning Layer** — *"lift the brain from local-only to shared & synced across a team."*

## The whole arc (6 phases, P0→P5)
- **P0** — local brain GA (per-developer brain, works on your machine) ✅ shipped
- **P1** — **shared/hosted brain** ← this ✅ done-on-clone
- **P2** — unified MCP surface (one chokepoint every agent tool routes through)
- **P3** — coordinated agents
- **P4** — federation
- **P5** — behavioral intelligence (the Salesforce ask)

## What P1 is, concretely
P0's brain is **local** — each dev's machine holds its own durable facts, semantic index, history. Useful solo, but a team can't share what they've learned. **P1 makes the brain a hosted, team-shared, multi-tenant service.** Its 4 milestones are the layers of that:

| | What it makes possible |
|---|---|
| **M1** store | the brain's artifacts live on a server — encrypted, content-addressed, per-repo |
| **M2** fact-sync | teammates' durable facts **merge** into one shared set (conflict/merge, no silent overwrite) |
| **M3** remote MCP | your agent **queries** the shared brain over the wire (not just your local one) |
| **M4** auth/tenancy | one team's brain is **walled off** from another's (multi-tenant isolation) |

So after P1: instead of "my brain on my laptop," it's **"our team's brain, hosted, that every member's agent reads and writes, safely isolated per-tenant."**

**Governing rule the whole time:** no new infrastructure — P1 rides entire.io's existing rails (session-share stack, SpiceDB authz, Postgres), which is why M1–M4 were mostly *wiring proven components onto the brain*, not greenfield.

P1 is the differentiator — it's what turns the brain from a personal tool into shared team memory, and it's the foundation P2–P5 build on.

what is cost; i on't duenrstand this; is this going on cloud etc

Fair question. Let me clear it up plainly.

## Right now: **$0. Nothing is on the cloud.**
Everything I built is on **your laptop**:
- Code = local git branches (not pushed anywhere).
- The tests = a **throwaway Postgres in Docker** on your machine that I spin up and delete each run.
- No servers, no cloud storage, no prod, no data hosted anywhere.

So far this has cost **nothing** in infrastructure. It's just code + local tests.

## "Is this going on cloud?" — yes, *when you deploy it*, that's the whole point of P1
P1 = **hosted brain**. "Hosted" literally means "runs on servers in the cloud instead of on each person's laptop." So once you ship it to prod, it uses cloud resources. That's by design — a shared team brain has to live somewhere central.

## But the cost is **small** — because the design rule was "no new infrastructure"
P1 **rides entire.io's existing cloud** — the same servers/storage/database/key-service that session-sharing already uses and already pays for. It's not a new system to stand up. When live, the extra cost is just *more data + more requests on infra that's already running*:

| Resource | What it's for | Cost shape |
|---|---|---|
| **S3** (object storage) | the encrypted brain blobs (facts, snapshots) | pennies per GB/month — brains are small (text) |
| **Postgres** | brain tables (keys, fact pointers, audit log) | already your existing DB — marginal |
| **KMS** (key service) | encryption keys | fractions of a cent per operation |
| **Runners** (compute) | distill + sync jobs on code push | pay per job, only when someone pushes |
| **API server** | the brain endpoints | already deployed — adds a little load |

No new cluster, no new database, no new service = **no big new line item.** It scales with usage (more repos/members/facts = a bit more), not a fixed upfront cost.

## The short version for your boss
> "P1 costs nothing today — it's all local. When we ship it, it runs on our **existing** cloud (same S3/Postgres/KMS/runners as session-share), so the added cost is small and usage-based — mostly cheap object storage for the encrypted brains. No new infrastructure to buy or run."

If you want, I can put a rough **$/month estimate** in the review artifact (based on # of repos × brain size × request volume) so your boss sees an actual number — but the honest headline is: **marginal, because it reuses what's already paid for.**
